genesis-8.summary: God remembers Noah and the animals and sends a wind. The water goes down, and the ship rests on the mountains of Ararat. Noah sends out a raven and then a dove. The dove comes back with an olive leaf, then does not return. God tells Noah to leave the ship with his family and the animals. Noah builds an altar and offers burnt offerings. The LORD says he will not again curse the ground or strike every living thing. Seedtime and harvest, summer and winter, day and night will not stop.

verse.text: While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.”

genesis-8.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-10.summary: This is the family record of Noah’s sons after the flood. Japheth’s line spreads to the coasts and islands. Ham’s line includes Cush, Mizraim, and Canaan. Cush’s son Nimrod is a mighty hunter, and his kingdom begins at Babel. Canaan’s families spread from Sidon toward Gaza. Shem’s line includes Eber, Peleg, and Joktan. Each list ends with families, languages, lands, and nations. From these families the nations spread over the earth.

verse.text: These are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations, according to their nations. The nations divided from these on the earth after the flood.

genesis-10.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.
genesis-10.placeNote: Babel is shown at Babylon, the traditional site.

genesis-11.summary: All people speak one language and settle on a plain in Shinar. They bake bricks and plan a city with a tower to the sky. They want a name for themselves and fear being scattered. The LORD comes down to see, confuses their language, and scatters them. The city is called Babel. Then the record runs from Shem to Terah. Terah fathers Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Abram’s wife Sarai has no child. Terah leaves Ur for Canaan but settles in Haran and dies there.

verse.text: They said, “Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole earth.”

genesis-11.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.
genesis-11.placeNote: Babel is shown at Babylon, the traditional site.

genesis-12.summary: The LORD tells Abram to leave his country and his father’s house. He promises a great nation and a blessing for all families through Abram. Abram goes at age seventy-five with Sarai and Lot. In Canaan the LORD promises the land to his offspring, and Abram builds altars. A famine sends him to Egypt. He asks Sarai to say she is his sister, because he fears being killed. Pharaoh takes her and pays Abram well, and the LORD sends plagues. Pharaoh rebukes Abram and sends them away.

verse.text: I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who treats you with contempt. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”

genesis-12.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-13.summary: Abram returns from Egypt to Bethel, rich in livestock, silver, and gold. Lot also has flocks, and the land cannot hold both. Their herdsmen quarrel. Abram asks for no strife and offers Lot his choice of land. Lot sees the well-watered Jordan plain and chooses it. He camps near Sodom, whose men are very wicked. The LORD tells Abram to look all around, for the land will be his. Abram moves to the oaks of Mamre at Hebron and builds an altar.

verse.text: Isn’t the whole land before you? Please separate yourself from me. If you go to the left hand, then I will go to the right. Or if you go to the right hand, then I will go to the left.”

genesis-13.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-14.summary: Four kings make war on five kings near the Salt Sea. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah flee, and the winners take goods, food, and people. They take Lot, who lives in Sodom. Abram leads 318 trained men, attacks by night, and brings everyone back. Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings bread and wine. He blesses Abram, and Abram gives him a tenth. The king of Sodom offers Abram the goods. Abram refuses even a thread, so the king cannot say he made Abram rich.

verse.text: that I will not take a thread nor a sandal strap nor anything that is yours, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich.’

genesis-14.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-15.summary: The LORD comes to Abram in a vision and says not to fear. Abram says he has no child, and a servant will be his heir. The LORD says his own son will be his heir and shows him the stars. Abram believes, and the LORD counts it as righteousness. Abram asks how he will know the land is his. He cuts animals in half, and a deep sleep and darkness fall on him. The LORD says his offspring will serve in a foreign land four hundred years. A furnace and a torch pass between the pieces, and the LORD makes a covenant.

verse.text: He said to Abram, “Know for sure that your offspring will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them. They will afflict them four hundred years.

genesis-15.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-16.summary: Sarai has no children and gives her Egyptian servant Hagar to Abram as a wife. Hagar conceives and looks down on Sarai. Sarai blames Abram, and he says Hagar is in her hand. Sarai treats her harshly, and Hagar runs away. The LORD’s angel finds her by a spring and tells her to return. He promises her many offspring and a son named Ishmael, because the LORD heard. Hagar names the LORD “a God who sees.” She bears Ishmael when Abram is eighty-six.

verse.text: The LORD’s angel said to her, “Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hands.”

genesis-16.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-17.summary: Abram is ninety-nine when the LORD appears as God Almighty. God makes a covenant: many nations will come from Abram, and Canaan will be theirs. God changes his name to Abraham. Every male in his house, even bought servants, must be circumcised as the sign. Sarai’s name becomes Sarah, and she will bear a son. Abraham laughs and asks that Ishmael might live before God. God says Sarah will bear Isaac, and Ishmael will also become a great nation. Abraham circumcises every male in his house that same day.

verse.text: Abraham took Ishmael his son, all who were born in his house, and all who were bought with his money: every male among the men of Abraham’s house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the same day, as God had said to him.

genesis-17.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-18.summary: The LORD appears to Abraham at Mamre as three men stand near his tent. Abraham runs to meet them and serves bread, a calf, butter, and milk. One says Sarah will have a son next year. Sarah laughs to herself, and the LORD asks if anything is too hard for him. The men look toward Sodom. The LORD tells Abraham that the outcry against Sodom is great. Abraham asks if God will kill the righteous with the wicked. He bargains from fifty down, and the LORD will spare the city for ten.

verse.text: May it be far from you to do things like that, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be like the wicked. May that be far from you. Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?”

genesis-18.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-19.summary: Two angels come to Sodom, and Lot urges them to stay in his house. The men of the city surround it and demand the guests. Lot offers his two daughters, and the crowd turns on him. The angels pull Lot in and strike the men blind. They warn that the LORD will destroy the city, but Lot’s sons-in-law think he jokes. At dawn the angels drag Lot, his wife, and his daughters out. Fire and sulfur fall, and Lot’s wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. In a cave, Lot’s daughters make him drunk and bear Moab and Ben Ammi.

verse.text: See now, I have two virgin daughters. Please let me bring them out to you, and you may do to them what seems good to you. Only don’t do anything to these men, because they have come under the shadow of my roof.”

genesis-19.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-20.summary: Abraham moves to Gerar and again says Sarah is his sister. King Abimelech takes her. God warns Abimelech in a dream that she is a man’s wife. Abimelech says he acted with a clean heart, and God agrees. In the morning he asks Abraham why he did this. Abraham says he thought no one there feared God. He adds that Sarah is his half sister. Abimelech gives animals, servants, and silver, and Abraham prays for his house.

verse.text: Abraham said, “Because I thought, ‘Surely the fear of God is not in this place. They will kill me for my wife’s sake.’

genesis-20.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-21.summary: The LORD does as he said, and Sarah bears Isaac when Abraham is one hundred. Sarah says God has made her laugh. At Isaac’s weaning feast, Sarah sees Hagar’s son mocking. She tells Abraham to send Hagar and the boy away. Abraham is grieved, but God says to listen and promises a nation from the boy. In the wilderness the water runs out, and Hagar weeps. God hears the boy, and Hagar sees a well. Abraham and Abimelech then swear an oath over a well at Beersheba.

verse.text: God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went, filled the container with water, and gave the boy a drink.

genesis-21.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-22.summary: God tests Abraham and tells him to offer his son Isaac in Moriah. Abraham rises early and travels three days with Isaac and two servants. Isaac carries the wood and asks where the lamb is. Abraham says God will provide the lamb. He builds the altar, binds Isaac, and takes the knife. The LORD’s angel stops him and says he now knows Abraham fears God. Abraham offers a ram caught in a thicket. The LORD swears to bless him and all nations through his offspring.

verse.text: Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.

genesis-22.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-23.summary: Sarah dies at Hebron at age 127, and Abraham mourns her. He tells the Hittites he is a foreigner and asks for a burial place. They offer him the best of their tombs. Abraham asks to buy the cave of Machpelah from Ephron at full price. Ephron offers the field as a gift, then names its worth: four hundred shekels. Abraham weighs out the silver before the people at the city gate. The field, cave, and trees are deeded to him. He buries Sarah there.

verse.text: to Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all who went in at the gate of his city.

genesis-23.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-24.summary: Old Abraham makes his servant swear to find Isaac a wife among his relatives. The servant takes ten camels to the city of Nahor. At the well he prays for a woman who also waters his camels. Rebekah comes and does just that. He gives her gold and learns she is Bethuel’s daughter, of Abraham’s family. He tells her brother Laban the whole story, and the family agrees. They ask Rebekah, and she says, “I will go.” Isaac meets her, marries her, and loves her.

verse.text: They called Rebekah, and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” She said, “I will go.”

genesis-24.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-25.summary: Abraham marries Keturah and has more sons, but he gives all he has to Isaac. He dies at 175, and Isaac and Ishmael bury him beside Sarah. Ishmael’s twelve sons are listed. Isaac prays for Rebekah, who has no child, and she conceives twins. The LORD tells her the elder will serve the younger. Esau is born first, red and hairy, and Jacob follows holding his heel. Esau comes in from the field starving and asks for Jacob’s stew. Jacob asks for the birthright, and Esau swears it away.

verse.text: Esau said, “Behold, I am about to die. What good is the birthright to me?”

genesis-25.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-26.summary: In a famine the LORD tells Isaac to stay and not go to Egypt. He repeats to Isaac the oath he swore to Abraham. In Gerar Isaac says Rebekah is his sister, and Abimelech finds out and rebukes him. Isaac’s crops yield a hundredfold, and the Philistines envy him. They fill his father’s wells with earth and send him away. Isaac’s men dig wells, and the herdsmen of Gerar claim two of them. He moves again, digs a third, and names it Rehoboth for the room they found. Abimelech then comes to make a peace oath at Beersheba.

verse.text: He left that place, and dug another well. They didn’t argue over that one. So he called it Rehoboth. He said, “For now the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”

genesis-26.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-27.summary: Isaac is old and blind and sends Esau to hunt game before he blesses him. Rebekah hears and tells Jacob to bring two goats. She dresses Jacob in Esau’s clothes and covers his hands with goat skins. Jacob tells his father he is Esau. Isaac doubts the voice, feels the hands, and blesses him as lord over his brothers. Esau returns, and Isaac trembles. Esau weeps and begs for a blessing, and plans to kill Jacob. Rebekah tells Jacob to flee to her brother Laban in Haran.

verse.text: Isaac answered Esau, “Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given to him for servants. I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What then will I do for you, my son?”

genesis-27.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-28.summary: Isaac blesses Jacob and sends him to Paddan Aram to marry a daughter of Laban. Esau sees this and marries a daughter of Ishmael. On the way Jacob sleeps with a stone under his head. He dreams of a stairway to heaven with angels going up and down. The LORD promises him the land, many offspring, and his presence everywhere. Jacob wakes and says the LORD is in this place. He sets up the stone, pours oil on it, and names the place Bethel. He vows a tenth to God if God brings him home in peace.

verse.text: Jacob awakened out of his sleep, and he said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I didn’t know it.”

genesis-28.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-29.summary: Jacob reaches a well near Haran and meets Rachel, Laban’s daughter. He rolls the stone away, waters her sheep, and weeps. Laban welcomes him as family. Jacob loves Rachel and works seven years for her. At the wedding feast Laban brings him Leah in the evening. Jacob protests, and Laban says the younger is not given before the firstborn. Jacob marries Rachel a week later and works seven more years. The LORD sees that Leah is unloved, and she bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah.

verse.text: In the morning, behold, it was Leah! He said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? Didn’t I serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?”

genesis-29.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-30.summary: Rachel has no children and envies Leah. She gives her servant Bilhah to Jacob, and Bilhah bears Dan and Naphtali. Leah gives her servant Zilpah, who bears Gad and Asher. Rachel trades a night with Jacob for Leah’s mandrake plants. Leah bears Issachar, Zebulun, and a daughter, Dinah. God remembers Rachel, and she bears Joseph. Jacob asks to go home, and Laban asks him to stay for wages. Jacob takes the spotted and dark animals as pay, and his flocks grow large.

verse.text: Leah said to her, “Is it a small matter that you have taken away my husband? Would you take away my son’s mandrakes, also?” Rachel said, “Therefore he will lie with you tonight for your son’s mandrakes.”

genesis-30.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-31.summary: Laban’s sons say Jacob took their father’s wealth, and Laban’s face turns cold. The LORD tells Jacob to return home. Jacob tells Rachel and Leah that Laban changed his wages ten times. They agree to go, saying their father sold them. Jacob leaves in secret, and Rachel steals her father’s household idols. Laban chases them, but God warns him in a dream. He searches the tents and finds nothing, and Jacob lists twenty years of hard service. The two men pile stones as a border and swear to do no harm.

verse.text: Aren’t we considered as foreigners by him? For he has sold us, and has also used up our money.

genesis-31.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-32.summary: Angels meet Jacob on his way. He sends word to Esau, and hears that Esau is coming with four hundred men. Jacob is afraid and splits his camp in two. He prays, saying he is not worthy, and asks God to save him from Esau. He sends herds ahead as a gift, with space between them. That night he sends his family across the Jabbok and is left alone. A man wrestles with him until dawn and strains his hip. The man names him Israel, and Jacob limps away from Peniel.

verse.text: Please deliver me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau; for I fear him, lest he come and strike me and the mothers with the children.

genesis-32.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-33.summary: Jacob sees Esau coming with four hundred men. He lines up the women and children and goes ahead, bowing seven times. Esau runs to him, hugs him, and they weep. Esau asks about the family and about the herds he met. Esau says he has enough, but Jacob urges him to take the gift. Esau offers to travel together, but Jacob says his children and flocks are slow. Esau returns to Seir. Jacob goes to Succoth and then Shechem, buys land, and builds an altar.

verse.text: Jacob said, “Please, no, if I have now found favor in your sight, then receive my present at my hand, because I have seen your face, as one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me.

genesis-33.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-34.summary: Dinah, Leah’s daughter, goes out to visit the women of the land. Shechem, the prince’s son, takes her, lies with her, and shames her. He then wants to marry her, and his father Hamor asks Jacob. Jacob’s sons answer with deceit: every male in the city must be circumcised. On the third day Simeon and Levi kill all the males and take Dinah back. The brothers plunder the city and take the women and children. Jacob says they have put the family in danger. They ask if their sister should be treated like a prostitute.

verse.text: They said, “Should he deal with our sister as with a prostitute?”

genesis-34.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-35.summary: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel and build an altar. Jacob tells his household to put away foreign gods and make themselves clean. They hand over the gods and earrings, and he buries them under an oak. At Bethel God blesses him, repeats the name Israel, and promises the land. Rebekah’s nurse Deborah dies there. On the road Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin and is buried near Bethlehem. Reuben lies with Bilhah, his father’s concubine. Jacob reaches Isaac at Hebron, and Esau and Jacob bury their father.

verse.text: Then Jacob said to his household, and to all who were with him, “Put away the foreign gods that are among you, purify yourselves, and change your garments.

genesis-35.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-36.summary: This is the family record of Esau, who is also called Edom. Esau’s wives bear him five sons in Canaan. He moves to Seir, because the land cannot hold both brothers’ herds. His sons and grandsons become chiefs of Edom. The Horites, who lived in Seir, are listed with their chiefs. Eight kings rule Edom before Israel has any king. No king in the list is the son of the king before him. The list ends with Esau as the father of the Edomites.

verse.text: These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Israel.

genesis-36.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-37.summary: Israel loves seventeen-year-old Joseph most and gives him a tunic of many colors. His brothers hate him more when he dreams that they bow to him. Jacob sends Joseph to check on his brothers near Shechem. They plan to kill him, but Reuben persuades them to throw him in a pit. Judah proposes selling him, and he is sold for twenty pieces of silver. The brothers dip his tunic in goat’s blood and show it to their father. Jacob decides an animal killed Joseph and refuses comfort. In Egypt Joseph is sold to Potiphar, Pharaoh’s captain of the guard.

verse.text: They took the tunic of many colors, and they brought it to their father, and said, “We have found this. Examine it, now, and see if it is your son’s tunic or not.”

genesis-37.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-38.summary: Judah marries a Canaanite woman and has three sons: Er, Onan, and Shelah. Er marries Tamar and dies. Onan refuses to give his brother an heir and also dies. Judah sends Tamar home and keeps Shelah from her. Later Tamar veils herself by the road, and Judah takes her for a prostitute. He leaves his signet, cord, and staff as a pledge, and she conceives. When Judah hears she is pregnant, he orders her burned. She sends him the pledge, and he says she is more righteous than he.

verse.text: Judah acknowledged them, and said, “She is more righteous than I, because I didn’t give her to Shelah, my son.” He knew her again no more.

routes.title: Judah goes to Adullam and Timnah

genesis-38.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-39.summary: Potiphar, an Egyptian officer, buys Joseph. The LORD is with Joseph, and Potiphar puts him over his whole house. Potiphar’s wife asks Joseph to lie with her, and he refuses. He says it would wrong his master and be a sin against God. One day she grabs his garment, and he runs out and leaves it. She tells the household and her husband that the Hebrew servant came at her. Potiphar puts Joseph in the king’s prison. The LORD is with him there, and the keeper puts him over the prisoners.

verse.text: She spoke to him according to these words, saying, “The Hebrew servant, whom you have brought to us, came in to me to mock me,

genesis-39.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-40.summary: Pharaoh’s chief cup bearer and chief baker are jailed where Joseph is held. Joseph looks after them. Each has a dream on the same night, and Joseph sees they are sad. He says interpretations belong to God and asks to hear the dreams. He tells the cup bearer he will get his post back in three days. He asks the cup bearer to remember him and speak to Pharaoh. He tells the baker he will be hanged in three days. Both things happen on Pharaoh’s birthday, and the cup bearer forgets Joseph.

verse.text: But remember me when it is well with you. Please show kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.

genesis-40.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-41.summary: Two years later Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows eaten by seven thin ones. He also dreams of seven good heads of grain swallowed by seven thin ones. No wise man can explain it, and the cup bearer remembers Joseph. Joseph says the answer is not in him but comes from God. The dreams mean seven years of plenty and then seven of famine. He advises storing a fifth of each harvest under a wise man. Pharaoh sets Joseph over all Egypt and gives him his ring and a wife. Joseph stores grain, has two sons, and sells grain when the famine comes.

verse.text: The food will be to supply the land against the seven years of famine, which will be in the land of Egypt; so that the land will not perish through the famine.”

genesis-41.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-42.summary: Jacob sends ten sons to Egypt for grain but keeps Benjamin home. They bow before Joseph, the governor, and do not know him. Joseph knows them, remembers his dreams, and calls them spies. He holds them three days, then keeps Simeon and demands Benjamin. The brothers say to each other that they are guilty about Joseph. Joseph understands them and turns away to weep. He fills their sacks and puts their money back in them. Back home, Jacob refuses to let Benjamin go.

verse.text: They said to one another, “We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn’t listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”

routes.title: Ten brothers go down to Egypt

genesis-42.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-43.summary: The grain runs out, and Jacob tells his sons to buy more. Judah says they cannot go without Benjamin. He offers himself as a pledge for the boy’s return. Israel agrees and sends gifts and double money. In Egypt, Joseph has the brothers brought to his house, and they fear a trap. The steward calms them and brings Simeon out. Joseph sees Benjamin, leaves the room, and weeps. The brothers are seated by age, and Benjamin gets five times as much food.

verse.text: I’ll be collateral for him. From my hand will you require him. If I don’t bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever;

genesis-43.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-44.summary: Joseph has his silver cup hidden in Benjamin’s sack. His steward overtakes the brothers and finds it there. They tear their clothes and all return to the city. Judah says God has found out their guilt, and all will be slaves. Joseph says only the one with the cup will stay. Judah steps close and tells of their old father and his love for the boy. He says the father will die if Benjamin does not return. He asks to stay as a slave in the boy’s place.

verse.text: Now therefore, please let your servant stay instead of the boy, my lord’s slave; and let the boy go up with his brothers.

genesis-44.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-45.summary: Joseph can no longer hold back and sends everyone else out. He weeps aloud and says, “I am Joseph!” His brothers are too afraid to answer. He says not to be angry, because God sent him ahead to save lives. Five years of famine remain, so they must bring his father to Goshen. He weeps on Benjamin and kisses all his brothers. Pharaoh sends wagons and promises the best of Egypt. Jacob’s heart faints at the news, then revives when he sees the wagons.

verse.text: Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.

genesis-45.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-46.summary: Israel sets out and offers sacrifices at Beersheba. God tells him in a night vision not to fear going to Egypt. God will make him a great nation there and bring him back. Jacob’s sons carry him, their wives, and their children in Pharaoh’s wagons. The chapter lists the family by mother, seventy people in all. Judah goes ahead to lead the way to Goshen. Joseph meets his father and weeps on his neck for a long time. He tells his brothers to say they are herdsmen, so they can live in Goshen.

verse.text: that you shall say, ‘Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers:’ that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.”

genesis-46.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-47.summary: Joseph presents five brothers to Pharaoh, and they ask to live in Goshen as shepherds. Pharaoh gives them the best of the land. Jacob, age 130, blesses Pharaoh and calls his years few and hard. The famine grows worse. The Egyptians pay Joseph for grain with money, then with livestock. In the end they sell their land and themselves to Pharaoh. Joseph gives them seed and takes a fifth of each harvest for Pharaoh. Before he dies, Israel makes Joseph swear to bury him in Canaan.

verse.text: Then Joseph said to the people, “Behold, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh. Behold, here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land.

genesis-47.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-48.summary: Joseph hears his father is sick and brings his sons Manasseh and Ephraim. Jacob recalls God’s promise at Luz and claims the two boys as his own sons. He remembers Rachel’s death on the road. Israel’s eyes are dim, and he kisses the boys. Joseph sets Manasseh, the firstborn, at Israel’s right hand. Israel crosses his hands and puts his right hand on Ephraim. Joseph objects, and his father says, “I know, my son, I know.” He sets Ephraim before Manasseh and promises that God will bring them back.

verse.text: His father refused, and said, “I know, my son, I know. He also will become a people, and he also will be great. However, his younger brother will be greater than he, and his offspring will become a multitude of nations.”

genesis-48.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-49.summary: Jacob gathers his sons to tell what will come to each. Reuben, the firstborn, will not excel, because he went to his father’s bed. Simeon and Levi are cursed for their anger and will be scattered. Judah is a lion’s cub, and the ruler’s staff will stay with him. Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, and Naphtali each get a short saying. Joseph is a fruitful vine, helped by the Mighty One of Jacob. Benjamin is a hungry wolf. Jacob orders his burial in the cave at Machpelah and dies.

verse.text: Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel. I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.

genesis-49.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

genesis-50.summary: Joseph weeps over his father and has him embalmed. Egypt mourns seventy days. With Pharaoh’s leave, Joseph and a great company bury Jacob in the cave at Machpelah. Back in Egypt the brothers fear that Joseph will now repay them. They send a message asking forgiveness and bow before him. Joseph weeps and tells them not to fear. He says they meant evil, but God meant it for good, to save many lives. Dying at 110, he makes Israel swear to carry his bones out of Egypt.

verse.text: Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for am I in the place of God?

genesis-50.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-1.summary: Jacob’s seventy descendants in Egypt grow into a great people after Joseph dies. A new king who did not know Joseph fears their numbers. He sets taskmasters over them, and they build the store cities Pithom and Raamses. The harder Egypt presses them, the more they multiply. The king tells the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah, to kill newborn boys. The midwives fear God and let the boys live. God deals well with them and gives them families. Pharaoh then orders all his people to throw Hebrew baby boys into the river.

verse.text: Therefore they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with their burdens. They built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses.

exodus-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-2.summary: A Levite woman bears a son and hides him three months. She puts him in a papyrus basket among the river reeds, and his sister watches. Pharaoh’s daughter finds him, pities him, and knows he is a Hebrew child. The sister offers a nurse and brings the boy’s own mother. Pharaoh’s daughter adopts him and names him Moses. Grown, Moses kills an Egyptian who beat a Hebrew, and he flees to Midian. He defends seven sisters at a well and marries one, Zipporah. Israel groans in slavery, and God hears and remembers his covenant.

verse.text: The child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, and said, “Because I drew him out of the water.”

exodus-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-3.summary: Moses keeps his father-in-law’s flock and comes to Horeb, God’s mountain. He sees a bush on fire that does not burn up. God calls him by name and tells him to take off his sandals. The LORD has seen his people’s suffering and has come down to rescue them. He sends Moses to Pharaoh, and Moses asks, “Who am I?” God promises to be with him and gives his name: “I AM WHO I AM.” Moses must tell the elders and then ask Pharaoh for a three-day journey. God says Pharaoh will refuse until God strikes Egypt.

verse.text: The LORD said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows.

routes.title: Moses leads the flock to Horeb

exodus-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-4.summary: Moses says the people will not believe him. The LORD gives him three signs with a rod, his hand, and river water. Moses says he is slow of speech and asks God to send someone else. The LORD is angry and names Aaron, his brother, to speak for him. Moses takes leave of Jethro and sets out with his wife and sons. The LORD tells him to call Israel “my firstborn” before Pharaoh. On the way the LORD meets him to kill him, and Zipporah circumcises her son. Aaron meets Moses, and the people believe and worship.

verse.text: The LORD’s anger burned against Moses, and he said, “What about Aaron, your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. Also, behold, he is coming out to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.

exodus-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-5.summary: Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh the LORD’s word: let my people go. Pharaoh says he does not know the LORD and will not let Israel go. He calls the people idle. That day he orders that they get no straw but make as many bricks. The people scatter to gather stubble, and their Israelite officers are beaten. The officers appeal to Pharaoh, and he repeats, “You are idle!” They blame Moses and Aaron. Moses asks the LORD why he sent him, since the people are not rescued.

verse.text: But Pharaoh said, “You are idle! You are idle! Therefore you say, ‘Let’s go and sacrifice to the LORD.’

exodus-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-6.summary: The LORD tells Moses that Pharaoh will drive Israel out by a strong hand. God says he is the LORD, who made a covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He has heard Israel groan and remembers that covenant. He promises to free them, take them as his people, and give them the land. The people do not listen, because of crushed spirits and cruel slavery. Moses asks how Pharaoh will listen if Israel will not. The chapter lists the families of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi, down to Aaron and Moses. The LORD again sends Moses to Pharaoh.

verse.text: Moses spoke so to the children of Israel, but they didn’t listen to Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.

exodus-6.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-7.summary: The LORD makes Moses like God to Pharaoh, with Aaron as his prophet. He says Pharaoh will not listen, and Egypt will learn that he is the LORD. Moses is eighty and Aaron eighty-three. Aaron’s rod becomes a serpent before Pharaoh, and it swallows the magicians’ rods. Pharaoh’s heart stays hard. In the morning Aaron strikes the river, and its water turns to blood. The fish die, and the Egyptians dig for water to drink. The magicians do the same, and Pharaoh goes home unmoved.

verse.text: Moses and Aaron did so, as the LORD commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and struck the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.

exodus-7.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-8.summary: Frogs come up from the river and fill houses, beds, and ovens. Pharaoh asks Moses to pray and promises to let the people go. The frogs die, and Pharaoh hardens his heart. Aaron strikes the dust, and it becomes lice on people and animals. The magicians cannot copy it and say, “This is God’s finger.” Swarms of flies fill Egypt, but not Goshen, where Israel lives. Pharaoh offers a sacrifice inside Egypt, then a short trip into the wilderness. Moses prays, the flies leave, and Pharaoh again refuses.

verse.text: Pharaoh said, “I will let you go, that you may sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness, only you shall not go very far away. Pray for me.”

exodus-8.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-9.summary: A disease kills Egypt’s livestock in the field, but none of Israel’s animals die. Moses throws furnace ashes into the air, and boils break out on people and animals. The magicians cannot stand before Moses. The LORD says he let Pharaoh stand to show his power in all the earth. He warns of heavy hail and tells Egypt to bring servants and animals inside. Some of Pharaoh’s servants fear the word and obey; others do not. Hail and fire strike all Egypt except Goshen. Pharaoh says he has sinned, but when the hail stops he hardens his heart.

verse.text: Those who feared the LORD’s word among the servants of Pharaoh made their servants and their livestock flee into the houses.

exodus-9.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-10.summary: The LORD says these signs are for Israel to tell their children and grandchildren. Moses warns of locusts, and Pharaoh’s servants beg him to let the men go. Pharaoh asks who will go, and Moses says everyone, with flocks and herds. Pharaoh will let only the men go and drives Moses out. Locusts eat every green thing the hail left. Pharaoh admits sin, the locusts are blown into the Red Sea, and he refuses again. Three days of thick darkness cover Egypt, but Israel has light. Pharaoh says to go but leave the animals, and Moses says not a hoof stays.

verse.text: Pharaoh called to Moses, and said, “Go, serve the LORD. Only let your flocks and your herds stay behind. Let your little ones also go with you.”

exodus-10.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-11.summary: The LORD tells Moses that one more plague will make Pharaoh drive Israel out. The people are to ask their Egyptian neighbors for silver and gold. Moses is highly regarded in Egypt. He tells Pharaoh the LORD will go through Egypt about midnight. Every firstborn will die, from Pharaoh’s son to the slave girl’s at the mill. A great cry will rise, but not a dog will bark at Israel. Moses leaves Pharaoh in hot anger. The LORD hardens Pharaoh’s heart, and he still refuses.

verse.text: and all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, even to the firstborn of the female servant who is behind the mill, and all the firstborn of livestock.

exodus-11.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-12.summary: The LORD makes this month the first of the year. Each household must take a lamb without defect and kill it on the fourteenth day. They put its blood on the door posts and eat it roasted, dressed to leave. The LORD will strike Egypt’s firstborn and pass over the houses with blood. Israel must keep this day and seven days of bread without yeast, forever. At midnight every Egyptian house has someone dead, and Pharaoh tells Israel to go. They leave in haste with unrisen dough and Egyptian silver and gold. About 600,000 men leave on foot, with a mixed crowd, after 430 years.

verse.text: It will happen, when your children ask you, ‘What do you mean by this service?’

exodus-12.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-13.summary: The LORD claims every firstborn male in Israel, human and animal. Moses tells the people to remember this day with seven days of unleavened bread. They must tell their sons what the LORD did when they left Egypt. Firstborn animals are sacrificed, and firstborn sons are bought back. God does not lead them by the near road through Philistine land. He says they might see war and return to Egypt. He leads them by the wilderness toward the Red Sea, and Moses carries Joseph’s bones. The LORD goes ahead in a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.

verse.text: When Pharaoh had let the people go, God didn’t lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, “Lest perhaps the people change their minds when they see war, and they return to Egypt”;

exodus-13.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-14.summary: The LORD has Israel camp by the sea, so Pharaoh will think they are trapped. Pharaoh regrets freeing his slaves and chases them with six hundred chosen chariots. The people see the army, cry out, and tell Moses that serving Egypt was better. Moses says to stand still and see the LORD’s rescue. The cloud moves behind Israel, between the two camps. Moses stretches out his hand, and an east wind divides the sea all night. Israel crosses on dry ground with walls of water on each side. The Egyptians follow, the water returns, and not one of them is left.

verse.text: Isn’t this the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”

routes.title: Israel turns back to the sea

exodus-14.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-15.summary: Moses and Israel sing to the LORD, who threw horse and rider into the sea. The song says the LORD is a warrior, and Pharaoh’s captains sank like a stone. It says the nations tremble and the LORD will plant his people on his mountain. Miriam the prophetess leads the women with tambourines and dancing. Israel then walks three days in the wilderness without water. At Marah the water is bitter, and the people grumble at Moses. The LORD shows Moses a tree that makes the water sweet. He promises health if they listen, and they camp at Elim’s twelve springs.

verse.text: The people murmured against Moses, saying, “What shall we drink?”

routes.title: From the sea to Marah and Elim

exodus-15.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-16.summary: In the second month Israel reaches the wilderness of Sin and complains of hunger. They say they wish they had died by the meat pots of Egypt. The LORD promises bread from the sky each day, as a test. Quail come at evening, and a fine flake covers the ground at dawn. Each person gathers an omer, and no one has too much or too little. What is kept overnight rots, except on the sixth day, when they gather double. On the seventh day there is none, because it is the Sabbath. They call it manna and eat it forty years.

verse.text: When they measured it with an omer, he who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack. They each gathered according to his eating.

routes.title: From Elim to the wilderness of Sin

exodus-16.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-17.summary: Israel camps at Rephidim, where there is no water. The people quarrel with Moses and say he brought them out to die. Moses cries to the LORD and says they are ready to stone him. He strikes the rock at Horeb before the elders, and water comes out. The place is named Massah and Meribah for their testing and quarrel. Amalek attacks, and Joshua leads the fight while Moses stands on the hill. Israel wins while Moses’ hands are up, so Aaron and Hur hold them until sunset. Moses builds an altar named “The LORD our Banner.”

verse.text: But Moses’ hands were heavy; so they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset.

routes.title: From the wilderness of Sin to Rephidim

exodus-17.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-18.summary: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law and priest of Midian, hears what the LORD did for Israel. He brings Moses’ wife Zipporah and their two sons to the camp. Moses tells him everything, and Jethro blesses the LORD and offers sacrifices. The next day Moses judges the people alone from morning to evening. Jethro says this is not good and will wear out Moses and the people. He advises choosing honest, able men to judge small cases. Hard cases will still come to Moses. Moses does all this, and Jethro goes home.

verse.text: If you will do this thing, and God commands you so, then you will be able to endure, and all these people also will go to their place in peace.”

exodus-18.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-19.summary: In the third month Israel camps before Mount Sinai. The LORD reminds them how he carried them on eagles’ wings. If they keep his covenant, they will be his own, a kingdom of priests. All the people answer that they will do what the LORD has spoken. They wash their clothes, and a boundary is set around the mountain. On the third day there is thunder, lightning, thick cloud, and a loud trumpet. The mountain smokes and shakes as the LORD comes down in fire. Moses goes up and is sent back to warn the people.

verse.text: All the people answered together, and said, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do.” Moses reported the words of the people to the LORD.

exodus-19.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-20.summary: God speaks and names himself as the one who brought Israel out of slavery. He commands no other gods, no idols, and no misuse of his name. The seventh day is a Sabbath of rest for children, servants, animals, and strangers. They must honor father and mother. They must not murder, commit adultery, steal, give false testimony, or covet. The people tremble at the thunder and smoke and stand far off. They ask Moses to speak for God, and Moses goes into the thick darkness. The LORD forbids gods of silver or gold and allows a plain altar of earth.

verse.text: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work in it, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates;

exodus-20.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-21.summary: These are the rulings set before Israel. A Hebrew servant serves six years and goes free in the seventh. A daughter sold as a servant keeps rights to food and clothing, or goes free. Murder brings death, but an accidental killer may flee to a set place. Kidnapping and striking or cursing parents bring death. One who injures another pays for lost time and healing. A master who destroys a servant’s eye or tooth must free that servant. Owners pay for harm from an open pit or a bull known to gore.

verse.text: “If a man strikes his servant’s eye, or his maid’s eye, and destroys it, he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.

exodus-21.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-22.summary: A thief pays back more than he stole, up to five oxen for one. A person pays for crops ruined by his animal or his fire. Disputes over goods left in another’s care come before God. A man who seduces an unpledged virgin must pay a dowry for her. Israel must not wrong a foreigner, because they were foreigners in Egypt. God will hear the cry of any widow or fatherless child they wrong. Lenders must not charge the poor interest. A cloak taken as a pledge must be returned before sunset.

verse.text: If you take your neighbor’s garment as collateral, you shall restore it to him before the sun goes down,

exodus-22.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-23.summary: Israel must not spread false reports or follow a crowd to do evil. Judges must not favor the poor or deny them justice, and must refuse bribes. A person must return an enemy’s stray ox and help his fallen donkey. Israel must not oppress foreigners, since they know a foreigner’s heart. The land rests every seventh year so the poor may eat. The seventh day gives rest to animals, servants, and foreigners. Three feasts are kept each year. God will send an angel ahead and drive out the nations little by little.

verse.text: If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him. You shall surely help him with it.

exodus-23.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-24.summary: The LORD calls Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders to come up and worship. Moses tells the people all the LORD’s words, and they promise to do them. He writes the words down and builds an altar with twelve pillars. He reads the book of the covenant aloud, and the people again promise to obey. Moses sprinkles blood on the altar and on the people. The leaders go up, see the God of Israel, and eat and drink. The LORD calls Moses higher to receive stone tablets. Moses enters the cloud and stays forty days and nights.

verse.text: He took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people, and they said, “We will do all that the LORD has said, and be obedient.”

exodus-24.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-25.summary: The LORD tells Moses to take an offering from everyone with a willing heart. The gifts are gold, silver, bronze, fine cloth, skins, wood, oil, spices, and stones. The people are to make a sanctuary so that God may live among them. They must follow the pattern God shows Moses. The ark is a gold-covered chest with poles, and it holds the covenant. Its gold cover, the mercy seat, has two cherubim, and God will meet Moses there. A gold-covered table holds the bread of the presence. A lamp stand of pure gold has seven lamps.

verse.text: Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.

exodus-25.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-26.summary: The tabernacle is made of ten linen curtains in blue, purple, and scarlet, with cherubim. Gold clasps join them into one piece. A cover of goats’ hair goes over it, then ram skins and hides. Upright boards of acacia wood stand in silver sockets and are held by bars. All of it follows what Moses saw on the mountain. A veil with cherubim hangs on four pillars inside. The ark goes behind the veil, in the most holy place. The table and lamp stand stay outside the veil, and a screen covers the door.

verse.text: You shall hang up the veil under the clasps, and shall bring the ark of the covenant in there within the veil. The veil shall separate the holy place from the most holy for you.

exodus-26.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-27.summary: The altar is square, made of acacia wood covered with bronze, with horns. Its pots, shovels, basins, and grating are bronze, and poles carry it. The court around the tabernacle is one hundred cubits long and fifty wide. Linen hangings on bronze-footed pillars form its walls. A screen of blue, purple, and scarlet covers the gate. The people of Israel must bring pure beaten olive oil for the lamp. Aaron and his sons keep the lamp burning from evening to morning. This is a lasting rule for Israel.

verse.text: “You shall command the children of Israel, that they bring to you pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.

exodus-27.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-28.summary: Aaron and his four sons become priests, and skilled workers make Aaron’s holy garments. The ephod, a priestly garment, has two shoulder stones with the names of Israel’s sons. The breastplate holds twelve stones, one for each tribe. Aaron carries the names over his heart when he enters the holy place. The Urim and Thummim go in the breastplate. A blue robe has gold bells on its hem. A gold plate on his forehead says “HOLY TO THE LORD.” His sons receive tunics, sashes, and headbands.

verse.text: Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment on his heart, when he goes in to the holy place, for a memorial before the LORD continually.

exodus-28.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-29.summary: Moses is told how to make Aaron and his sons priests. They are washed, dressed in the holy garments, and anointed with oil. A bull is offered for sin, and a ram is burned whole. Blood from a second ram goes on each priest’s right ear, thumb, and big toe. The priests eat their share of that ram at the tent door. The rites last seven days and also make the altar holy. After that two lambs are offered every day, one at morning and one at evening. God says he will meet Israel there and live among them.

verse.text: I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God.

exodus-29.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-30.summary: A small gold altar for incense stands before the veil. Aaron burns incense on it every morning and evening. When Israel is counted, each man twenty and older gives half a shekel. The rich give no more and the poor no less. The money serves the Tent of Meeting. A bronze basin holds water for the priests to wash hands and feet. A holy spiced oil anoints the tent, its furniture, and the priests. No one may copy the oil or the incense for private use.

verse.text: The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than the half shekel, when they give the offering of the LORD, to make atonement for your souls.

exodus-30.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-31.summary: The LORD names Bezalel of Judah and fills him with God’s Spirit and skill. He will work in gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood. Oholiab of Dan will work with him, and other skilled people will help. They are to make the tent, its furniture, the garments, the oil, and the incense. Then the LORD says Israel must surely keep his Sabbaths. The Sabbath is a sign between God and Israel for all generations. Six days are for work, and the seventh is holy rest. God gives Moses two stone tablets written with his finger.

verse.text: “Speak also to the children of Israel, saying, ‘Most certainly you shall keep my Sabbaths; for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you.

exodus-31.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-32.summary: Moses delays on the mountain, and the people ask Aaron to make gods. Aaron collects their gold earrings and makes a calf. The people say these gods brought them out of Egypt, and they feast. The LORD tells Moses he will destroy them, and Moses pleads for them. The LORD turns from the harm he spoke of. Moses comes down, sees the calf and dancing, and breaks the tablets. He grinds the calf to powder, and Aaron blames the people and the fire. The Levites kill about three thousand, and Moses asks God to forgive the people.

verse.text: He received what they handed him, fashioned it with an engraving tool, and made it a molded calf. Then they said, “These are your gods, Israel, which brought you up out of the land of Egypt.”

exodus-32.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-33.summary: The LORD tells Moses to lead the people on, with an angel ahead. He says he will not go among them, because they are stubborn. The people mourn and take off their jewelry. Moses pitches a tent outside the camp, and the cloud comes down when he enters. The LORD speaks with Moses face to face, as with a friend. Moses says that if God’s presence does not go, they should not leave. The LORD agrees to go with them. Moses asks to see God’s glory and is allowed to see his back.

verse.text: Moses said to him, “If your presence doesn’t go with me, don’t carry us up from here.

exodus-33.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-34.summary: Moses cuts two new stone tablets and goes up Sinai alone. The LORD comes down in the cloud and declares his name. He is merciful, slow to anger, and forgiving, yet does not clear the guilty. Moses bows and asks God to go with this stubborn people and pardon them. The LORD makes a covenant and promises wonders. Israel must make no treaty with the people of the land or worship their gods. The feasts, firstborn, and Sabbath laws are repeated. Moses comes down with a shining face and afterward wears a veil.

verse.text: The LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, “The LORD! The LORD, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,

exodus-34.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-35.summary: Moses gathers all Israel and repeats the Sabbath rule first. Then he asks for an offering from everyone with a willing heart. He lists what must be made, from the tent to the priests’ garments. Men and women bring gold jewelry, cloth, skins, silver, bronze, and wood. Skilled women spin the colored yarn and the goats’ hair. The rulers bring stones, spice, and oil. All of it is a free offering to the LORD. Moses names Bezalel and Oholiab, whom God filled with skill to work and teach.

verse.text: The children of Israel brought a free will offering to the LORD; every man and woman whose heart made them willing to bring for all the work, which the LORD had commanded to be made by Moses.

exodus-35.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-36.summary: Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled worker begin the work. The people keep bringing free gifts every morning. The workers tell Moses there is far more than enough. Moses orders that no one bring anything more, and the people stop. The workers make the ten linen curtains with cherubim and join them with gold clasps. They make the goats’ hair covering and the skin coverings. They set up acacia boards in silver sockets and overlay them with gold. They make the veil and the screen for the door.

verse.text: Moses gave a commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, “Let neither man nor woman make anything else for the offering for the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing.

exodus-36.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-37.summary: Bezalel makes the ark of acacia wood and covers it with gold inside and out. He makes its rings and poles for carrying. He makes the gold mercy seat with two cherubim facing each other. He makes the gold-covered table and its dishes. He makes the lamp stand from one piece of pure gold, with seven lamps. He makes the gold incense altar with its poles. He makes the holy oil and the incense.

verse.text: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. Its length was two and a half cubits, and its width a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.

exodus-37.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-38.summary: Bezalel makes the bronze altar for burnt offerings with its tools and poles. He makes the bronze basin from the mirrors of women serving at the tent. He makes the court with linen hangings, bronze sockets, and silver hooks. Then the chapter gives the amounts of the materials. Ithamar, Aaron’s son, kept the count for the Levites. The gold weighed over twenty-nine talents. The silver came from the half shekel paid by 603,550 men. The bronze weighed over seventy talents, and each metal’s use is listed.

verse.text: These are the amounts of materials used for the tabernacle, even the Tabernacle of the Testimony, as they were counted, according to the commandment of Moses, for the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.

exodus-38.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-39.summary: The workers make Aaron’s holy garments from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. They beat gold into thin wires and weave it into the ephod. They set the onyx shoulder stones and the twelve stones of the breastplate. They make the blue robe with bells and pomegranates on its hem. They make tunics, turbans, and sashes, and the gold plate reading “HOLY TO THE LORD.” All the work is finished as the LORD commanded Moses. The people bring every part to Moses. He inspects it and blesses them.

verse.text: Moses saw all the work, and behold, they had done it as the LORD had commanded. They had done so; and Moses blessed them.

exodus-39.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

exodus-40.summary: The LORD tells Moses to raise the tabernacle on the year’s first day. Moses puts the covenant in the ark and hangs the veil in front of it. He sets the table, the lamp stand, and the incense altar in their places. He puts the altar of burnt offering and the basin outside. He anoints the tent and washes and dresses Aaron and his sons. Moses finishes the work, and the cloud covers the tent. The LORD’s glory fills it, and Moses cannot enter. Israel travels when the cloud lifts and stays when it rests.

verse.text: When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward, throughout all their journeys;

exodus-40.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-1.summary: The LORD speaks to Moses from the Tent of Meeting about offerings. A burnt offering from the herd must be a male without defect. The giver lays a hand on its head and kills it. The priests sprinkle its blood on the altar and arrange the pieces on the fire. The giver washes the inner parts and legs, and the priest burns all of it. The same steps apply to a sheep or goat. A burnt offering may also be doves or pigeons, which the priest handles. Each is called a pleasant aroma to the LORD.

verse.text: He shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.

leviticus-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-2.summary: A meal offering is fine flour with oil and frankincense. The priest burns a handful with all the frankincense as a memorial part. The rest belongs to Aaron and his sons and is most holy. The offering may be baked in an oven, on a griddle, or in a pan. It must have no yeast and no honey. Every meal offering must be seasoned with salt. A first fruits offering is fresh grain, roasted and crushed, with oil and frankincense.

verse.text: That which is left of the meal offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is a most holy part of the offerings of the LORD made by fire.

leviticus-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-3.summary: A peace offering may be a male or female animal without defect. It may come from the herd, the sheep, or the goats. The giver lays a hand on its head and kills it at the tent door. The priests sprinkle the blood around the altar. The fat around the inner parts, the kidneys, and the liver cover are burned. For a lamb, the whole fat tail is burned too. All the fat belongs to the LORD. Israel must never eat fat or blood.

verse.text: “ ‘It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings, that you shall eat neither fat nor blood.’ ”

leviticus-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-4.summary: These offerings are for sins done without meaning to. If the anointed priest sins, the people share the guilt, and he offers a bull. Its blood is sprinkled before the veil, and its body is burned outside the camp. If the whole assembly sins, the elders lay hands on a bull. A ruler who sins brings a male goat. A common person brings a female goat or lamb. In each case the priest makes atonement, and the person is forgiven.

verse.text: if the anointed priest sins so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin which he has sinned a young bull without defect to the LORD for a sin offering.

leviticus-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-5.summary: Some cases need a trespass offering. A witness stays silent, a person touches something unclean, or someone swears a rash oath. The guilty person must confess the sin. He brings a female lamb or goat, and the priest makes atonement. If he cannot afford a lamb, he brings two doves or pigeons. If he cannot afford birds, he brings a tenth of an ephah of flour. One who misuses holy things brings a ram, repays the loss, and adds a fifth. A person who sins without knowing it is still guilty and brings a ram.

verse.text: “ ‘If he can’t afford a lamb, then he shall bring his trespass offering for that in which he has sinned, two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, to the LORD; one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.

leviticus-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-6.summary: A person may cheat a neighbor over a deposit, a theft, or a found item. He must return it in full and add a fifth. He gives it to the owner on the day he is found guilty. Then he brings a ram as a trespass offering and is forgiven. The priests must keep the altar fire burning all night and clear the ashes. The priests eat what is left of the meal offering in a holy place. A priest’s own meal offering is burned whole. The priest who offers a sin offering eats it in the court.

verse.text: or any thing about which he has sworn falsely: he shall restore it in full, and shall add a fifth part more to it. He shall return it to him to whom it belongs in the day of his being found guilty.

leviticus-6.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-7.summary: The trespass offering is most holy, and the priests eat it in a holy place. The priest who offers a burnt offering keeps its skin. A peace offering for thanksgiving comes with cakes and bread. Its meat must be eaten the same day. Meat from a vow or free will offering may be eaten for two days. Anything left on the third day is burned. No one may eat fat or blood, and the unclean may not eat this meat. The breast and right thigh of peace offerings go to the priests.

verse.text: The flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten on the day of his offering. He shall not leave any of it until the morning.

leviticus-7.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-8.summary: The LORD tells Moses to gather all the people at the tent door. Moses washes Aaron and his sons before them. He dresses Aaron in the tunic, robe, ephod, breastplate, and turban. He anoints the tabernacle, the altar, and Aaron with oil. He offers a bull for sin and a ram as a burnt offering. He puts blood from a second ram on their right ears, thumbs, and big toes. He sprinkles oil and blood on them and their garments. They stay at the tent door seven days.

verse.text: and assemble all the congregation at the door of the Tent of Meeting.”

leviticus-8.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-9.summary: On the eighth day Moses tells Aaron to offer a calf for his own sin. The people bring a goat, a calf, a lamb, a bull, and a ram. Moses says the LORD’s glory will appear to them. Aaron first offers the sin offering and burnt offering for himself. Then he offers the people’s goat, burnt offering, meal offering, and peace offerings. He lifts his hands and blesses the people. Moses and Aaron go into the tent, come out, and bless them again. The LORD’s glory appears, fire burns the offering, and the people fall down.

verse.text: Moses said to Aaron, “Draw near to the altar, and offer your sin offering, and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself, and for the people; and offer the offering of the people, and make atonement for them, as the LORD commanded.”

leviticus-9.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-10.summary: Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu offer strange fire that the LORD did not command. Fire comes out from the LORD and kills them. Moses says God will be shown holy, and Aaron keeps silent. Cousins carry the bodies out of the camp. Aaron and his other sons may not mourn openly or leave the tent. The LORD tells Aaron that priests must not drink wine on duty. They must tell holy from common and teach Israel the laws. Moses is angry that the sin offering was burned, not eaten, and accepts Aaron’s answer.

verse.text: Aaron spoke to Moses, “Behold, today they have offered their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD; and such things as these have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been pleasing in the LORD’s sight?”

leviticus-10.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-11.summary: The LORD tells Moses and Aaron which animals Israel may eat. Land animals must have a split hoof and chew the cud. Camels, hyraxes, hares, and pigs are unclean. Water creatures must have fins and scales. Many named birds are forbidden, and so are most winged insects, except locusts and grasshoppers. Touching a dead unclean animal makes a person unclean until evening. Pots and ovens that touch a carcass must be washed or broken. Israel must be holy, because the LORD who brought them from Egypt is holy.

verse.text: He who eats of its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening. He also who carries its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening.

leviticus-11.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-12.summary: A woman who bears a son is unclean for seven days. The boy is circumcised on the eighth day. She then waits thirty-three more days and may not enter the sanctuary. For a daughter the times are doubled: two weeks and sixty-six days. When the time ends, she brings the priest a lamb and a pigeon or dove. If she cannot afford a lamb, she brings two doves or two pigeons. The priest makes atonement for her, and she is clean.

verse.text: If she cannot afford a lamb, then she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons: the one for a burnt offering, and the other for a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.’ ”

leviticus-12.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-13.summary: A person with a swelling, scab, or bright spot goes to a priest. The priest looks for white hair and a mark deeper than the skin. If it is unclear, he isolates the person for seven days and looks again. He may wait seven more days before deciding. A faded mark means clean, and a spreading one means unclean. A person with leprosy wears torn clothes, calls out “Unclean,” and lives outside the camp. Cloth or leather with a greenish or reddish spot is also shown to the priest. It is shut away seven days and burned if the spot spreads.

verse.text: The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. Behold, if in his eyes the plague is arrested and the plague hasn’t spread in the skin, then the priest shall isolate him for seven more days.

leviticus-13.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-14.summary: This is the law for a healed leper. The priest goes outside the camp to examine him. Two birds are used: one is killed, and the living one is set free. The person washes, shaves, and waits seven days before entering his tent. On the eighth day he brings lambs, flour, and oil, and the priest makes atonement. A poor person may bring one lamb and two birds. A house with spreading mildew is emptied, shut up, scraped, and, if needed, torn down. A house that stays clear is declared clean.

verse.text: “If he is poor, and can’t afford so much, then he shall take one male lamb for a trespass offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, and one tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering, and a log of oil;

leviticus-14.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-15.summary: A man with a bodily discharge is unclean. His bed, his seat, and anyone he touches become unclean until evening. When it stops, he counts seven days, washes, and brings two birds to the priest. A man with an emission of semen bathes and is unclean until evening. A woman in her monthly period is unclean for seven days. A longer flow of blood makes her unclean for as long as it lasts. When it stops, she counts seven days and brings two birds. These rules keep Israel from defiling the tabernacle that is among them.

verse.text: “ ‘Thus you shall separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, so they will not die in their uncleanness when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.’ ”

leviticus-15.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-16.summary: Aaron may not enter the Most Holy Place at just any time. Once a year he bathes and dresses in plain linen. He offers a bull for himself and his house. He casts lots over two goats: one for the LORD and one as the scapegoat. He takes incense and blood inside the veil and sprinkles the mercy seat. He makes atonement for the Holy Place, the tent, and the altar. He confesses Israel’s sins over the live goat and sends it into the wilderness. On that day, the tenth of the seventh month, all Israel rests and humbles itself.

verse.text: He shall make atonement for the Holy Place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions, even all their sins; and so he shall do for the Tent of Meeting that dwells with them in the middle of their uncleanness.

leviticus-16.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-17.summary: Anyone who kills a bull, lamb, or goat must bring it to the tent door. Killing it elsewhere counts as bloodshed. The rule is meant to end sacrifices in the open field to goat idols. The priest sprinkles the blood on the LORD’s altar. No Israelite or foreigner living among them may eat blood. The life is in the blood, and God gave it for atonement on the altar. A hunter must pour out the blood of his catch and cover it with dust. Anyone who eats an animal found dead must wash and wait until evening.

verse.text: For the life of the flesh is in the blood. I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls; for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life.

leviticus-17.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-18.summary: The LORD tells Israel not to follow the practices of Egypt or Canaan. They must keep his statutes and live by them. The chapter forbids sexual relations with close relatives, and it lists them one by one. It forbids marrying a wife’s sister as a rival, and adultery. It forbids giving children to Molech. It forbids a man lying with a man, and sex with animals. The nations before Israel did these things, and the land was defiled. The land vomited them out, and it will do the same to Israel.

verse.text: that the land not vomit you out also, when you defile it, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.

leviticus-18.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-19.summary: The LORD tells all Israel to be holy, because he is holy. They must respect parents, keep Sabbaths, and avoid idols. Farmers must leave field corners and fallen grapes for the poor and the foreigner. They must not steal, lie, hold back wages overnight, or trip the blind. Judges must not favor the poor or the great. They must not hate or take revenge, but love their neighbor as themselves. They must love the foreigner as themselves, since they were foreigners in Egypt. Scales, weights, and measures must be honest.

verse.text: You shall have just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.

leviticus-19.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-20.summary: Anyone who gives a child to Molech must be stoned. If the people look away, God will act against that family. Those who turn to mediums are cut off. Israel must be holy and keep God’s statutes. Death is set for cursing parents, adultery, and several unions forbidden in chapter 18. Other unions bring being cut off or dying childless. Israel must not follow the customs of the nations being driven out. The LORD has set them apart to be his and to inherit the land.

verse.text: But I have said to you, “You shall inherit their land, and I will give it to you to possess it, a land flowing with milk and honey.” I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

leviticus-20.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-21.summary: Priests may not touch the dead, except for their closest relatives. They may not shave their heads or cut their flesh. They may not marry a prostitute or a divorced woman. The high priest may not go near any dead body, even a parent’s. He must marry a virgin of his own people. A priest with a bodily defect may not come near the altar or the veil.
