The list includes the blind, the lame, and the injured. He may still eat the holy and most holy food.

verse.text: He shall eat the bread of his God, both of the most holy, and of the holy.

leviticus-21.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-22.summary: Priests must stay away from the holy food while they are unclean. An unclean priest washes, waits until evening, and then may eat his bread. Only the priest’s household may eat it, including a slave he bought. A married daughter may not, but a childless widow who returns home may. Anyone who eats it by mistake repays it and adds a fifth. Animals for vows and free gifts must have no defect. A newborn animal stays seven days with its mother. A cow or ewe and its young may not be killed on the same day.

verse.text: Whether it is a cow or ewe, you shall not kill it and its young both in one day.

leviticus-22.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-23.summary: The LORD gives Moses the set feasts of the year. The Sabbath comes every seventh day. Passover falls in the first month, with seven days of unleavened bread. A sheaf of first grain is waved, and fifty days later two loaves are offered. At harvest the field corners and gleanings are left for the poor and the foreigner. The seventh month has a day of trumpets and the day of atonement. Then comes the seven-day feast of booths. Israel lives in shelters to remember the journey out of Egypt.

verse.text: “ ‘When you reap the harvest of your land, you must not wholly reap into the corners of your field. You must not gather the gleanings of your harvest. You must leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.’ ”

leviticus-23.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-24.summary: Israel must bring pure olive oil so the lamp burns every night. Twelve loaves are set on the gold table each Sabbath, and the priests eat them. Then a fight breaks out in the camp. A man with an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father curses the Name. He is held until the LORD’s will is known. The LORD orders the hearers to lay hands on him and all to stone him. The LORD adds rules: life for life, eye for eye, and payment for animals. The same law applies to the foreigner and the native-born.

verse.text: You shall have one kind of law for the foreigner as well as the native-born; for I am the LORD your God.’ ”

leviticus-24.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-25.summary: Every seventh year the land must rest, with no sowing or pruning. After forty-nine years a trumpet announces the fiftieth year, the Jubilee. Liberty is declared, and each person returns to his family’s land. Land prices follow the number of crops left before the Jubilee. The land may not be sold forever, because it belongs to the LORD. A relative may buy back land for a poor brother. Israel must lend to the poor without interest. A poor Israelite who sells himself serves as hired help until the Jubilee.

verse.text: “ ‘The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine; for you are strangers and live as foreigners with me.

leviticus-25.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-26.summary: Israel must make no idols and must keep the Sabbaths. If they obey, God will send rain, harvests, peace, and victory. He will set his tent among them and walk with them. If they refuse, he will send sickness, defeat, drought, wild animals, and siege. Each stage is harder than the last. In the end their cities fall, and they are scattered among the nations. Then the land will enjoy the Sabbaths it missed. If they confess, God will remember his covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.

verse.text: Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly and to break my covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.

leviticus-26.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

leviticus-27.summary: A person vowed to the LORD is given a value in silver. The value depends on age and sex, from three to fifty shekels. A poor person is valued by the priest according to what he can pay. An animal given for offering becomes holy and may not be swapped. A house or field may be dedicated and bought back by adding a fifth. A field’s value is counted by the years left until the Jubilee. Firstborn animals already belong to the LORD. A tenth of crops and herds is holy to the LORD.

verse.text: But if he is poorer than your valuation, then he shall be set before the priest, and the priest shall assign a value to him. The priest shall assign a value according to his ability to pay.

leviticus-27.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-1.summary: In the second year after Egypt, the LORD tells Moses to count Israel. The count covers men twenty and older who can go to war. One leader from each tribe helps Moses and Aaron. Each tribe is counted by families and fathers’ houses. The total is 603,550. The Levites are not counted with the rest. They care for the tabernacle, carry it, and camp around it. No outsider may come near it.

verse.text: from twenty years old and upward, all who are able to go out to war in Israel. You and Aaron shall count them by their divisions.

numbers-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-2.summary: The LORD arranges the camp around the Tent of Meeting. Each tribe camps under its own banner, at a distance from the tent. Judah’s group camps on the east and sets out first. Reuben’s group camps on the south and sets out second. Then the tent moves, with the Levites in the middle. Ephraim’s group camps on the west and sets out third. Dan’s group camps on the north and sets out last. Israel camps and marches as the LORD commanded.

verse.text: “Then the Tent of Meeting shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. As they encamp, so shall they set out, every man in his place, by their standards.

numbers-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-3.summary: Aaron’s sons Eleazar and Ithamar serve as priests after Nadab and Abihu die. The tribe of Levi is given to Aaron to help with the tabernacle. The LORD says he takes the Levites in place of every firstborn in Israel. The firstborn became his on the day he struck Egypt’s firstborn. Levite males a month old and up are counted: 22,000. Their three clans camp around the tent and each has its duties. Israel’s firstborn males number 22,273. The extra 273 are bought back at five shekels each, paid to Aaron.

verse.text: “Behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn who open the womb among the children of Israel; and the Levites shall be mine,

numbers-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-4.summary: The LORD orders a count of Levite men aged thirty to fifty. The sons of Kohath carry the most holy things. First Aaron and his sons cover the ark, table, lamp stand, and altars. The Kohathites must not touch or look at the holy things, or they will die. The sons of Gershon carry the curtains and coverings. The sons of Merari carry the boards, bars, pillars, and sockets. Aaron’s sons Eleazar and Ithamar direct the work. In all, 8,580 Levites are counted for this service.

verse.text: “When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the furniture of the sanctuary, as the camp moves forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to carry it; but they shall not touch the sanctuary, lest they die. The sons of Kohath shall carry these things belonging to the Tent of Meeting.

numbers-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-5.summary: The unclean are sent outside the camp, because the LORD dwells in it. Anyone who wrongs another must confess, repay in full, and add a fifth. If no relative can receive it, the payment goes to the priest. Then comes a law for a husband who suspects his wife and has no witness. He brings her to the priest with a barley offering. The priest mixes holy water with dust from the floor, and she swears an oath. She drinks the water. If guilty, her body swells; if not, she is free and can bear children.

verse.text: and the spirit of jealousy comes on him, and he is jealous of his wife and she is defiled; or if the spirit of jealousy comes on him, and he is jealous of his wife and she isn’t defiled;

numbers-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-6.summary: A man or woman may make a special vow as a Nazirite. For the days of the vow, the person avoids wine and anything from the grapevine. No razor touches the head, and the hair grows long. The person does not go near a dead body, even a parent’s. If someone dies nearby, the vow starts over after cleansing. When the time ends, the Nazirite brings offerings and shaves the head. Then the LORD gives the priests words to bless Israel. They ask the LORD to bless, keep, shine on, and give peace.

verse.text: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them: ‘When either man or woman shall make a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD,

numbers-6.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-7.summary: When the tabernacle is set up, the tribal leaders bring six wagons and twelve oxen. Moses gives two wagons to Gershon’s sons and four to Merari’s sons. Kohath’s sons get none, because they carry the holy things on their shoulders. Then each leader brings an offering for the altar, one leader each day. For twelve days every tribe gives the same gift. It is a silver platter, a silver bowl, a gold ladle of incense, and animals. The totals are listed at the end. Moses then hears the LORD’s voice from above the mercy seat.

verse.text: But to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the sanctuary belonged to them; they carried it on their shoulders.

numbers-7.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-8.summary: Aaron sets the seven lamps to light the space in front of the lamp stand. The Levites are cleansed with water, shaving, and washed clothes. The whole people gather and lay hands on them. Aaron presents them to the LORD as an offering from Israel. They belong to the LORD in place of Israel’s firstborn. Then they begin their service at the tent under Aaron and his sons. A Levite serves from age twenty-five to fifty. After fifty he stops the heavy work but may still assist his brothers.

verse.text: but shall assist their brothers in the Tent of Meeting, to perform the duty, and shall perform no service. This is how you shall have the Levites do their duties.”

numbers-8.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-9.summary: In the first month of the second year, Israel keeps the Passover at Sinai. Some men are unclean from touching a dead body and cannot join. They ask Moses why they must be kept back. Moses waits to hear from the LORD. The LORD says anyone unclean or far away may keep it one month later. A foreigner living with Israel may keep it by the same rules. The cloud covers the tabernacle by day and looks like fire by night. Israel camps while it rests and travels when it lifts, however long that takes.

verse.text: Those men said to him, “We are unclean because of the dead body of a man. Why are we kept back, that we may not offer the offering of the LORD in its appointed season among the children of Israel?”

numbers-9.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-10.summary: The LORD tells Moses to make two silver trumpets. Priests blow them to gather the people, start the march, and mark feasts. On the twentieth day of the second month the cloud lifts. Israel leaves Sinai in order, with Judah’s group first. The Levites carry the tabernacle and the holy things between the groups. Moses asks Hobab the Midianite to come and be their eyes in the wilderness. The ark goes ahead three days to find a resting place. Moses prays when the ark sets out and when it rests.

verse.text: Moses said, “Don’t leave us, please; because you know how we are to encamp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.

numbers-10.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-13.summary: The LORD tells Moses to send one leader from each tribe into Canaan. Moses tells them to look at the land, the people, and the cities. They travel forty days and bring back a huge cluster of grapes. They report that the land flows with milk and honey. They also say the people are strong and the cities walled. Caleb says Israel should go up at once and is well able to win. The others say the people are too strong. They spread a bad report and say they felt like grasshoppers.

verse.text: Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, “Let’s go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it!”

routes.title: The spies go up to Hebron

numbers-13.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-14.summary: The people weep all night and want to choose a leader and return to Egypt. Joshua and Caleb say the land is good and the LORD is with them. The people talk of stoning them. The LORD threatens to destroy them, and Moses pleads God’s name and mercy. The LORD pardons, but that generation will die in the wilderness over forty years. Only Caleb and Joshua will enter, with the children. The ten spies die of plague. The people then go up without Moses or the ark and are beaten back.

verse.text: But they presumed to go up to the top of the mountain. Nevertheless, the ark of the LORD’s covenant and Moses didn’t depart out of the camp.

numbers-14.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-20.summary: Miriam dies at Kadesh. There is no water, and the people quarrel with Moses and Aaron. The LORD tells Moses to take the rod and speak to the rock. Moses calls the people rebels and strikes the rock twice, and water pours out. The LORD says they did not believe him and will not bring Israel in. Edom refuses to let Israel pass through, even for payment. At Mount Hor, Moses puts Aaron’s garments on his son Eleazar. Aaron dies there, and Israel weeps thirty days.

verse.text: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you didn’t believe in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.”

routes.title: Messengers to the king of Edom

numbers-20.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-21.summary: The king of Arad attacks, and Israel defeats him after a vow to the LORD. On the road around Edom the people speak against God and Moses. They call the manna disgusting food. The LORD sends venomous snakes, and many die. The people confess, and Moses prays. Moses sets a bronze snake on a pole, and whoever looks at it lives. Israel travels on and sings at a well. They defeat the kings Sihon and Og and take their land.

verse.text: Moses made a serpent of bronze, and set it on the pole. If a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked at the serpent of bronze, he lived.

numbers-21.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-22.summary: Israel camps in the plains of Moab, and Moab is afraid. King Balak sends for Balaam to curse Israel. God tells Balaam not to go, because the people are blessed. Balak sends higher princes and promises great honor. God lets Balaam go but only to say what God tells him. The donkey sees the LORD’s angel with a sword and turns aside three times. Balaam beats her, and the LORD opens her mouth to speak. Then Balaam sees the angel, who lets him go on with the same warning.

verse.text: The LORD opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”

numbers-22.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-23.summary: Balaam has Balak build seven altars and offer bulls and rams. The LORD puts a word in Balaam’s mouth. Balaam asks how he can curse those whom God has not cursed. Balak takes him to a second place, where he sees only part of Israel. Seven more altars are built. Balaam says God is not a man who lies or changes his mind. God has blessed, and Balaam cannot reverse it. Balak takes him to a third place, the top of Peor.

verse.text: Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place, where you may see them. You shall see just part of them, and shall not see them all. Curse them from there for me.”

numbers-23.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-24.summary: Balaam sees that the LORD wants to bless Israel and uses no omens this time. The Spirit of God comes on him as he looks at Israel’s tents. He says their tents are lovely, like gardens by a river. He says those who bless Israel are blessed, and those who curse it are cursed. Balak is furious and sends him home without the promised honor. Balaam reminds him that no amount of silver could change the LORD’s word. He says a star will come from Jacob and a scepter from Israel. He speaks against Moab, Edom, Amalek, and others, and goes home.

verse.text: Therefore, flee to your place, now! I thought to promote you to great honor; but, behold, the LORD has kept you back from honor.”

numbers-24.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-25.summary: At Shittim, Israelite men go after Moabite women and join the sacrifices to their gods. Israel joins itself to Baal of Peor, and the LORD’s anger burns. Moses orders the judges to put the guilty to death. An Israelite man brings a Midianite woman into the camp while the people weep. Phinehas, Aaron’s grandson, kills them both with a spear. A plague stops after twenty-four thousand have died. The LORD gives Phinehas a covenant of peace and a lasting priesthood. The LORD tells Moses to treat the Midianites as enemies.

verse.text: It shall be to him, and to his offspring after him, the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he was jealous for his God, and made atonement for the children of Israel.’ ”

numbers-25.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-26.summary: After the plague the LORD orders a new count of men twenty and older. Moses and Eleazar count them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan. The list recalls Dathan, Abiram, and Korah, and notes that Korah’s sons did not die. It names Zelophehad’s five daughters. The total is 601,730. The land will be divided by these names: larger groups get more, smaller groups less. The place of each share is chosen by lot. No one from the first count is left except Caleb and Joshua.

verse.text: To the more you shall give the more inheritance, and to the fewer you shall give the less inheritance. To everyone according to those who were counted of him shall his inheritance be given.

numbers-26.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-27.summary: Zelophehad’s five daughters come before Moses, the priest, and the leaders. Their father died in the wilderness and left no son. They ask for land among their father’s brothers so his name is not lost. Moses brings their case to the LORD. The LORD says the daughters are right and must receive the inheritance. He makes it a rule: with no son, the land goes to a daughter. Then the LORD tells Moses he will see the land and die. Moses asks for a new leader and lays hands on Joshua before the people.

verse.text: Why should the name of our father be taken away from among his family, because he had no son? Give to us a possession among the brothers of our father.”

numbers-27.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-28.summary: The LORD tells Israel to bring his offerings at their set times. Two lambs are offered every day, one in the morning and one at evening. Each comes with flour, oil, and a drink offering. Two more lambs are offered every Sabbath. At each new month there are bulls, a ram, and seven lambs. Passover is on the fourteenth day of the first month. Seven days of unleavened bread follow, with offerings each day. The feast of weeks has its own offerings.

verse.text: “Command the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘See that you present my offering, my food for my offerings made by fire, as a pleasant aroma to me, in their due season.’

numbers-28.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-29.summary: The seventh month has three sacred times. The first day is a day of trumpets with rest and offerings. The tenth day is a day to humble oneself and do no work. On the fifteenth day a seven-day feast begins. Thirteen bulls are offered the first day, and one fewer each day after. On the seventh day there are seven bulls. The eighth day is a solemn assembly with one bull. These offerings are in addition to vows and free gifts.

verse.text: “ ‘On the eighth day you shall have a solemn assembly. You shall do no regular work;

numbers-29.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-30.summary: Moses tells the tribal heads the LORD’s rule on vows. A man who vows must not break his word. A young woman’s vow stands if her father hears it and says nothing. If he forbids it that day, it does not stand, and the LORD forgives her. A wife’s vow stands if her husband hears and says nothing. If he forbids it that day, it is void. A widow’s or divorced woman’s vow stands. A husband who cancels a vow later bears her guilt.

verse.text: But if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he establishes all her vows or all her pledges which are on her. He has established them, because he said nothing to her in the day that he heard them.

numbers-30.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-31.summary: The LORD tells Moses to take vengeance on Midian before he dies. Twelve thousand men go to war with Phinehas the priest. They kill Midian’s men, its five kings, and Balaam. They bring back the women, children, and herds. Moses is angry that the women were spared, because of what happened at Peor. He orders the boys and the women who have lain with a man killed. The soldiers purify themselves seven days outside the camp. The plunder is divided, and the officers give gold because no soldier was lost.

verse.text: Now therefore kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known man by lying with him.

numbers-31.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-32.summary: Reuben and Gad have large herds and want the grazing land east of the Jordan. They ask Moses for it and ask not to cross the river. Moses asks if their brothers should go to war while they sit there. He says they are acting like the spies who discouraged Israel. They promise to build towns for their families and then fight in front of Israel. They will not go home until every tribe has its land. Moses agrees and warns that their sin will find them out if they fail. He gives them and half of Manasseh the lands of Sihon and Og.

verse.text: Moses said to the children of Gad, and to the children of Reuben, “Shall your brothers go to war while you sit here?

numbers-32.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-33.summary: Moses writes down the stages of Israel’s journey at the LORD’s command. The list begins at Rameses, the day after the Passover. Egypt is burying its firstborn as Israel leaves. Dozens of camps are named, from the Red Sea to Sinai to Kadesh. Aaron dies on Mount Hor in the fortieth year, at age 123. The list ends in the plains of Moab by the Jordan. The LORD tells Israel to drive out Canaan’s people and destroy their idols. Any who remain will be like thorns in Israel’s sides.

verse.text: Moses wrote the starting points of their journeys by the commandment of the LORD. These are their journeys according to their starting points.

numbers-33.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-34.summary: The LORD gives Moses the borders of the land of Canaan. The south border runs from the Salt Sea along Edom. The Great Sea is the west border. The north and east borders are traced, ending at the Jordan and the Salt Sea. This land is for the nine and a half tribes, by lot. Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh already have land east of the Jordan. Eleazar the priest and Joshua will divide the land. One leader from each tribe is named to help, with Caleb for Judah.

verse.text: You shall take one prince of every tribe, to divide the land for inheritance.

numbers-34.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-35.summary: Israel must give the Levites forty-eight towns with pasture land around them. Six of these are cities of refuge. A person who kills someone by accident may flee there from the avenger. He must not die before he stands trial before the community. One who killed with a weapon or from hatred is put to death. One who killed without hatred stays in the city until the high priest dies. No one is put to death on one witness alone. No payment can free a murderer, because blood pollutes the land.

verse.text: The cities shall be for your refuge from the avenger, that the man slayer not die until he stands before the congregation for judgment.

numbers-35.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

numbers-36.summary: The family heads of Manasseh come to Moses with a problem. Zelophehad’s daughters will inherit land. If they marry men of another tribe, the land will pass to that tribe. Moses answers by the LORD’s word that they speak rightly. The daughters may marry whom they think best, but only within their father’s tribe. Any daughter who inherits land must do the same. The five daughters marry sons of their father’s brothers. So their land stays in Manasseh, and the book ends in the plains of Moab.

verse.text: This is the thing which the LORD commands concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, ‘Let them be married to whom they think best, only they shall marry into the family of the tribe of their father.

numbers-36.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-1.summary: Moses speaks to all Israel east of the Jordan in the fortieth year. He recalls how the LORD told them at Horeb to go and take the land. He recalls choosing leaders and judges to share his load. At Kadesh the people asked for spies, who brought back good fruit. Still the people refused to go up and said the LORD hated them. The LORD swore that generation would not see the land, except Caleb and Joshua. Moses says the LORD was angry with him too. The people then went up without the LORD and were beaten back.

verse.text: Also the LORD was angry with me for your sakes, saying, “You also shall not go in there.

deuteronomy-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-2.summary: Israel wandered around Mount Seir for many days. The LORD told them not to fight Esau’s people and to pay for food. He gave Moab and Ammon to Lot’s children, so Israel must leave them alone. Other peoples had also replaced earlier peoples in those lands. Thirty-eight years passed until the fighting men of the first generation died. Then the LORD gave Sihon the Amorite into Israel’s hand. Moses sent Sihon words of peace, and Sihon refused. Israel defeated him and destroyed his cities.

verse.text: Don’t contend with them; for I will not give you any of their land, no, not so much as for the sole of the foot to tread on, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau for a possession.

routes.title: Past Edom and Moab to Heshbon

deuteronomy-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-3.summary: Og king of Bashan comes out to fight, and the LORD gives him to Israel. Israel takes his sixty walled cities. Moses gives the land east of the Jordan to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. Their fighting men must still cross and help their brothers. Moses tells Joshua not to fear the kingdoms ahead. Moses begs the LORD to let him cross and see the good land. The LORD refuses and tells him to look from the top of Pisgah. He must strengthen Joshua, who will lead the people over.

verse.text: But commission Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him; for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which you shall see.”

deuteronomy-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-4.summary: Moses tells Israel to keep the statutes and not add or take away. Other nations will call Israel wise for having such laws and so near a God. They must not forget Horeb, where the mountain burned and they heard a voice. They saw no form, so they must make no image of any creature. They must not worship the sun, moon, or stars. If they make idols, they will be scattered among the nations. Yet if they seek the LORD there with all their heart, they will find him. Moses sets apart three cities of refuge east of the Jordan.

verse.text: Be very careful, for you saw no kind of form on the day that the LORD spoke to you in Horeb out of the middle of the fire,

deuteronomy-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-5.summary: Moses calls all Israel to hear the statutes. He says the covenant at Horeb was made with those alive today. He repeats the ten commandments. The Sabbath command says servants must rest as well as their masters. Israel must remember it was a servant in Egypt until the LORD brought it out. The LORD wrote the words on two stone tablets. The people were afraid of the fire and asked Moses to listen for them. The LORD approved and wished they would always have such a heart.

verse.text: You shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out of there by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm. Therefore the LORD your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.

deuteronomy-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-6.summary: Moses gives the commandments Israel must keep in the land. The LORD is one, and Israel must love him with heart, soul, and might. These words must be on their hearts and taught to their children. They talk of them at home, on the road, at night, and at dawn. They are to tie them on hand and forehead and write them on doorposts. In the land they will have cities, houses, wells, and vineyards they did not make. Then they must not forget the LORD. When a son asks what the laws mean, the parent tells of slavery and rescue.

verse.text: and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.

deuteronomy-6.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-7.summary: Moses says the LORD will drive out seven nations greater than Israel. Israel is told to destroy them, make no treaty, and not marry among them. The reason given is that they would turn Israel to other gods. Israel must break their altars and burn their images. The LORD chose Israel, though it was the fewest of all peoples. He chose it because he loves it and keeps his oath to the fathers. If Israel obeys, he will bless its children, crops, and herds. The nations will be driven out little by little.

verse.text: The LORD didn’t set his love on you nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples;

deuteronomy-7.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-8.summary: Moses tells Israel to remember the forty years in the wilderness. God humbled them, let them hunger, and fed them with manna. He taught them that people do not live by bread alone. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell. Now he brings them to a land of water, wheat, vines, olives, and metal. When they are full and rich, they must not forget the LORD. They must not say their own power got this wealth. If they forget and serve other gods, they will perish like the nations before them.

verse.text: and lest you say in your heart, “My power and the might of my hand has gotten me this wealth.”

deuteronomy-8.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-9.summary: Israel is about to cross the Jordan against nations greater and taller. The LORD will go ahead like a devouring fire. Israel must not say the land is a reward for its righteousness. The nations are driven out for their wickedness and because of God’s oath. Israel is a stubborn people, and Moses tells them to remember it. He recalls the golden calf, the broken tablets, and forty days of prayer. He names Taberah, Massah, Kibroth Hattaavah, and Kadesh. He prayed that God would remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and spare his people.

verse.text: Know therefore that the LORD your God doesn’t give you this good land to possess for your righteousness, for you are a stiff-necked people.

deuteronomy-9.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-10.summary: Moses recalls cutting two new tablets and making a wooden ark for them. The LORD wrote the ten commandments again, and Moses put them in the ark. Aaron died, and the tribe of Levi was set apart to carry the ark. The LORD listened to Moses and did not destroy Israel. Now the LORD asks Israel to fear him, love him, and keep his commands. He owns heaven and earth, yet he set his love on their fathers. He takes no bribes and gives justice to the fatherless and widow. He loves the foreigner, so Israel must love the foreigner too.

verse.text: Therefore love the foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.

deuteronomy-10.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-11.summary: Moses tells those who saw Egypt and the wilderness to love the LORD. The land ahead is not like Egypt, where they watered fields by foot. It is a land of hills and valleys that drinks rain from the sky. The LORD’s eyes are on it all year. If Israel obeys, he will send early and late rain. If they turn to other gods, he will shut the sky. They must teach these words to their children and write them on their doorposts. Moses sets a blessing and a curse before them, on Gerizim and Ebal.

verse.text: For the land, where you go in to possess isn’t like the land of Egypt that you came out of, where you sowed your seed and watered it with your foot, as a garden of herbs;

deuteronomy-11.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-12.summary: Israel must destroy the places where the nations served their gods. They must not worship the LORD that way, at every hill and tree. They are to bring offerings and tithes to the one place he will choose. There they eat and rejoice with sons, daughters, servants, and the Levite. They may kill and eat meat in any town, as they would a deer. But they must pour out the blood and not eat it. Holy gifts and vows still go to the chosen place. They must not copy the nations, who even burn their children for their gods.

verse.text: Yet you may kill and eat meat within all your gates, after all the desire of your soul, according to the LORD your God’s blessing which he has given you. The unclean and the clean may eat of it, as of the gazelle and the deer.

deuteronomy-12.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-13.summary: A prophet may give a sign that comes true and then urge other gods. Israel must not listen, because the LORD is testing their love. That prophet is to be put to death. If a brother, child, wife, or close friend secretly urges other gods, the same applies. The one who was urged must not hide it. If a town is said to have turned, the report must be checked with care. If it is true, the town is destroyed and burned. Nothing from it may be kept.

verse.text: you shall not listen to the words of that prophet, or to that dreamer of dreams; for the LORD your God is testing you, to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

deuteronomy-13.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-14.summary: Israel is the LORD’s children and must not cut themselves for the dead. They may eat cud-chewing animals with split hooves, and fish with fins and scales. Camels, hares, pigs, and many birds are forbidden. Each year they eat a tenth of their crops at the chosen place. If the way is far, they may bring money and buy food there. They must not forget the Levite. Every third year the tithe is stored in their own towns. The Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow come and eat their fill.

verse.text: The Levite, because he has no portion nor inheritance with you, as well as the foreigner living among you, the fatherless, and the widow who are within your gates shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied; that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hand which you do.

deuteronomy-14.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-15.summary: Every seven years a creditor must cancel what a fellow Israelite owes. If Israel obeys, there will be no poor among them. They must open their hand to a poor brother and lend what he needs. They must not refuse a loan because the year of release is near. They must give freely, because there will always be poor in the land. A Hebrew servant goes free in the seventh year. He must be sent away with gifts from flock, grain, and wine. Firstborn male animals belong to the LORD.

verse.text: Beware that there not be a wicked thought in your heart, saying, “The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand,” and your eye be evil against your poor brother and you give him nothing; and he cry to the LORD against you, and it be sin to you.

deuteronomy-15.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-16.summary: Israel keeps the Passover in the month of Abib, at the place the LORD chooses. They eat unleavened bread seven days, the bread of affliction. Seven weeks after harvest begins, they keep the feast of weeks with a free gift. They rejoice with children, servants, Levites, foreigners, the fatherless, and widows. They keep the feast of booths seven days after the harvest is in. Three times a year the men come before the LORD with a gift. Judges in every town must judge fairly and take no bribe. No sacred pole or pillar may stand by the LORD’s altar.

verse.text: You shall rejoice before the LORD your God: you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite who is within your gates, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow who are among you, in the place which the LORD your God shall choose to cause his name to dwell there.

deuteronomy-16.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-17.summary: No animal with a defect may be offered to the LORD. Serving other gods brings death, but only on two or three witnesses. Hard cases go to the priests and the judge at the chosen place. Their verdict must be followed. Israel may one day ask for a king like other nations. He must be an Israelite whom the LORD chooses. He must not collect many horses, wives, or much silver and gold. He must write his own copy of this law and read it all his life.

verse.text: Only he shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt, to the end that he may multiply horses; because the LORD has said to you, “You shall not go back that way again.”

deuteronomy-17.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-18.summary: The priests and Levites have no land, and the LORD is their inheritance. They receive set parts of sacrifices and the first of grain, wine, oil, and wool. A Levite from any town may come and serve at the chosen place. Israel must not copy the nations who burn children, tell fortunes, or consult the dead. The LORD will raise up a prophet like Moses from among them. Israel asked for this at Horeb, when they feared God’s voice. A prophet who speaks falsely in God’s name must die. If what a prophet says does not happen, the LORD did not say it.

verse.text: When a prophet speaks in the LORD’s name, if the thing doesn’t follow, nor happen, that is the thing which the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. You shall not be afraid of him.

deuteronomy-18.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-19.summary: Israel must set apart three cities in the land for anyone who kills by accident. An example is an ax head that flies off and strikes a neighbor. The cities keep the avenger from killing him in hot anger. If the land grows, three more cities are added. A man who kills from hatred is handed over to die. No one may move a neighbor’s boundary stone. A charge needs two or three witnesses, not one. A false witness receives the penalty he meant for the other person.

verse.text: One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin that he sins. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall a matter be established.

deuteronomy-19.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-20.summary: Before battle a priest tells the army the LORD fights for them. Officers send home men with a new house, vineyard, or bride. They also send home anyone who is afraid. A distant city must first be offered peace. If it refuses, its men are killed and the rest are taken. Cities of the land itself must be destroyed, to keep Israel from their gods. During a long siege Israel must not cut down fruit trees. Only trees that give no food may be used for siege works.

verse.text: When you shall besiege a city a long time, in making war against it to take it, you shall not destroy its trees by wielding an ax against them; for you may eat of them. You shall not cut them down, for is the tree of the field man, that it should be besieged by you?

deuteronomy-20.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-21.summary: When a slain body is found and no killer is known, the nearest elders act. They break a heifer’s neck, wash their hands, and ask the LORD’s forgiveness. A soldier who marries a captive woman must first give her a month to mourn. If he later sends her away, he may not sell her. A man with two wives must give the firstborn’s double share to the true firstborn. He may not favor the son of the wife he loves. Parents may bring a stubborn, rebellious son to the elders, and he is stoned. A hanged body must be buried the same day.

verse.text: but he shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the hated, by giving him a double portion of all that he has; for he is the beginning of his strength. The right of the firstborn is his.

deuteronomy-21.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-22.summary: Anyone who finds a neighbor’s stray animal or lost item must return it. A fallen animal must be helped up. A mother bird must be let go when the young are taken. A new house needs a railing around its roof so no one falls. Seeds, plow animals, and cloth types must not be mixed. A husband who falsely accuses his bride is fined, and a guilty bride is stoned. Adultery brings death for both. A woman forced in the open country is not guilty, and only the man dies.

verse.text: When you build a new house, then you shall make a railing around your roof, so that you don’t bring blood on your house if anyone falls from there.

deuteronomy-22.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-23.summary: Some people may not enter the LORD’s assembly. Ammonites and Moabites are barred, because they refused bread and hired Balaam. Edomites and Egyptians are not to be hated, and their third generation may enter. The army camp must be kept clean, because the LORD walks in it. An escaped servant must not be handed back to his master. He may live where he chooses and must not be oppressed. Israel must not charge a brother interest and must pay its vows. A person may eat in a neighbor’s field but not carry food away.

verse.text: You shall not deliver to his master a servant who has escaped from his master to you.

deuteronomy-23.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-24.summary: A man who divorces his wife gives her a written certificate. If she remarries and is free again, the first husband may not take her back. A newly married man stays home from war for a year. No one may take a millstone as a pledge, because it is a person’s living. A lender waits outside for a pledge and returns a poor man’s cloak by sunset. A hired worker must be paid the same day. Each person dies for his own sin, not a parent’s or child’s. Forgotten sheaves, olives, and grapes are left for foreigners, the fatherless, and widows.

verse.text: In his day you shall give him his wages, neither shall the sun go down on it, for he is poor and sets his heart on it, lest he cry against you to the LORD, and it be sin to you.

deuteronomy-24.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-25.summary: Judges must clear the innocent and condemn the guilty. A beating may not go past forty strokes, so the person is not degraded. An ox must not be muzzled while it treads grain. If a man dies without a son, his brother should marry the widow. If the brother refuses, she removes his sandal before the elders. Israel must not keep two sets of weights or measures. Weights and measures must be full and fair. Israel must remember how Amalek attacked the weak at the rear.

verse.text: You shall have a perfect and just weight. You shall have a perfect and just measure, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.

deuteronomy-25.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-26.summary: In the land, each Israelite brings a basket of first fruits to the priest. He says that he has come to the land the LORD swore to give. He says his father was a Syrian near death who went to Egypt. Egypt made them slaves, and the LORD heard their cry and brought them out. Now he brings the first of what the LORD gave. He rejoices with the Levite and the foreigner. In the third year he gives the tithe to the Levite, foreigner, fatherless, and widow. Israel declares the LORD is its God, and the LORD declares Israel his own people.

verse.text: You shall answer and say before the LORD your God, “My father was a Syrian ready to perish. He went down into Egypt, and lived there, few in number. There he became a great, mighty, and populous nation.

deuteronomy-26.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-27.summary: After crossing the Jordan, the people must set up large plastered stones. They must write the law on them plainly, on Mount Ebal. They build an altar there of uncut stones. Six tribes stand on Gerizim to bless and six on Ebal for the curse. The Levites call out twelve curses in a loud voice. The curses name secret idols, dishonoring parents, and moving a boundary stone. They name misleading the blind, denying justice to the weak, and secret killing. After each one, all the people answer, “Amen.”

verse.text: ‘Cursed is he who leads the blind astray on the road.’ All the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

deuteronomy-27.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-28.summary: If Israel listens to the LORD, blessings will overtake them. They will be blessed in city and field, in children, crops, and herds. The LORD will send rain, and they will lend and not borrow. If they do not listen, curses will overtake them. They will suffer sickness, drought, defeat, and loss of all they work for. A far nation whose language they do not know will besiege their towns. They will be scattered among the nations and find no rest. They will even be offered as slaves in Egypt, and no one will buy them.

verse.text: Because you didn’t serve the LORD your God with joyfulness and with gladness of heart, by reason of the abundance of all things;

deuteronomy-28.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-29.summary: Moses gathers all Israel in Moab for a covenant beyond the one at Horeb. He recalls Egypt and forty years when their clothes did not wear out. Everyone stands before the LORD: leaders, men, children, wives, and foreigners. Even the woodcutter and the water carrier are there. The covenant is also made with those not present that day. No one who turns to other gods in secret will be pardoned. Later nations will ask why the land was ruined and hear the reason. Secret things belong to the LORD, and revealed things to Israel and its children.

verse.text: your little ones, your wives, and the foreigners who are in the middle of your camps, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water,

deuteronomy-29.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-30.summary: When scattered Israel returns to the LORD, he will gather them. He will bring them back from the farthest places. He will change their hearts so they love him and live. The command is not too hard or too far away. It is not in heaven or across the sea. The word is very near, in their mouth and heart. Moses sets life and death, blessing and curse, before them. He tells them to choose life by loving the LORD and holding to him.

verse.text: But the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do it.

deuteronomy-30.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-31.summary: Moses is 120 and tells Israel he will not cross the Jordan. The LORD and Joshua will go before them, so they must be strong. Moses writes the law and gives it to the priests and elders. Every seven years, at the feast of booths, it must be read to everyone. Men, women, children, and foreigners are to hear and learn. The LORD tells Moses the people will turn to other gods after his death. Moses writes a song to stand as a witness against them. The book of the law is placed beside the ark.

verse.text: and that their children, who have not known, may hear and learn to fear the LORD your God, as long as you live in the land where you go over the Jordan to possess it.”

deuteronomy-31.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-32.summary: Moses sings a song and calls heaven and earth to listen. He calls God the Rock, whose work is perfect and whose ways are just. God found Israel in a desert and carried it as an eagle does. He fed Israel with honey and oil from the rock. But Israel grew fat, kicked, and left the God who made it. It turned to strange gods, so God hid his face. Yet he will judge his people and have compassion when their strength is gone. The LORD then tells Moses to climb Mount Nebo, see the land, and die there.

verse.text: But Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked. You have grown fat. You have grown thick. You have become sleek. Then he abandoned God who made him, and rejected the Rock of his salvation.

deuteronomy-32.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-33.summary: Before he dies, Moses blesses the tribes of Israel. He says the LORD came from Sinai and loves the people. Moses gave them a law as the inheritance of all Jacob. He asks that Reuben live and that the LORD hear Judah. Levi keeps the Urim and Thummim and teaches the law. Benjamin rests in safety, and Joseph’s land is blessed with dew and deep water. Zebulun, Issachar, Gad, Dan, Naphtali, and Asher each get a saying. Moses ends: no one is like God, and Israel is saved by the LORD.

verse.text: Moses commanded us a law, an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.

deuteronomy-33.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

deuteronomy-34.summary: Moses climbs Mount Nebo, and the LORD shows him the whole land. The LORD says this is the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses may see it but not cross over. Moses dies there in Moab, and no one knows his tomb. He was 120, with clear eyes and full strength. Israel weeps for him thirty days. Joshua is full of the spirit of wisdom, because Moses laid hands on him. No prophet like Moses has risen since, whom the LORD knew face to face.

verse.text: Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him. The children of Israel listened to him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses.

deuteronomy-34.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-1.summary: After Moses dies, the LORD tells Joshua to lead Israel across the Jordan. He promises to give them every place their feet tread. He says he will be with Joshua as he was with Moses. He tells Joshua three times to be strong and courageous. Joshua must keep the law and think on it day and night. Joshua tells the officers to prepare to cross in three days. He reminds Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh to fight beside their brothers. They promise to obey him as they obeyed Moses.

verse.text: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.

joshua-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-2.summary: Joshua secretly sends two spies to Jericho. They stay in the house of Rahab, a prostitute. The king sends for them, and Rahab hides them under flax on her roof. She tells the king’s men that the spies already left. She tells the spies the LORD has given Israel the land. She asks them to spare her family, and they swear to it. She lets them down by a cord from her window in the city wall. She must tie a scarlet cord there and keep her family inside.

verse.text: As soon as we had heard it, our hearts melted, and there wasn’t any more spirit in any man, because of you: for the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath.

joshua-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-3.summary: Israel camps at the Jordan for three days. The officers tell the people to follow the ark at a distance. Joshua tells them to make themselves ready for the LORD’s wonders. The LORD says he will make Joshua great, as he was with Moses. The priests carry the ark to the river, which is in flood at harvest. When their feet touch the water, the river stops and piles up far upstream. The priests stand on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. All Israel crosses over near Jericho.

verse.text: It shall be that when the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of GOD, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan will be cut off. The waters that come down from above shall stand in one heap.”

joshua-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-4.summary: After the crossing, the LORD tells Joshua to choose twelve men, one from each tribe. Each carries a stone from the riverbed where the priests stood. Joshua also sets up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan. About forty thousand armed men cross toward Jericho. That day the people honor Joshua as they had honored Moses. When the priests come out, the river returns and overflows its banks. Israel camps at Gilgal, and Joshua sets up the twelve stones there. The stones are for children who will ask what they mean.

verse.text: that this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask in the future, saying, ‘What do you mean by these stones?’

joshua-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-5.summary: The kings of the land hear about the Jordan and lose heart. The LORD tells Joshua to circumcise the men born in the wilderness. The older generation had died there for not listening. The LORD says he has rolled away Egypt’s reproach, and the place is named Gilgal. Israel keeps the Passover in the plains of Jericho. They eat the produce of the land, and the manna stops. Near Jericho Joshua meets a man with a drawn sword. He is commander of the LORD’s army, and Joshua bows and removes his sandals.

verse.text: He said, “No; but I have come now as commander of the LORD’s army.” Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and worshiped, and asked him, “What does my lord say to his servant?”

joshua-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-6.summary: Jericho is shut tight. The LORD tells Joshua to march around it once a day for six days. Seven priests carry ram’s horn trumpets before the ark. On day seven they circle seven times and shout, and the wall falls flat. Israel destroys everyone in the city, young and old, and the animals. The two spies bring out Rahab and her whole family. The city is burned, and its metals go to the LORD’s treasury. Rahab lives in Israel from then on, and Joshua curses anyone who rebuilds Jericho.

verse.text: But Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and all that she had, Joshua saved alive. She lives in the middle of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

joshua-6.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-7.summary: Achan of Judah secretly takes some of the goods devoted to the LORD. Israel sends about three thousand men against Ai, and they are driven back. Thirty-six die, and the people lose heart. Joshua falls before the ark and asks why God brought them over the Jordan. The LORD says Israel has sinned and stolen devoted things. The next morning Judah is singled out, then a family, then Achan. Achan confesses that he hid a robe, silver, and gold under his tent. Israel stones him and his household in the valley of Achor.

verse.text: When I saw among the plunder a beautiful Babylonian robe, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels, then I coveted them and took them. Behold, they are hidden in the ground in the middle of my tent, with the silver under it.”

routes.title: Men go up from Jericho to Ai

joshua-7.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-8.summary: The LORD tells Joshua not to fear and to set an ambush behind Ai. Joshua hides men west of the city and camps the rest to the north. Israel pretends to flee, and every man of Ai chases them. Joshua stretches out his javelin, and the hidden men take and burn the city. Twelve thousand people of Ai die, and its king is hanged. Israel keeps the livestock and goods this time. Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal and writes the law on stones. He reads every word to all Israel, with the women, children, and foreigners.

verse.text: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua didn’t read before all the assembly of Israel, with the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who were among them.

joshua-8.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-9.summary: The kings west of the Jordan join to fight Israel. The people of Gibeon choose a trick. They come with worn sacks, patched sandals, and moldy bread, and claim a far country. Israel’s men taste their food and do not ask the LORD. Joshua makes a covenant to let them live, and the leaders swear to it. Three days later Israel learns that they live nearby. The people grumble, but the leaders will not break an oath sworn by the LORD. The Gibeonites become woodcutters and water carriers for the altar.

verse.text: Joshua made peace with them, and made a covenant with them, to let them live. The princes of the congregation swore to them.

joshua-9.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-10.summary: Five Amorite kings, led by Jerusalem’s king, attack Gibeon for making peace with Israel. Gibeon begs Joshua not to abandon it. Joshua marches all night from Gilgal and surprises them. The LORD throws them into confusion and sends great hailstones. Joshua asks for the sun and moon to stand still, and they do. The five kings hide in a cave at Makkedah and are later put to death. Joshua takes Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron, and Debir. He holds the southern land because the LORD fought for Israel.

verse.text: The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, “Don’t abandon your servants! Come up to us quickly and save us! Help us; for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the hill country have gathered together against us.”

joshua-10.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-11.summary: Jabin king of Hazor gathers the northern kings with horses and chariots. Their army is like the sand of the seashore. The LORD tells Joshua not to fear. Joshua attacks suddenly at the waters of Merom and wins. He cripples their horses and burns their chariots, as the LORD said. He burns Hazor, the leading city, but not the other cities on their mounds. The war with these kings lasts a long time. Joshua takes the whole land, and the land rests from war.

verse.text: Joshua made war a long time with all those kings.

joshua-11.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-12.summary: This chapter lists the kings Israel defeated. East of the Jordan, Moses defeated Sihon of Heshbon and Og of Bashan. Their land went to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. West of the Jordan, Joshua defeated kings from the hill country to the lowland. The list names each city’s king and counts “one” after each. It begins with Jericho and Ai. It includes Jerusalem, Hebron, Lachish, Hazor, and Megiddo. The total is thirty-one kings.

verse.text: the king of Tirzah, one: all the kings thirty-one.

joshua-12.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-13.summary: Joshua is old, and the LORD says much land remains to be taken. The Philistine regions, the Geshurites, and lands toward Lebanon are still unconquered. The LORD promises to drive those peoples out. Joshua must divide the western land among nine and a half tribes. The chapter then reviews the eastern land Moses gave. Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh each receive their towns there. Israel did not drive out the Geshurites and Maacathites. Levi receives no land, because the LORD is their inheritance.

verse.text: Now Joshua was old and well advanced in years. The LORD said to him, “You are old and advanced in years, and there remains yet very much land to be possessed.

joshua-13.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-14.summary: Eleazar, Joshua, and the tribal heads divide Canaan by lot. Caleb of Judah comes to Joshua at Gilgal. He recalls spying out the land at age forty and giving an honest report. Moses swore that the land he walked on would be his. Caleb is now eighty-five and says he is as strong as ever. He asks for the hill country where the Anakim live in walled cities. Joshua blesses him and gives him Hebron. Then the land rests from war.

verse.text: Now therefore give me this hill country, of which the LORD spoke in that day; for you heard in that day how the Anakim were there, and great and fortified cities. It may be that the LORD will be with me, and I shall drive them out, as the LORD said.”

joshua-14.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-15.summary: Judah’s land is described by its borders, from the Salt Sea to the Great Sea. Caleb receives Hebron and drives out three sons of Anak. He offers his daughter Achsah to whoever takes Debir. Othniel takes the city and marries her. Achsah asks her father for springs of water to go with her dry land. Caleb gives her the upper and lower springs. Judah’s towns are then listed by region. Judah could not drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem.

verse.text: She said, “Give me a blessing. Because you have set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water.” So he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

joshua-15.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-16.summary: The lot for Joseph’s sons starts at the Jordan near Jericho. It runs through Bethel toward Beth Horon and ends at the sea. Manasseh and Ephraim take their inheritance. Ephraim’s border is traced from Ataroth to the brook of Kanah. Ephraim also has towns set inside Manasseh’s land. They did not drive out the Canaanites of Gezer. Those Canaanites live among Ephraim and do forced labor.

verse.text: They didn’t drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer; but the Canaanites dwell in the territory of Ephraim to this day, and have become servants to do forced labor.

joshua-16.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-17.summary: Manasseh, Joseph’s firstborn, receives land on both sides of the Jordan. Zelophehad’s five daughters come to Eleazar, Joshua, and the leaders. They say the LORD commanded Moses to give them an inheritance. They receive land among their father’s brothers. Manasseh could not drive out the Canaanites and later forced them to work. Joseph’s people complain that one share is too small. Joshua tells them to clear the forest in the hill country. He says they can drive out the Canaanites despite their iron chariots.

verse.text: They came to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the princes, saying, “The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.” Therefore according to the commandment of the LORD he gave them an inheritance among the brothers of their father.

joshua-17.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-18.summary: All Israel gathers at Shiloh and sets up the Tent of Meeting. Seven tribes still have no land. Joshua asks how long they will put off taking it. Three men from each tribe walk the land and write it up in seven parts. Joshua casts lots for them before the LORD at Shiloh. The first lot is Benjamin’s, between Judah and Joseph. Its borders and towns are listed. Its towns include Jericho, Bethel, Gibeon, and Jerusalem.

verse.text: The men arose and went. Joshua commanded those who went to survey the land, saying, “Go walk through the land, survey it, and come again to me. I will cast lots for you here before the LORD in Shiloh.”

joshua-18.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-19.summary: Simeon’s share lies inside Judah’s, because Judah’s part was too large. Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali receive their borders and towns. Dan’s share is listed last. Dan’s people also go north and take the town of Leshem. When all the tribes have land, Israel gives Joshua a share. He asks for Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He builds up the town and lives there. The division is finished at Shiloh, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

verse.text: So they finished distributing the land for inheritance by its borders. The children of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun among them.

joshua-19.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-20.summary: The LORD tells Joshua to set up the cities of refuge. A person who kills by accident may flee to one. He states his case to the elders at the city gate. They take him in and give him a place to live. They must not hand him over to the avenger of blood. He stays until he stands trial and until the high priest dies. Three cities are west of the Jordan: Kedesh, Shechem, and Hebron. Three are east: Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan.

verse.text: If the avenger of blood pursues him, then they shall not deliver up the man slayer into his hand; because he struck his neighbor unintentionally, and didn’t hate him before.

joshua-20.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-21.summary: The Levite leaders come to Eleazar and Joshua at Shiloh. They recall that the LORD commanded towns and pasture for them. Each tribe gives towns from its own land. Aaron’s family receives thirteen towns in Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. The other Kohathites, the Gershonites, and the Merarites receive theirs by lot. In all the Levites receive forty-eight towns with pasture. The LORD gives Israel the land and rest on every side. Not one good promise of the LORD has failed.

verse.text: The children of Israel gave to the Levites out of their inheritance, according to the commandment of the LORD, these cities with their pasture lands.

joshua-21.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-22.summary: Joshua thanks Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh and sends them home. Near the Jordan they build a large altar. The other tribes hear of it and gather at Shiloh for war. First they send Phinehas and ten leaders to ask what it means. They fear another sin like Peor or Achan’s. The eastern tribes say the altar is not for sacrifice. It is a witness that their children also belong to the LORD. Phinehas is satisfied, and the war is called off.

verse.text: but it will be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may perform the service of the LORD before him with our burnt offerings, with our sacrifices, and with our peace offerings;’ that your children may not tell our children in time to come, ‘You have no portion in the LORD.’

joshua-22.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-23.summary: Years later Joshua is old and calls Israel’s leaders together. He reminds them that the LORD fought for them. Nations still remain in the land, and the LORD will drive them out. Israel must keep the law of Moses and hold fast to the LORD. They must not serve the gods of those nations or marry among them. If they do, the LORD will stop driving the nations out. Those nations will become a snare, a whip, and thorns. As every good promise came true, so will the warnings.

verse.text: know for a certainty that the LORD your God will no longer drive these nations from out of your sight; but they shall be a snare and a trap to you, a scourge in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from off this good land which the LORD your God has given you.

joshua-23.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

joshua-24.summary: Joshua gathers all the tribes at Shechem. He speaks for the LORD and retells the story from Abraham to the conquest. Their fathers served other gods beyond the River. The LORD brought them from Egypt and gave them land they did not work. Joshua tells them to choose whom they will serve. He says he and his house will serve the LORD. The people promise three times, and Joshua sets up a stone as a witness. Joshua dies at 110, and Joseph’s bones are buried at Shechem.

verse.text: If it seems evil to you to serve the LORD, choose today whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.”

joshua-24.dateNote: The Church chronology gives the order of these events, not their years.

judges-1.summary: After Joshua dies, Israel asks the LORD who should fight first. Judah goes up with Simeon and defeats Adoni-Bezek. Caleb’s daughter Achsah again receives her springs. Judah takes the hill country but cannot drive out the plain’s iron chariots. Benjamin does not drive the Jebusites from Jerusalem. Joseph’s house takes Bethel with help from a man of the city. Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, and Naphtali leave Canaanites in their towns. When Israel grows strong, it puts them to forced labor.

verse.text: When Israel had grown strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, and didn’t utterly drive them out.

judges-1.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-2.summary: The LORD’s angel comes to Bochim and says Israel has not obeyed. So the nations will stay as thorns and their gods as a snare. The people weep. The account then looks back: Israel served the LORD while Joshua and the elders lived. A new generation arose that did not know the LORD or his works. They served the Baals, and the LORD gave them to raiders. He raised up judges to save them, but after each judge they turned back. So the LORD left the nations to test Israel.

verse.text: After all that generation were gathered to their fathers, another generation arose after them who didn’t know the LORD, nor the work which he had done for Israel.

judges-2.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-3.summary: The LORD leaves several nations to test Israel. Israel marries among them and serves their gods. A king of Mesopotamia rules them eight years, and Othniel, of Caleb’s family, saves them. Then Eglon king of Moab rules Israel eighteen years. The LORD raises up Ehud, a left-handed man of Benjamin. Ehud hides a sword on his right thigh and kills Eglon in private. He escapes, calls Israel to fight, and Moab is subdued. Shamgar later kills six hundred Philistines with an ox goad.

verse.text: But when the children of Israel cried to the LORD, the LORD raised up a savior for them: Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. The children of Israel sent tribute by him to Eglon the king of Moab.

judges-3.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-4.summary: Israel does evil again, and Jabin king of Canaan oppresses them twenty years. His general Sisera has nine hundred iron chariots. Deborah, a prophetess, judges Israel under a palm tree. She tells Barak that the LORD commands him to gather ten thousand men. Barak will go only if she goes with him. She agrees but says a woman will get the honor. The LORD routs Sisera’s army, and Sisera flees on foot to Jael’s tent. Jael gives him milk and kills him with a tent peg as he sleeps.

verse.text: She said, “I will surely go with you. Nevertheless, the journey that you take won’t be for your honor; for the LORD will sell Sisera into a woman’s hand.” Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.

judges-4.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-5.summary: Deborah and Barak sing after the victory. They praise leaders and people who offered themselves willingly. The song recalls empty roads and villages before Deborah arose. It praises the tribes that came: Ephraim, Benjamin, Zebulun, Issachar, and Naphtali. It asks why Reuben, Gilead, Dan, and Asher stayed home. The stars and the river Kishon fought against Sisera. Jael is called most blessed of women for killing him. The song ends with Sisera’s mother waiting at her window for him.

verse.text: Gilead lived beyond the Jordan. Why did Dan remain in ships? Asher sat still at the haven of the sea, and lived by his creeks.

judges-5.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-6.summary: Midian raids Israel for seven years and strips the land at harvest. Israel cries out, and a prophet reminds them they did not listen. The LORD’s angel finds Gideon threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it. He calls Gideon a mighty man and sends him to save Israel. Gideon says his family is the poorest and he is the least. At night he tears down his father’s altar to Baal. His father Joash tells the angry town to let Baal defend himself. Gideon gathers an army and twice asks for a sign with a fleece.

verse.text: Joash said to all who stood against him, “Will you contend for Baal? Or will you save him? He who will contend for him, let him be put to death by morning! If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because someone has broken down his altar!”

judges-6.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-7.summary: Gideon camps with thirty-two thousand men. The LORD says they are too many, or Israel will boast that it saved itself. The fearful go home, and ten thousand remain. At the water the LORD keeps only the three hundred who lap from their hands. Gideon sneaks to the enemy camp and hears a man tell a dream of defeat. He gives each man a trumpet, a jar, and a torch. At night they blow, break the jars, and shout. The Midianites turn on each other and flee.

verse.text: The LORD said to Gideon, “The people who are with you are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hand, lest Israel brag against me, saying, ‘My own hand has saved me.’

judges-7.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-8.summary: Ephraim complains at being called late, and Gideon calms them with praise. He chases two Midianite kings across the Jordan with his tired three hundred. Succoth and Penuel refuse him bread. He captures the kings, then punishes Succoth’s elders and kills the men of Penuel. He kills the two kings for the death of his brothers. Israel asks him to rule, and he says the LORD will rule. But he collects gold earrings and makes an ephod that Israel worships. After his death Israel turns to the Baals and forgets his family.

verse.text: Gideon made an ephod out of it, and put it in Ophrah, his city. Then all Israel played the prostitute with it there; and it became a snare to Gideon and to his house.

judges-8.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-9.summary: Abimelech, Gideon’s son by a woman of Shechem, asks Shechem to make him ruler. They give him silver, and he hires men and kills his seventy brothers.
