Only the youngest, Jotham, escapes. Jotham shouts a story from Mount Gerizim about trees choosing a king. The olive, fig, and vine refuse, and the bramble accepts. Three years later Shechem turns against Abimelech. He destroys the city and burns its tower with the people inside. At Thebez a woman drops a millstone on his head, and he dies.

verse.text: “The bramble said to the trees, ‘If in truth you anoint me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.’

judges-9.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-10.summary: Tola judges Israel twenty-three years, and Jair twenty-two. Israel again serves the gods of the nations around it. The LORD gives them to the Philistines and Ammonites for eighteen years. Israel cries out and admits its sin. The LORD lists his past rescues and says he will save them no more. He tells them to cry to the gods they chose. Israel confesses again, puts away the foreign gods, and serves the LORD. He can bear their misery no longer, and Ammon gathers for war.

verse.text: Go and cry to the gods which you have chosen. Let them save you in the time of your distress!”

judges-10.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-11.summary: Jephthah is a strong fighter, but his brothers drive him out as a prostitute’s son. When Ammon attacks, the elders of Gilead ask him to lead them. He agrees on condition that he stay their head. He sends Ammon’s king a long case from history that Israel took no Ammonite land. The king does not listen. Jephthah vows to offer whatever first comes from his house if he wins. He wins, and his only daughter comes out dancing to meet him. She asks two months to mourn, and he does to her as he vowed.

verse.text: When he saw her, he tore his clothes, and said, “Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you are one of those who trouble me; for I have opened my mouth to the LORD, and I can’t go back.”

judges-11.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-12.summary: The men of Ephraim are angry that Jephthah fought Ammon without them. They threaten to burn his house. Jephthah says he called and they did not come. Gilead fights Ephraim and takes the Jordan crossings. Each fleeing man is told to say “Shibboleth.” An Ephraimite says “Sibboleth” and is killed. Forty-two thousand of Ephraim die. Jephthah judges six years, and Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon follow him.

verse.text: then they said to him, “Now say ‘Shibboleth;’ ” and he said “Sibboleth”; for he couldn’t manage to pronounce it correctly, then they seized him and killed him at the fords of the Jordan. At that time, forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell.

judges-12.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-13.summary: Israel does evil, and the Philistines rule them forty years. The LORD’s angel appears to the childless wife of Manoah of Dan. She will bear a son who must be a Nazirite from birth. She must drink no wine, and no razor may touch his head. Manoah prays for the man to return, and the angel comes again to the woman. Manoah offers a goat, and the angel goes up in the altar flame. Manoah fears they will die for seeing God. His wife says God would not accept their offering and then kill them.

verse.text: But his wife said to him, “If the LORD were pleased to kill us, he wouldn’t have received a burnt offering and a meal offering at our hand, and he wouldn’t have shown us all these things, nor would he have told us such things as these at this time.”

judges-13.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-14.summary: Samson sees a Philistine woman in Timnah and demands her as his wife. His parents object, not knowing the LORD is seeking an occasion against the Philistines. On the way Samson tears a young lion apart with his hands. Later he finds honey in its carcass and eats it. At his wedding feast he bets thirty guests they cannot solve his riddle. They threaten to burn his wife and her father’s house unless she gets the answer. She weeps until Samson tells her, and she tells them. Samson kills thirty men to pay the bet, and his wife is given away.

verse.text: On the seventh day, they said to Samson’s wife, “Entice your husband, that he may declare to us the riddle, lest we burn you and your father’s house with fire. Have you called us to impoverish us? Isn’t that so?”

judges-14.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-15.summary: Samson returns for his wife and learns she was given to another man. He ties torches to three hundred foxes and burns the Philistines’ grain. The Philistines burn his wife and her father. Samson strikes them down and hides in a rock cleft. Three thousand men of Judah come to hand him over. He lets them bind him, then snaps the ropes when the Spirit comes on him. He kills a thousand men with a donkey’s jawbone. He is thirsty and calls on the LORD, and God opens a spring.

verse.text: Then the Philistines said, “Who has done this?” They said, “Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he has taken his wife and given her to his companion.” The Philistines came up, and burned her and her father with fire.

judges-15.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-16.summary: Samson visits a prostitute in Gaza and carries off the city gates at midnight. He loves Delilah, and Philistine lords pay her to learn his secret. Three times he lies to her, and each time she tests it. She presses him daily until he tells her about his uncut hair. She has his head shaved while he sleeps, and the LORD leaves him. The Philistines blind him and make him grind grain in prison. At a feast for their god Dagon they bring him out for sport. He prays, pushes down the two pillars, and dies with them.

verse.text: Samson called to the LORD, and said, “Lord GOD, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, only this once, God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.”

judges-16.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-17.summary: Micah of Ephraim admits he took his mother’s eleven hundred pieces of silver. She blesses him and has part of it made into an idol. Micah has a shrine, an ephod, and household gods, and makes a son his priest. In those days Israel had no king, and everyone did what seemed right. A young Levite from Bethlehem comes looking for a place. Micah hires him for ten pieces of silver a year, clothes, and food. The Levite becomes his priest. Micah says the LORD will surely do him good now.

verse.text: Then Micah said, “Now I know that the LORD will do good to me, since I have a Levite as my priest.”

judges-17.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-18.summary: The tribe of Dan is looking for land. Five scouts stay at Micah’s house and ask his Levite for a word from God. They find Laish, a quiet town with no defender. Six hundred armed Danites set out. On the way they take Micah’s idol, ephod, and gods, and invite the priest along. The priest is glad to serve a tribe in place of one man. Micah chases them and is warned off. Dan burns Laish, kills its people, renames it Dan, and sets up the idol.

verse.text: He said, “You have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and have gone away! What more do I have? How can you ask me, ‘What ails you?’ ”

judges-18.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-19.summary: A Levite’s concubine leaves him and returns to her father in Bethlehem. He goes to bring her back and is kept there for days. On the way home they pass a foreign town and reach Gibeah of Benjamin. Only an old man takes them in. Men of the city surround the house and demand the Levite. He pushes his concubine out to them, and they abuse her all night. In the morning she lies dead at the door. He cuts her body into twelve pieces and sends them through Israel.

verse.text: It was so, that all who saw it said, “Such a deed has not been done or seen from the day that the children of Israel came up out of the land of Egypt to this day! Consider it, take counsel, and speak.”

judges-19.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-20.summary: All Israel gathers at Mizpah, four hundred thousand armed men. The Levite tells what Gibeah did but leaves out his own part. The tribes demand that Benjamin hand over the guilty men. Benjamin refuses and gathers its army. Israel asks God who should go first and loses twenty-two thousand men. They weep, ask again, and lose eighteen thousand more. After fasting and offerings, they set an ambush and win on the third day. Benjamin loses twenty-five thousand men, and only six hundred escape.

verse.text: Behold, you children of Israel, all of you, give here your advice and counsel.”

routes.title: Benjamin flees to the rock of Rimmon

judges-20.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

judges-21.summary: Israel had sworn not to give daughters to Benjamin. Now the people weep that a tribe is nearly gone. Six hundred Benjamite men survive and need wives. Israel finds that Jabesh Gilead sent no one to the assembly. They kill its people and take four hundred young women for Benjamin. That is not enough. The elders tell the remaining men to seize dancers at the Shiloh feast. The book ends: there was no king, and everyone did what seemed right.

verse.text: It shall be, when their fathers or their brothers come to complain to us, that we will say to them, ‘Grant them graciously to us, because we didn’t take for each man his wife in battle, neither did you give them to them; otherwise you would now be guilty.’ ”

judges-21.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

ruth-1.summary: In the days of the judges a famine strikes Bethlehem. Elimelech takes his wife Naomi and two sons to Moab. He dies, and the sons marry Moabite women, Orpah and Ruth. After about ten years both sons die. Naomi hears there is food in Judah and starts home. She tells her daughters-in-law to go back to their mothers. Orpah leaves, but Ruth promises to share Naomi’s people, God, and grave. They reach Bethlehem at the start of the barley harvest.

verse.text: She said to them, “Don’t call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.

routes.title: Loss and the return to Bethlehem

ruth-1.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

ruth-2.summary: Ruth asks Naomi to let her gather leftover grain behind the harvesters. She happens to come to the field of Boaz, a relative of Elimelech. Boaz asks who she is, and the foreman reports her request and steady work. Boaz tells her to stay in his field and drink from his water. He has heard what she did for Naomi. He shares his meal and tells his men to leave extra stalks for her. Ruth carries home a large measure of barley. Naomi blesses Boaz and says he is a close relative.

verse.text: She said, ‘Please let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves.’ So she came, and has continued even from the morning until now, except that she rested a little in the house.”

ruth-2.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

ruth-3.summary: Naomi wants a secure home for Ruth. She sends her to the threshing floor where Boaz winnows barley at night. Ruth washes, dresses, and waits until he has eaten and lies down. She uncovers his feet and lies there. At midnight he wakes and asks who she is. She asks him to spread his garment over her as a near kinsman. Boaz blesses her and promises to act, but a nearer kinsman has first right. He sends her home before dawn with six measures of barley.

verse.text: He said, “Who are you?” She answered, “I am Ruth your servant. Therefore spread the corner of your garment over your servant; for you are a near kinsman.”

ruth-3.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

ruth-4.summary: Boaz sits at the town gate and stops the nearer kinsman. He gathers ten elders as witnesses. He says Naomi is selling Elimelech’s field, and the man agrees to buy it. Boaz adds that the buyer must marry Ruth and raise an heir for the dead. The man withdraws and hands over his sandal to confirm it. Boaz declares that he has bought the land and taken Ruth as his wife. Ruth bears Obed, and the women tell Naomi her life is restored. Obed becomes the grandfather of David.

verse.text: Boaz said to the elders and to all the people, “You are witnesses today, that I have bought all that was Elimelech’s, and all that was Chilion’s and Mahlon’s, from the hand of Naomi.

ruth-4.dateNote: The Church chronology calls the dates of the judges very uncertain.

1-samuel-1.summary: Elkanah has two wives, and Hannah has no children. Each year at Shiloh the other wife taunts her until she weeps. Hannah prays in bitter grief and vows to give a son to the LORD. Eli the priest sees her lips move and thinks she is drunk. She explains, and he sends her away with a blessing. She bears a son and names him Samuel. When he is weaned she brings him to Eli at Shiloh. She gives him to the LORD for his whole life.

verse.text: Don’t consider your servant a wicked woman; for I have been speaking out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation.”

1-samuel-1.dateNote: The Church chronology gives no year before Saul's reign.

1-samuel-2.summary: Hannah sings that the LORD brings down the strong and lifts the poor. Eli’s sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are priests who do not know the LORD. They take the best meat by force before the fat is burned. They also sleep with women who serve at the tent door. Eli rebukes them, but they do not listen. Meanwhile the boy Samuel grows and serves before the LORD. A man of God tells Eli that his house will lose the priesthood. Both sons will die on one day.

verse.text: Why do you kick at my sacrifice and at my offering, which I have commanded in my habitation, and honor your sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the best of all the offerings of Israel my people?’

1-samuel-2.dateNote: The Church chronology gives no year before Saul's reign.

1-samuel-3.summary: The boy Samuel serves under Eli, and words from the LORD are rare. One night a voice calls Samuel, and he runs to Eli. This happens three times before Eli understands. He tells Samuel to answer, “Speak, LORD, for your servant hears.” The LORD says he will judge Eli’s house for the sons’ sin. Eli knew and did not restrain them. In the morning Samuel is afraid, but Eli makes him tell everything. All Israel learns that Samuel is a prophet.

verse.text: Samuel told him every bit, and hid nothing from him. He said, “It is the LORD. Let him do what seems good to him.”

1-samuel-3.dateNote: The Church chronology gives no year before Saul's reign.

1-samuel-4.summary: Israel fights the Philistines and loses four thousand men. The elders send to Shiloh for the ark of the covenant. Hophni and Phinehas come with it, and the camp shouts. The Philistines are afraid but urge each other to fight like men. Israel loses thirty thousand men, the ark is captured, and Eli’s sons die. A runner brings the news to Shiloh. Eli falls from his seat and dies when he hears about the ark. His daughter-in-law dies in childbirth and names her son Ichabod.

verse.text: When the people had come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let’s get the ark of the LORD’s covenant out of Shiloh and bring it to us, that it may come among us and save us out of the hand of our enemies.”

routes.title: The ark is captured and Eli’s household suffers loss

1-samuel-4.dateNote: The Church chronology gives no year before Saul's reign.

1-samuel-5.summary: The Philistines bring the ark to Ashdod and set it beside their god Dagon. The next morning Dagon’s statue lies face down before the ark. They set it up, and the next day it has fallen again. Its head and hands lie broken on the threshold. The LORD strikes Ashdod with tumors. The people send the ark to Gath, and the same thing happens. Gath sends it to Ekron, and Ekron cries out in terror. The city’s cry goes up to heaven.

verse.text: When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel shall not stay with us, for his hand is severe on us and on Dagon our god.”

routes.title: The ark among the Philistine towns

1-samuel-5.dateNote: The Church chronology gives no year before Saul's reign.

1-samuel-6.summary: After seven months the Philistines ask their priests how to send the ark back. The priests advise a guilt offering of five golden tumors and five golden mice. They warn the people not to harden their hearts as Egypt did. They hitch two milk cows to a new cart and pen up the calves. If the cows go toward Israel, the LORD sent the plague. The cows walk straight to Beth Shemesh, lowing as they go. The people there rejoice and offer the cows. Some look into the ark and die, and the town sends it away.

verse.text: Behold, if it goes up by the way of its own border to Beth Shemesh, then he has done us this great evil; but if not, then we shall know that it is not his hand that struck us. It was a chance that happened to us.”

routes.title: The ark returns to Beth Shemesh

1-samuel-6.dateNote: The Church chronology gives no year before Saul's reign.

1-samuel-7.summary: The ark stays at Kiriath Jearim for twenty years. Samuel tells Israel to put away foreign gods and serve the LORD alone. They do so and gather at Mizpah to fast and confess. The Philistines hear of the gathering and attack. The people beg Samuel to keep praying for them. He offers a lamb, and the LORD thunders against the Philistines. Israel chases them, and Samuel sets up a stone named Ebenezer. Samuel judges Israel on a yearly circuit from his home in Ramah.

verse.text: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “The LORD helped us until now.”

routes.title: Samuel leads the gathering at Mizpah

1-samuel-7.dateNote: The Church chronology gives no year before Saul's reign.

1-samuel-8.summary: Samuel grows old, and his sons take bribes as judges. The elders ask him for a king like all the nations have. Samuel is displeased and prays. The LORD says the people have rejected him, not Samuel, as king. Samuel must warn them how a king will behave. A king will take their sons, daughters, fields, crops, servants, and flocks. They will cry out, and the LORD will not answer. The people still insist, and the LORD tells Samuel to give them a king.

verse.text: He will take one tenth of your flocks; and you will be his servants.

1-samuel-9.summary: Saul, a tall young man of Benjamin, searches for his father’s lost donkeys. After three days he wants to turn back. His servant suggests asking a man of God in the nearby town. The servant also supplies the silver for a gift. The day before, the LORD told Samuel that a Benjamite would come. Samuel must anoint him as leader over Israel. Samuel seats Saul at the head of a feast and gives him a reserved portion. Saul says his tribe is the smallest and his family the least.

verse.text: The servant said to him, “Behold now, there is a man of God in this city, and he is a man who is held in honor. All that he says surely happens. Now let’s go there. Perhaps he can tell us which way to go.”

1-samuel-10.summary: Samuel pours oil on Saul’s head and names three signs for the road home. All three happen, and God gives Saul another heart. The Spirit comes on him, and he prophesies among a band of prophets. He tells his uncle about the donkeys but not about the kingdom. Samuel gathers Israel at Mizpah and chooses by lot. The lot falls on Saul, who is hiding among the baggage. The people shout, “Long live the king!” Some men despise him, and he keeps silent.

verse.text: Therefore they asked of the LORD further, “Is there yet a man to come here?” The LORD answered, “Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage.”

1-samuel-11.summary: Nahash the Ammonite surrounds Jabesh Gilead. He will make peace only if he may put out every right eye. The town sends messengers through Israel. Saul comes in from the field behind his oxen and hears the news. God’s Spirit comes on him, and he is very angry. He cuts up the oxen and sends the pieces as a summons. Israel gathers, and Saul breaks the Ammonite camp at dawn. He refuses to punish his critics, and the people renew the kingdom at Gilgal.

verse.text: Saul said, “No man shall be put to death today; for today the LORD has rescued Israel.”

1-samuel-12.summary: Samuel speaks to all Israel now that a king leads them. He asks whom he has cheated, oppressed, or taken a bribe from. The people answer that he has taken nothing. He reviews how the LORD rescued them each time they cried out. Still they asked for a king when the LORD was their king. If they and their king obey, it will go well. Samuel calls for thunder and rain at wheat harvest, and the people are afraid. He promises to keep praying for them and teaching them.

verse.text: Here I am. Witness against me before the LORD and before his anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? Of whose hand have I taken a bribe to make me blind my eyes? I will restore it to you.”

1-samuel-13.summary: Jonathan attacks a Philistine post, and the Philistines gather a huge army. Israel’s men hide in caves and pits, and some cross the Jordan. Saul waits seven days at Gilgal for Samuel, as he was told. Samuel does not come, and the soldiers begin to leave. Saul offers the burnt offering himself. Samuel arrives at once and says Saul’s kingdom will not last. The LORD has sought a man after his own heart. Saul is left with six hundred men, and only he and Jonathan have swords.

verse.text: Samuel said, “What have you done?” Saul said, “Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that you didn’t come within the days appointed, and that the Philistines assembled themselves together at Michmash,

1-samuel-14.summary: Jonathan and his armor bearer climb to a Philistine post alone. Jonathan says the LORD can save by many or by few. They kill about twenty men, and panic spreads through the Philistine camp. Saul joins the fight and puts a curse on anyone who eats before evening. Jonathan has not heard it and eats some honey. The hungry soldiers later eat meat with the blood. God gives Saul no answer, and the lot falls on Jonathan. Saul says he must die, but the people rescue him.

verse.text: The people said to Saul, “Shall Jonathan die, who has worked this great salvation in Israel? Far from it! As the LORD lives, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground, for he has worked with God today!” So the people rescued Jonathan, so he didn’t die.

1-samuel-15.summary: Samuel gives Saul the LORD’s command to destroy Amalek completely. The reason given is Amalek’s attack on Israel after Egypt. Saul defeats them but spares King Agag and the best animals. The LORD tells Samuel he regrets making Saul king. Saul greets Samuel and claims he has obeyed. Samuel asks about the sheep he hears and says obeying is better than sacrifice. Saul admits he feared the people, and the LORD rejects him as king. Samuel kills Agag and never visits Saul again.

verse.text: But the people took of the plunder, sheep and cattle, the best of the devoted things, to sacrifice to the LORD your God in Gilgal.”

routes.title: Saul goes by Carmel to Gilgal

1-samuel-16.summary: The LORD sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint a son of Jesse. Samuel admires the eldest, but the LORD looks at the heart. Seven sons pass by, and none is chosen. The youngest, David, is brought from the sheep, and Samuel anoints him. The LORD’s Spirit comes on David and leaves Saul. A troubling spirit torments Saul, and his servants seek a harp player. One of them recommends David. David enters Saul’s service, and his music gives the king relief.

verse.text: When the spirit from God was on Saul, David took the harp and played with his hand; so Saul was refreshed and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.

routes.title: David is anointed and enters Saul’s service

1-samuel-17.summary: The Philistine champion Goliath challenges Israel to single combat for forty days. Saul and his army are afraid. David brings food to his brothers and hears the challenge. He tells Saul that the LORD saved him from a lion and a bear. Saul dresses David in his own armor, but David takes it off. He chooses five smooth stones and his sling. He tells Goliath that the battle is the LORD’s. One stone sinks into the giant’s forehead, and David cuts off his head.

verse.text: Saul dressed David with his clothing. He put a helmet of bronze on his head, and he clad him with a coat of mail.

routes.title: David faces Goliath in the Valley of Elah

1-samuel-18.summary: Jonathan loves David and makes a covenant with him. He gives David his own robe, sword, and bow. Women sing that Saul has killed thousands and David ten thousands. Saul becomes angry and watches David from that day. Twice he throws a spear at him. He offers his daughter Merab, then gives her to another man. Michal loves David, and Saul asks a deadly bride price, hoping the Philistines kill him. David pays double, and Saul fears him even more.

verse.text: Saul was very angry, and this saying displeased him. He said, “They have credited David with ten thousands, and they have only credited me with thousands. What can he have more but the kingdom?”

1-samuel-19.summary: Saul tells Jonathan and his servants to kill David. Jonathan defends David, and Saul swears he will not die. War returns, David wins again, and Saul throws his spear a third time. Saul’s men watch David’s house that night. Michal lowers David from a window and puts a household idol in his bed. David flees to Samuel at Ramah. Three groups of Saul’s messengers are overcome and begin to prophesy. Saul goes himself, and the Spirit overcomes him too.

verse.text: Saul said to Michal, “Why have you deceived me like this and let my enemy go, so that he has escaped?” Michal answered Saul, “He said to me, ‘Let me go! Why should I kill you?’ ”

1-samuel-20.summary: David asks Jonathan why Saul wants him dead. They agree on a test at the new moon feast. Jonathan asks David to show kindness to his family in the future. At the feast Saul notices David’s empty seat. He rages at Jonathan and says David blocks his way to the throne. Jonathan asks what David has done, and Saul throws a spear at him. Jonathan warns David with a signal of arrows in the field. They weep, swear friendship again, and part.

verse.text: For as long as the son of Jesse lives on the earth, you will not be established, nor will your kingdom. Therefore now send and bring him to me, for he shall surely die!”

1-samuel-21.summary: David flees alone to the priests at Nob. He tells Ahimelech that the king sent him on secret business. He asks for bread, and the priest has only the holy bread. Ahimelech gives it once he hears the men have kept from women. David also takes Goliath’s sword, which was kept there. Doeg the Edomite, Saul’s chief herdsman, is present that day. David goes on to King Achish of Gath, where the servants recognize him. He pretends to be mad, and Achish sends him away.

verse.text: So the priest gave him holy bread; for there was no bread there but the show bread that was taken from before the LORD, to be replaced with hot bread in the day when it was taken away.

routes.title: David seeks food at Nob and refuge at Gath

1-samuel-22.summary: David hides in the cave of Adullam. His family and about four hundred troubled men join him. He leaves his parents with the king of Moab. Saul complains that his servants conspire against him. Doeg reports that Ahimelech gave David food and a sword. Ahimelech says David was the king’s loyal son-in-law. Saul orders the priests killed, and only Doeg obeys. Eighty-five priests and the town of Nob die, and Abiathar escapes to David.

verse.text: The king said to the guard who stood about him, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because their hand also is with David, and because they knew that he fled and didn’t disclose it to me.” But the servants of the king wouldn’t put out their hand to fall on the priests of the LORD.

routes.title: David gathers followers and Saul orders the Nob massacre

1-samuel-23.summary: David asks the LORD twice and then rescues the town of Keilah from Philistines. Saul hears and prepares to trap him inside its gates. David asks through the priest’s ephod whether Keilah will hand him over. The answer is yes, so he leaves with six hundred men. Jonathan finds him in the wilderness and strengthens his trust in God. The people of Ziph tell Saul where David hides. Saul closes in around a mountain. A Philistine raid calls him away just in time.

verse.text: Then David said, “Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul?” The LORD said, “They will deliver you up.”

routes.title: Keilah, wilderness pursuit, and Jonathan’s support

1-samuel-24.summary: Saul takes three thousand men to hunt David at En Gedi. He enters a cave alone, and David’s men are hiding deep inside. They say the LORD has given David his enemy. David cuts off a corner of Saul’s robe and then regrets even that. He will not harm the LORD’s anointed. Outside, he bows and shows Saul the cloth. Saul weeps and says David is more righteous than he is. He admits David will be king and asks mercy for his family.

verse.text: Moreover, my father, behold, yes, see the skirt of your robe in my hand; for in that I cut off the skirt of your robe and didn’t kill you, know and see that there is neither evil nor disobedience in my hand. I have not sinned against you, though you hunt for my life to take it.

1-samuel-25.summary: Samuel dies, and Israel mourns him. David’s men have guarded the flocks of Nabal, a rich and harsh man. David asks for food at shearing time, and Nabal insults him. David arms four hundred men and swears to kill every male. Nabal’s wife Abigail hurries out with food and meets David on the road. She asks him not to shed blood he will later regret. David blesses her and turns back. Nabal dies ten days later, and David marries Abigail.

verse.text: Blessed is your discretion, and blessed are you, who have kept me today from blood guiltiness, and from avenging myself with my own hand.

1-samuel-26.summary: The people of Ziph again tell Saul where David is. Saul camps with three thousand men. David and Abishai slip into the camp at night and find Saul asleep. Abishai offers to pin him to the ground with one stroke. David forbids it and takes Saul’s spear and water jar. From a far hill he calls to Abner and to Saul. Saul admits he has played the fool and promises no more harm. David returns the spear, and each goes his own way.

verse.text: This thing isn’t good that you have done. As the LORD lives, you are worthy to die, because you have not kept watch over your lord, the LORD’s anointed. Now see where the king’s spear is, and the jar of water that was at his head.”

1-samuel-27.summary: David decides that Saul will one day kill him. He crosses to the Philistines with six hundred men and their families. King Achish of Gath gives him the town of Ziklag. Saul stops searching for him. David raids the Geshurites, Girzites, and Amalekites to the south. He leaves no one alive and takes the livestock. He tells Achish that he has raided Judah. Achish believes David’s own people now hate him.

verse.text: David saved neither man nor woman alive to bring them to Gath, saying, “Lest they should tell about us, saying, ‘David did this, and this has been his way all the time he has lived in the country of the Philistines.’ ”

routes.title: David lives under Achish and conceals his raids

1-samuel-28.summary: The Philistines gather for war, and Achish expects David to fight for him. Samuel is dead, and Saul has driven mediums from the land. Saul is afraid, and the LORD gives him no answer. He disguises himself and visits a medium at Endor by night. He asks her to bring up Samuel. Samuel says the LORD has given the kingdom to David. Tomorrow Saul and his sons will die. Saul falls to the ground, and the woman persuades him to eat.

verse.text: The woman said to him, “Behold, you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off those who have familiar spirits and the wizards out of the land. Why then do you lay a snare for my life, to cause me to die?”

routes.title: Saul goes to Endor by night

1-samuel-29.summary: The Philistine armies gather at Aphek, and David marches at the rear with Achish. The Philistine commanders ask what these Hebrews are doing there. Achish says he has found no fault in David. The commanders are angry and demand that David be sent back. They quote the song about Saul’s thousands and David’s ten thousands. Achish apologizes and tells David to leave at dawn. David protests that he has done nothing wrong. He and his men return south in the morning.

verse.text: But the princes of the Philistines were angry with him; and the princes of the Philistines said to him, “Make the man return, that he may go back to his place where you have appointed him, and let him not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he become an adversary to us. For with what should this fellow reconcile himself to his lord? Should it not be with the heads of these men?

1-samuel-30.summary: David returns to Ziklag and finds it burned by Amalekites. The wives and children are gone, and his men talk of stoning him. David finds strength in the LORD and asks whether to pursue. Two hundred men are too tired to cross the brook Besor. An abandoned Egyptian slave leads the rest to the raiders. David recovers every person and all the goods. Some men want to give the two hundred nothing. David rules that all share alike and sends gifts to Judah’s elders.

verse.text: Who will listen to you in this matter? For as his share is who goes down to the battle, so shall his share be who stays with the baggage. They shall share alike.”

routes.title: David recovers the captives and shares the spoil

1-samuel-31.summary: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa. Jonathan and two of his brothers are killed. Archers wound Saul badly. He asks his armor bearer to kill him, and the man is afraid. Saul falls on his own sword, and the armor bearer does the same. The Philistines cut off Saul’s head and hang his body on Beth Shan’s wall. Men of Jabesh Gilead march all night and take the bodies down. They burn them, bury the bones, and fast seven days.

verse.text: all the valiant men arose, went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth Shan; and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.

routes.title: Saul and his sons die at Gilboa

2-samuel-1.summary: David is back in Ziklag when a man arrives from Saul’s camp. The man is an Amalekite, and he carries Saul’s crown and bracelet. He says the wounded Saul asked him for a final blow. David and his men tear their clothes and fast until evening. David has the man put to death for killing the LORD’s anointed. Then David sings a lament for Saul and Jonathan. Three times it cries, “How the mighty have fallen!” He orders the people of Judah to learn it.

verse.text: David said to him, “Your blood be on your head, for your mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I have slain the LORD’s anointed.’ ”

2-samuel-2.summary: David asks the LORD and moves to Hebron. The men of Judah anoint him king there. He thanks Jabesh Gilead for burying Saul. Abner, Saul’s general, makes Saul’s son Ishbosheth king over the other tribes. The two armies meet at the pool of Gibeon. A contest of twelve against twelve turns into a battle. Joab’s brother Asahel chases Abner, ignores two warnings, and is killed. At sunset Abner calls for a halt, and Joab stops the pursuit.

verse.text: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, “Shall the sword devour forever? Don’t you know that it will be bitterness in the latter end? How long will it be then, before you ask the people to return from following their brothers?”

routes.title: Two kingdoms and the battle at Gibeon

2-samuel-3.summary: The war between Saul’s house and David’s house lasts a long time. Ishbosheth accuses Abner over one of Saul’s concubines. Abner is furious and offers to bring all Israel to David. David first demands Michal back, and her husband follows her weeping. Abner meets David and leaves in peace. Joab calls him back and stabs him at the gate for Asahel’s death. David curses Joab’s house and leads the mourning for Abner. He says Zeruiah’s sons are too hard for him.

verse.text: Afterward, when David heard it, he said, “I and my kingdom are guiltless before the LORD forever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner.

routes.title: Abner changes allegiance and Joab kills him

2-samuel-4.summary: Ishbosheth loses courage when he hears Abner is dead. Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth is mentioned; he was lamed as a child in the flight. Two of Ishbosheth’s captains, Rechab and Baanah, enter his house at noon. They kill him on his bed and cut off his head. They carry it all night to David at Hebron. They say the LORD has avenged David on Saul’s family. David recalls the messenger he executed at Ziklag. He has the two men killed and buries the head in Abner’s tomb.

verse.text: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house on his bed, should I not now require his blood from your hand, and rid the earth of you?”

2-samuel-5.summary: All the tribes come to Hebron and anoint David king over Israel. He is thirty years old and reigns forty years in all. He captures the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites. Jerusalem becomes the City of David. Hiram king of Tyre sends cedar and craftsmen to build him a house. David takes more wives and has more children. The Philistines attack twice in the Valley of Rephaim. Each time David asks the LORD and wins.

verse.text: David perceived that the LORD had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel’s sake.

routes.title: David becomes king of Israel and takes Jerusalem

2-samuel-6.summary: David gathers thirty thousand men to bring the ark to Jerusalem. They carry it on a new cart, and Uzzah touches it and dies. David is angry and afraid and leaves it at Obed-Edom’s house. The LORD blesses that house for three months. David then brings the ark up with sacrifices, dancing in a linen ephod. Saul’s daughter Michal watches from a window and despises him. He blesses the people and gives everyone food. Michal mocks his display, and she has no child to her death.

verse.text: Then David returned to bless his household. Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, “How glorious the king of Israel was today, who uncovered himself today in the eyes of his servants’ maids, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!”

2-samuel-7.summary: David lives in a cedar house and wants to build one for the ark. The prophet Nathan first tells him to go ahead. That night the LORD sends Nathan back with a different word. The LORD never asked for a house of cedar. He took David from the pasture and will make David a house. A son will build the temple, and his throne will last forever. If he sins he will be disciplined, but not rejected like Saul. David sits before the LORD and asks, “Who am I?”

verse.text: He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

2-samuel-8.summary: David defeats the Philistines and takes their chief city. He defeats Moab and puts two thirds of the captives to death. He defeats Hadadezer of Zobah and the Syrians of Damascus. He places troops in Syria and Edom, and those peoples serve him. King Toi of Hamath sends gifts of silver, gold, and bronze. David dedicates the metal to the LORD. The LORD gives him victory wherever he goes. The chapter ends with a list of his chief officers.

verse.text: David reigned over all Israel; and David executed justice and righteousness for all his people.

2-samuel-9.summary: David asks whether anyone is left from Saul’s house. He wants to show kindness for Jonathan’s sake. Ziba, a servant of Saul’s house, names Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth, who is lame. David sends for him from Lo Debar. Mephibosheth falls on his face before the king. David tells him not to fear and restores all Saul’s land to him. Ziba and his household will farm it. Mephibosheth will eat at the king’s table like one of his sons.

verse.text: He bowed down, and said, “What is your servant, that you should look at such a dead dog as I am?”

2-samuel-10.summary: The king of Ammon dies, and David sends men to comfort his son Hanun. Hanun’s princes say the visitors are spies. Hanun shaves half of each man’s beard and cuts their clothes at the hips. David lets the shamed men wait at Jericho until their beards grow. Ammon hires Syrian armies. Joab splits his forces with his brother Abishai, and the Syrians flee. Hadadezer brings more Syrians from beyond the River. David defeats them, and they make peace with Israel.

verse.text: But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, “Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Hasn’t David sent his servants to you to search the city, to spy it out, and to overthrow it?”

2-samuel-11.summary: In spring David sends Joab to besiege Rabbah and stays in Jerusalem. From his roof he sees a woman bathing. She is Bathsheba, wife of Uriah the Hittite, one of his soldiers. David sends for her, lies with her, and she becomes pregnant. He calls Uriah home, but Uriah will not go to his house during war. David sends him back with a letter to Joab ordering his death. Uriah is killed at the city wall with other men. David marries Bathsheba, and the thing displeases the LORD.

verse.text: He wrote in the letter, saying, “Send Uriah to the forefront of the hottest battle, and retreat from him, that he may be struck and die.”

routes.title: Uriah carries the letter to Joab

2-samuel-12.summary: The LORD sends Nathan to David with a story. A rich man took a poor man’s only lamb to feed a guest. David says the man deserves to die. Nathan answers, “You are the man!” The sword will never leave David’s house, and his own wives will be taken. David confesses, and Nathan says he will not die, but the child will. David fasts for seven days until the child dies. Later Bathsheba bears Solomon, and David captures Rabbah.

verse.text: Nathan said to David, “You are the man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you out of the hand of Saul.

2-samuel-13.summary: David’s son Amnon desires his half sister Tamar. On a cousin’s advice he pretends to be ill and asks her to bring food. He seizes her, and she pleads with him. He rapes her, then hates her and has her thrown out. Tamar tears her royal robe and goes away crying. Her brother Absalom takes her into his house. David is very angry but does nothing. Two years later Absalom has Amnon killed and flees to Geshur.

verse.text: As for me, where would I carry my shame? And as for you, you will be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, please speak to the king; for he will not withhold me from you.”

routes.title: Amnon assaults Tamar and Absalom takes revenge

2-samuel-14.summary: Joab sees that David longs for Absalom. He sends a wise woman from Tekoa to the king in mourning clothes. She says one of her sons killed the other in a fight. Her clan now demands the life of the son who is left. David promises to protect him. She then asks why the king does not bring back his own banished son. David guesses that Joab is behind it and lets Absalom return. For two years Absalom may not see the king’s face.

verse.text: For we must die, and are like water spilled on the ground, which can’t be gathered up again; neither does God take away life, but devises means, that he who is banished not be an outcast from him.

2-samuel-15.summary: Absalom gets a chariot, horses, and fifty runners. He stands by the gate and meets people who bring cases to the king. He tells each one that his claim is good and no one will hear it. So he steals the hearts of Israel. After four years he goes to Hebron and has himself declared king. David flees Jerusalem with his household and loyal foreign troops. He sends the ark back to the city with the priests. He climbs the Mount of Olives weeping and sends Hushai to act as a spy.

verse.text: Absalom said moreover, “Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man who has any suit or cause might come to me, and I would do him justice!”

routes.title: Absalom gathers support and David leaves Jerusalem

2-samuel-16.summary: Ziba meets the fleeing king with donkeys, bread, fruit, and wine. He says Mephibosheth stayed in Jerusalem hoping to gain Saul’s kingdom. David gives Ziba all of Mephibosheth’s property. At Bahurim a man of Saul’s family named Shimei curses David and throws stones. Abishai wants to cut off his head. David says to leave him; perhaps the LORD told him to curse. Absalom enters Jerusalem, and Hushai pretends to serve him. On Ahithophel’s advice Absalom takes his father’s concubines in public.

verse.text: Then the king said to Ziba, “Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours.” Ziba said, “I bow down. Let me find favor in your sight, my lord, O king.”

2-samuel-17.summary: Ahithophel advises Absalom to strike David that night with twelve thousand men. Hushai argues for waiting and gathering all Israel. Absalom prefers Hushai’s advice, as the LORD intended. Hushai sends warning to David through the priests’ two sons. A boy sees them, and they hide in a well at Bahurim. A woman covers the well and sends the searchers away. David crosses the Jordan that night, and Ahithophel hangs himself. At Mahanaim three men bring beds, bowls, and food to David’s people.

verse.text: But a boy saw them, and told Absalom. Then they both went away quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, who had a well in his court; and they went down there.

routes.title: Hushai’s counsel and the messengers’ escape

2-samuel-18.summary: David divides his army under Joab, Abishai, and Ittai. The men will not let him fight. He orders the three to deal gently with Absalom, and all the soldiers hear it. David’s men win in the forest of Ephraim. Absalom’s head catches in an oak, and his mule runs on. A soldier refuses to touch him, but Joab stabs him. Two runners carry the news to the king. David asks only about Absalom and weeps, “My son, my son!”

verse.text: The king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, “Deal gently for my sake with the young man Absalom.” All the people heard when the king commanded all the captains concerning Absalom.

2-samuel-19.summary: Joab tells David that his weeping shames the men who saved him. David sits in the gate, and the people come to him. He invites Judah to bring him back and promises Joab’s post to Amasa. Shimei begs forgiveness at the Jordan, and David spares him. Mephibosheth comes unwashed and says Ziba deceived him. David tells the two to divide the land. Old Barzillai declines a place at court and sends Chimham. Israel and Judah then quarrel over who has more claim to the king.

verse.text: The king said to him, “Why do you speak any more of your matters? I say, you and Ziba divide the land.”

routes.title: David returns and hears competing claims

2-samuel-20.summary: Sheba, a man of Benjamin, calls Israel to leave David, and the northern tribes follow. David sets apart the ten concubines Absalom took. Amasa is slow to gather Judah’s army. Joab greets Amasa as a brother and stabs him. Joab’s army besieges Sheba in the town of Abel. A wise woman calls to Joab from the wall. She persuades the town to throw Sheba’s head over to him. Joab withdraws, and a list of David’s officers follows.

verse.text: I am among those who are peaceable and faithful in Israel. You seek to destroy a city and a mother in Israel. Why will you swallow up the LORD’s inheritance?”

routes.title: Sheba’s revolt and the wise woman of Abel

2-samuel-21.summary: A famine lasts three years, and David asks the LORD why. The answer is that Saul killed Gibeonites, breaking Israel’s old oath. The Gibeonites ask for seven of Saul’s male descendants. David spares Mephibosheth and hands over seven others. They are hanged on a hill at the start of barley harvest. Rizpah, mother of two of them, guards the bodies until the rain comes. David hears of it and buries the bones with Saul’s and Jonathan’s. Four giants later fall to David’s men.

verse.text: Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water poured on them from the sky. She allowed neither the birds of the sky to rest on them by day, nor the animals of the field by night.

routes.title: Rizpah guards the dead and warriors defend David

2-samuel-22.summary: David sings this song after the LORD rescues him from Saul and all his enemies. He calls the LORD his rock, fortress, and shield. Death’s waves surrounded him, and he cried out. The earth shook, and the LORD came down in storm and fire. He drew David out of deep waters. David says the LORD rewarded his clean hands. With God’s help he can run through a troop and leap a wall. The song ends with kindness to David and his descendants forever.

verse.text: You have also given me the shield of your salvation. Your gentleness has made me great.

2-samuel-23.summary: David’s last words say a ruler must be just and fear God. Such a ruler is like morning light after rain. God has made a lasting covenant with his house. The chapter then lists David’s mighty men and their deeds. One stood alone in a field and fought until his hand stuck to his sword. Three broke through Philistine lines to bring David water from Bethlehem’s well. Benaiah killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day. The list of the Thirty ends with Uriah the Hittite.

verse.text: He said, “Be it far from me, LORD, that I should do this! Isn’t this the blood of the men who risked their lives to go?” Therefore he would not drink it. The three mighty men did these things.

2-samuel-24.summary: The LORD is angry with Israel, and David is moved to count the people. Joab objects, but the king insists. The count takes almost ten months. Then David’s heart troubles him, and he confesses. The prophet Gad offers three punishments, and David chooses to fall into the LORD’s hand. A plague kills seventy thousand. The angel stops at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite. David buys the floor, builds an altar, and the plague ends.

verse.text: The king said to Araunah, “No, but I will most certainly buy it from you for a price. I will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God which cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

1-kings-1.summary: King David is old and weak. His son Adonijah declares himself king with the support of Joab and the priest Abiathar. He holds a feast and leaves out Solomon and the prophet Nathan. Nathan sends Bathsheba to remind David of his oath about Solomon. Nathan follows her in and confirms her report. David orders Solomon to ride the royal mule to Gihon. Zadok the priest anoints him, and the city shouts. Adonijah’s guests scatter, and he begs Solomon for his life.

verse.text: You, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, that you should tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

1-kings-2.summary: David tells Solomon to keep the LORD’s law and to deal with Joab and Shimei. David dies after forty years as king. Adonijah asks Bathsheba to request David’s last attendant, Abishag, as his wife. Solomon reads this as a claim to the throne and has him killed. He sends the priest Abiathar home to Anathoth. Joab flees to the altar and is killed there. Shimei is confined to Jerusalem and dies when he leaves it. The kingdom is now firmly in Solomon’s hand.

verse.text: To Abiathar the priest the king said, “Go to Anathoth, to your own fields, for you are worthy of death. But I will not at this time put you to death, because you bore the Lord GOD’s ark before David my father, and because you were afflicted in all in which my father was afflicted.”

routes.title: David dies and Solomon consolidates power

1-kings-3.summary: Solomon marries Pharaoh’s daughter and brings her to Jerusalem. He offers sacrifices at Gibeon, and the LORD appears to him in a dream. God tells him to ask for what he wants. Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people. God is pleased and adds riches and honor. Two prostitutes then come to him, each claiming the same living baby. Solomon calls for a sword to divide the child. The true mother gives up her claim, and he returns the child to her.

verse.text: Give your servant therefore an understanding heart to judge your people, that I may discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this great people of yours?”

1-kings-4.summary: The chapter lists Solomon’s chief officials. Twelve officers govern twelve districts. Each district supplies the king’s household for one month of the year. Judah and Israel are as many as the sand, eating and drinking. The court uses huge amounts of flour, meal, and meat each day. Everyone lives safely under his own vine and fig tree. God gives Solomon wisdom beyond all the people of the East. He speaks three thousand proverbs and teaches about trees and animals.

verse.text: Those officers provided food for King Solomon, and for all who came to King Solomon’s table, every man in his month. They let nothing be lacking.

1-kings-5.summary: King Hiram of Tyre sends greetings to Solomon. Solomon says he will build a house for the LORD’s name. He asks for cedar from Lebanon, cut by skilled Sidonians. Hiram agrees and floats the logs down the coast. Solomon pays him each year in wheat and oil. The two kings make a treaty. Solomon drafts thirty thousand Israelites to work in Lebanon in shifts. Thousands more carry loads and cut great stones for the foundation.

verse.text: King Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy was thirty thousand men.

routes.title: Hiram supplies timber for the temple

1-kings-6.summary: Solomon begins the temple in the fourth year of his reign. The house is sixty cubits long, twenty wide, and thirty high. Its stones are finished at the quarry, so no iron tool is heard on site. The LORD tells Solomon the promise holds if he keeps the commandments. The inside is lined with cedar and covered with gold. Two gold-covered cherubim stand in the inner room. The walls and doors are carved with palms and flowers. The work takes seven years.

verse.text: “Concerning this house which you are building, if you will walk in my statutes, and execute my ordinances, and keep all my commandments to walk in them, then I will establish my word with you, which I spoke to David your father.

1-kings-7.summary: Solomon spends thirteen years building his own palace. It includes the House of the Forest of Lebanon and a hall for judging. He builds a similar house for Pharaoh’s daughter. He brings Hiram, a bronze worker, from Tyre. Hiram casts two great pillars named Jachin and Boaz. He makes a huge basin called the sea, set on twelve bronze oxen. He makes ten wheeled stands, basins, pots, and shovels. Solomon adds the gold furnishings and David’s dedicated treasures.

verse.text: He was the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze; and he was filled with wisdom and understanding and skill to work all works in bronze. He came to King Solomon and performed all his work.

1-kings-8.summary: The elders and priests bring the ark into the temple. A cloud fills the house, and the priests cannot stand to serve. Solomon blesses the people and prays before the altar. He says heaven itself cannot contain God, much less this house. He asks God to hear prayers made toward it. He names drought, famine, defeat, and exile as times to pray. He asks God to hear the foreigner too. Israel then offers sacrifices and keeps a feast for fourteen days.

verse.text: “Moreover, concerning the foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, when he comes out of a far country for your name’s sake

1-kings-9.summary: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time and accepts the temple. If Solomon walks as David did, his throne will last. If Israel turns to other gods, the land and the house will be lost. Solomon gives Hiram twenty towns in Galilee, and Hiram is not pleased. Solomon uses forced labor to build Jerusalem’s wall, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer. The remaining Canaanite peoples are made laborers. Israelites serve as soldiers and officers. Solomon builds ships on the Red Sea that bring gold from Ophir.

verse.text: then I will cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them; and I will cast this house, which I have made holy for my name, out of my sight; and Israel will be a proverb and a byword among all peoples.

1-kings-10.summary: The queen of Sheba hears of Solomon and comes to test him with hard questions. He answers them all. She sees his house, his table, his servants, and his offerings. She says the report she heard was not even half the truth. She blesses the LORD, who made him king to do justice. They exchange rich gifts, and she goes home. Solomon’s yearly gold, his ivory throne, and his golden cups are described. He gathers chariots and buys horses from Egypt.

verse.text: Happy are your men, happy are these your servants who stand continually before you, who hear your wisdom.

1-kings-11.summary: Solomon loves many foreign women and has a thousand wives and concubines. In his old age they turn his heart to other gods. He builds high places for the gods of Moab and Ammon. The LORD says the kingdom will be torn from his son. One tribe will remain for David’s sake. Enemies rise in Edom and Damascus. The prophet Ahijah tears a new cloak and gives ten pieces to an officer, Jeroboam. Solomon tries to kill Jeroboam, who flees to Egypt until Solomon dies.

verse.text: Ahijah took the new garment that was on him, and tore it in twelve pieces.

routes.title: Solomon turns away and adversaries rise

1-kings-12.summary: Rehoboam goes to Shechem to be made king. Jeroboam and the people ask him to lighten Solomon’s heavy labor. The old advisers tell him to serve the people and speak kindly. The young men tell him to promise a heavier yoke. He follows the young men and threatens scorpions for whips. Ten tribes reject David’s house and make Jeroboam king. A prophet stops Rehoboam from going to war. Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan to keep his people from Jerusalem.

verse.text: “Your father made our yoke difficult. Now therefore make the hard service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you.”

routes.title: Rehoboam rejects the petition and the kingdom divides

1-kings-12.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 975–957 BC.

1-kings-13.summary: A man of God from Judah cries out against Jeroboam’s altar at Bethel. The altar splits, and the king’s hand withers and is healed. The man refuses the king’s meal, as God commanded him. An old prophet of Bethel rides after him. The old man lies and says an angel told him to bring the visitor home. The man of God eats, and a word comes that he will die. A lion kills him on the road and stands beside the body. The old prophet buries him in his own tomb.

verse.text: He said to him, “I also am a prophet as you are; and an angel spoke to me by the LORD’s word, saying, ‘Bring him back with you into your house, that he may eat bread and drink water.’ ” He lied to him.

1-kings-13.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 975–957 BC.

1-kings-14.summary: Jeroboam’s son falls sick. He sends his wife in disguise to the prophet Ahijah at Shiloh. Ahijah is blind, but the LORD tells him who is coming. He says Jeroboam’s whole house will be cut off for its idols. The child will die when she reaches home. Israel itself will be uprooted and scattered. In Judah, Rehoboam’s people build high places and sacred pillars. Shishak king of Egypt takes the temple’s treasures and Solomon’s gold shields.

verse.text: So when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet as she came in at the door, he said, “Come in, Jeroboam’s wife! Why do you pretend to be another? For I am sent to you with heavy news.

routes.title: Ahijah speaks and Shishak attacks Jerusalem

1-kings-14.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 975–957 BC.

1-kings-15.summary: Abijam rules Judah three years and follows his father’s sins. For David’s sake the LORD keeps a lamp in Jerusalem. Asa rules forty-one years and does what is right. He removes idols and even deposes his grandmother for her idol. Baasha of Israel fortifies Ramah to block Judah. Asa sends temple and palace treasure to Ben Hadad of Syria. Ben Hadad attacks northern Israel, and Baasha withdraws. In Israel, Baasha has killed Nadab and all Jeroboam’s house.

verse.text: “Let there be a treaty between me and you, like that between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent to you a present of silver and gold. Go, break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.”

1-kings-15.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 957–918 BC.

1-kings-16.summary: A prophet tells Baasha that his house will end like Jeroboam’s. His son Elah is killed while drunk by Zimri, a chariot commander. Zimri rules seven days and burns the palace over himself. Omri defeats a rival and becomes king. He buys the hill of Samaria and builds his capital there. His son Ahab marries Jezebel of Sidon and builds a temple for Baal. Ahab does more evil than all before him. In his days a man rebuilds Jericho at the cost of two sons.

verse.text: He bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver; and he built on the hill, and called the name of the city which he built, Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill.

routes.title: Omri moves the capital to Samaria

1-kings-16.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 957–918 BC.

1-kings-17.summary: Elijah tells Ahab there will be no dew or rain except at his word. The LORD hides him by a brook, where ravens bring him food. The brook dries up. The LORD sends him to a widow in Zarephath, a town of Sidon. She is gathering sticks to cook a last meal for herself and her son. Elijah asks for a small cake first and promises the flour and oil will last. They do. Later her son dies, Elijah prays, and the boy lives again.

verse.text: She said, “As the LORD your God lives, I don’t have anything baked, but only a handful of meal in a jar and a little oil in a jar. Behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and bake it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.”

routes.title: Elijah and the widow at Zarephath

1-kings-17.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 918–898 BC.

1-kings-18.summary: In the third year of drought the LORD sends Elijah to Ahab. Ahab’s steward Obadiah has hidden a hundred prophets from Jezebel. Elijah gathers Israel and four hundred fifty prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. Each side prepares a bull, and the God who answers by fire is God. Baal’s prophets cry out all day, and nothing happens. Elijah rebuilds the LORD’s altar and drenches it with water. He prays, and fire falls and burns up everything. The people confess the LORD, Baal’s prophets are killed, and rain comes.

verse.text: Elijah came near to all the people, and said, “How long will you waver between the two sides? If the LORD is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.” The people didn’t say a word.

1-kings-18.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 918–898 BC.

1-kings-19.summary: Jezebel swears to kill Elijah, and he runs for his life. In the wilderness he sits under a tree and asks to die. An angel twice wakes him and gives him food and water. He travels forty days to Horeb, the mountain of God. There a wind, an earthquake, and a fire pass, and then a quiet voice. Elijah says he alone is left. The LORD sends him to anoint two kings and Elisha. Elisha leaves his oxen and follows him.

verse.text: Yet I reserved seven thousand in Israel, all the knees of which have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.”

routes.title: Elijah receives care and calls Elisha

1-kings-19.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 918–898 BC.

1-kings-20.summary: Ben Hadad of Syria besieges Samaria and demands Ahab’s treasure and family. A prophet promises Ahab victory, and Israel wins. The Syrians decide the LORD is a god of the hills only. They return in spring and lose again on the plain. Ben Hadad’s servants come in sackcloth to beg for his life. Ahab calls him “my brother” and makes a treaty. A prophet in disguise tells Ahab a story and condemns him with it. Ahab goes home sullen and angry.

verse.text: Ben Hadad said to him, “The cities which my father took from your father I will restore. You shall make streets for yourself in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria.” “I”, said Ahab, “will let you go with this covenant.” So he made a covenant with him and let him go.

1-kings-20.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 918–898 BC.

1-kings-21.summary: Naboth owns a vineyard beside Ahab’s palace in Jezreel. Ahab offers him money or a better vineyard, and Naboth refuses. Ahab lies on his bed and will not eat. Jezebel writes letters in his name to the town’s elders. Two false witnesses accuse Naboth of cursing God and the king. He is stoned, and Ahab goes down to take the vineyard. Elijah meets him there with the LORD’s sentence on his house. Ahab humbles himself, and the disaster is delayed to his son’s time.

verse.text: Naboth said to Ahab, “May the LORD forbid me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you!”

1-kings-21.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 918–898 BC.

1-kings-22.summary: Jehoshaphat of Judah visits Ahab, who wants to retake Ramoth Gilead. Four hundred prophets promise success. Jehoshaphat asks for one more, and Ahab names Micaiah, whom he hates. Micaiah sees Israel scattered like sheep without a shepherd. He describes a lying spirit sent into the mouths of Ahab’s prophets. Ahab jails him and goes to battle in disguise. A random arrow strikes Ahab between the plates of his armor. He dies at evening, and dogs lick his blood in Samaria.

verse.text: The messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “See now, the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak good.”

routes.title: Micaiah warns Ahab before the final battle

1-kings-22.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 898–897 BC.

2-kings-1.summary: King Ahaziah of Israel falls through a lattice and is badly hurt. He sends men to ask Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron, if he will recover. Elijah meets them and asks whether Israel has no God. He says the king will die. Ahaziah sends a captain with fifty men to bring Elijah down. Fire from heaven burns them, and then a second fifty. A third captain kneels and begs for his men’s lives. Elijah goes with him, repeats the message, and the king dies.

verse.text: Again he sent the captain of a third fifty with his fifty. The third captain of fifty went up, and came and fell on his knees before Elijah, and begged him, and said to him, “Man of God, please let my life and the life of these fifty of your servants be precious in your sight.

2-kings-1.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 898–897 BC.

2-kings-2.summary: Elijah travels from Gilgal to Bethel, Jericho, and the Jordan. Three times he tells Elisha to stay, and Elisha refuses. Elijah strikes the river with his cloak, and they cross on dry ground. Elisha asks for a double share of his spirit. A chariot and horses of fire part them, and Elijah goes up in a whirlwind. Elisha takes up the fallen cloak and parts the Jordan again. He heals Jericho’s bad water with salt. Youths mock him near Bethel, and two bears maul forty-two of them.

verse.text: He took Elijah’s mantle that fell from him, and struck the waters, and said, “Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?” When he also had struck the waters, they were divided apart, and Elisha went over.

routes.title: Elijah departs and Elisha takes up the mantle

2-kings-2.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 897–884 BC.

2-kings-3.summary: Jehoram of Israel goes to war when Moab stops paying tribute. Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom join him. After seven days the armies have no water. Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet, and they find Elisha. Elisha says he helps only for Jehoshaphat’s sake. He promises water without rain, and the valley fills by morning. Moab sees the water red as blood, attacks, and is routed. Moab’s king sacrifices his son on the wall, and Israel withdraws.

verse.text: Elisha said to the king of Israel, “What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father, and to the prophets of your mother.” The king of Israel said to him, “No, for the LORD has called these three kings together to deliver them into the hand of Moab.”

2-kings-3.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 897–884 BC.

2-kings-4.summary: A prophet’s widow tells Elisha that a creditor will take her two sons as slaves. She has only a jar of oil. He tells her to borrow empty jars and pour, and the oil fills them all. A wealthy woman of Shunem builds Elisha a room. He promises her a son, and the boy later dies in her lap. She rides to Elisha, and he prays and stretches out on the child. The boy sneezes seven times and opens his eyes. Elisha also cures a poisoned stew and feeds a hundred men.

verse.text: Then she came and told the man of God. He said, “Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt; and you and your sons live on the rest.”

2-kings-4.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 897–884 BC.

2-kings-5.summary: Naaman commands the army of Syria, and he has a skin disease. A captive Israelite girl tells his wife about the prophet in Samaria. Naaman arrives with horses, chariots, and gifts. Elisha sends a messenger: wash seven times in the Jordan. Naaman is angry, but his servants persuade him. He washes and is healed, and he confesses Israel’s God. Elisha refuses any gift. His servant Gehazi runs after Naaman for silver and leaves with the disease.

verse.text: His servants came near and spoke to him, and said, “My father, if the prophet had asked you do some great thing, wouldn’t you have done it? How much rather then, when he says to you, ‘Wash, and be clean’?”

routes.title: Naaman accepts help and Gehazi pursues payment

2-kings-5.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 897–884 BC.

2-kings-6.summary: A borrowed axe head falls into the Jordan, and Elisha makes it float. He warns Israel’s king about Syrian ambushes again and again. Syria sends an army to seize him at Dothan. His servant panics until he sees horses and chariots of fire. The Syrians are struck blind, and Elisha leads them into Samaria. He tells the king to feed them and send them home. Later Syria besieges Samaria, and the famine is terrible. The king blames Elisha and swears to kill him.

verse.text: He answered, “You shall not strike them. Would you strike those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, then go to their master.”

routes.title: Elisha leads an army to Samaria

2-kings-6.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 897–884 BC.

2-kings-7.summary: Elisha says that by tomorrow flour will be cheap at Samaria’s gate. An officer scoffs, and Elisha says he will see it but not eat. Four men with skin disease sit outside the gate. They decide to surrender to the Syrians, since they will die anyway. They find the camp empty, because the LORD made the Syrians hear an army. They eat and hide silver, then decide to report it. The king suspects a trap and sends scouts. The people rush out for food, and the officer is trampled in the gate.

verse.text: Then they said to one another, “We aren’t doing right. Today is a day of good news, and we keep silent. If we wait until the morning light, punishment will overtake us. Now therefore come, let’s go and tell the king’s household.”

2-kings-7.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 897–884 BC.

2-kings-8.summary: Elisha had warned the woman of Shunem about a seven-year famine. She lived among the Philistines and now returns. She appeals to the king for her house and land. At that moment Gehazi is telling the king about her son. The king restores her property and its income. Elisha goes to Damascus and weeps over what Hazael will do to Israel. Hazael smothers his sick king and takes the throne. In Judah, Jehoram marries Ahab’s daughter and follows Israel’s ways.

verse.text: As he was telling the king how he had restored to life him who was dead, behold, the woman whose son he had restored to life begged the king for her house and for her land. Gehazi said, “My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.”

routes.title: The Shunammite returns and Hazael takes power

2-kings-8.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 897–884 BC.

2-kings-9.summary: Elisha sends a young prophet to anoint Jehu, an army commander, as king. The message is to destroy Ahab’s house. Jehu’s fellow officers blow the trumpet and proclaim him. He drives furiously to Jezreel. King Joram rides out, and Jehu shoots him through the heart. The body is thrown onto Naboth’s field. Jehu’s men also kill Ahaziah king of Judah. Jezebel is thrown from a window, and dogs eat her body.

verse.text: ‘Surely I have seen yesterday the blood of Naboth, and the blood of his sons,’ says the LORD; ‘and I will repay you in this plot of ground,’ says the LORD. Now therefore take and cast him onto the plot of ground, according to the LORD’s word.”

routes.title: Jehu is anointed and kills the rulers

2-kings-9.dateDetail: Jehu's reign. The Church table gives no revised year for Jehoahaz.
2-kings-9.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 884–842 BC.

2-kings-10.summary: Jehu writes to Samaria’s leaders, and they send him the heads of Ahab’s seventy sons. He kills all who remain of Ahab’s house in Jezreel. He also kills forty-two relatives of Judah’s king. He invites Jehonadab to see his zeal for the LORD. By a trick he gathers Baal’s worshipers into their temple and kills them. He destroys the temple and makes it a latrine. Yet he keeps Jeroboam’s golden calves. Hazael of Syria begins to take Israel’s land east of the Jordan.

verse.text: But Jehu took no heed to walk in the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam, with which he made Israel to sin.

routes.title: Jehu goes from Jezreel to Samaria

2-kings-10.dateDetail: Jehu's reign. The Church table gives no revised year for Jehoahaz.
2-kings-10.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 884–842 BC.

2-kings-11.summary: Athaliah, mother of the dead king of Judah, kills the royal children and rules. The king’s sister Jehosheba steals away the baby Joash. He is hidden in the temple for six years. In the seventh year the priest Jehoiada brings in the guard captains. They surround the boy, crown him, and give him the covenant. Athaliah hears the noise and cries, “Treason!” She is put to death outside the temple. The people tear down Baal’s temple, and Joash takes the throne at seven.

verse.text: He was with her hidden in the LORD’s house six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.

2-kings-11.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 884–841 BC.

2-kings-12.summary: Joash does right as long as the priest Jehoiada teaches him. He tells the priests to use offerings to repair the temple. After many years no repairs are done. Jehoiada sets a chest with a hole in its lid beside the altar. The king’s scribe and the high priest count the silver. It is paid straight to carpenters, masons, and stonecutters. Later Hazael threatens Jerusalem, and Joash buys him off with temple treasure. His own servants kill him.

verse.text: Moreover they didn’t demand an accounting from the men into whose hand they delivered the money to give to those who did the work; for they dealt faithfully.

routes.title: Hazael takes Gath and turns to Jerusalem

2-kings-12.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 884–841 BC.

2-kings-13.summary: Jehoahaz rules Israel, and Hazael of Syria crushes his army. He seeks the LORD, and Israel gets relief. His son Jehoash visits the dying Elisha and weeps over him. Elisha has him shoot an arrow east and calls it the LORD’s arrow of victory. He tells him to strike the ground with the other arrows. The king strikes three times and stops, and Elisha is angry. Elisha dies, and a dead man revives on touching his bones. Jehoash defeats Syria three times.

verse.text: The man of God was angry with him, and said, “You should have struck five or six times. Then you would have struck Syria until you had consumed it, but now you will strike Syria just three times.”

2-kings-13.dateDetail: Jehoahaz has no revised year, so the range starts with Jehoash.
2-kings-13.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 842–773 BC.

2-kings-14.summary: Amaziah of Judah executes the servants who killed his father. He spares their children, as the law of Moses requires. He defeats Edom and then challenges Jehoash of Israel. Jehoash answers with a fable of a thistle and a cedar. Judah is beaten, Jerusalem’s wall is broken, and the temple gold is taken. Amaziah is later killed at Lachish. In Israel, Jeroboam the second rules forty-one years and does evil. Yet he restores Israel’s borders, as the prophet Jonah had said.

verse.text: but the children of the murderers he didn’t put to death, according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moses, as the LORD commanded, saying, “The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children be put to death for the fathers; but every man shall die for his own sin.”

routes.title: Amaziah loses a war and Jeroboam restores territory

2-kings-14.dateDetail: Jehoahaz has no revised year, so the range starts with Jehoash.
2-kings-14.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 842–773 BC.

2-kings-15.summary: Azariah rules Judah fifty-two years and lives apart with a skin disease. In Israel, Zechariah rules six months and is murdered. Shallum lasts one month before Menahem kills him. Menahem pays the king of Assyria a thousand talents of silver to keep his throne. His son Pekahiah is killed by Pekah, an officer. Tiglath Pileser of Assyria takes Galilee and Gilead and deports the people. Hoshea kills Pekah and rules. In Judah, Jotham does right, but the high places remain.

verse.text: Menahem exacted the money from Israel, even from all the mighty men of wealth, from each man fifty shekels of silver, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back, and didn’t stay there in the land.

2-kings-15.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 811–742 BC.
