2-kings-16.summary: Ahaz rules Judah and does not do right. He even burns his son as an offering. The kings of Syria and Israel attack Jerusalem. Ahaz sends temple silver to Tiglath Pileser and calls himself his servant and son. Assyria captures Damascus. Ahaz goes there, sees an altar, and sends its design to the priest Urijah. Urijah builds a copy, and the king offers on it. Ahaz moves the bronze altar and strips other temple furnishings because of Assyria’s king.

verse.text: King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria, and saw the altar that was at Damascus; and King Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest a drawing of the altar and plans to build it.

routes.title: Ahaz seeks Assyrian help and changes the altar

2-kings-16.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 742–726 BC.

2-kings-17.summary: Hoshea of Israel stops paying Assyria and looks to Egypt. Assyria jails him and besieges Samaria for three years. The city falls, and Israel is carried away to Assyria. The writer explains that Israel served other gods and ignored every prophet. Judah also failed to keep the commandments. Assyria settles people from other lands in Samaria’s towns. Lions attack them, and a priest is sent back to teach about the LORD. They fear the LORD and also serve their own gods.

verse.text: The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, from Cuthah, from Avva, and from Hamath and Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel; and they possessed Samaria and lived in its cities.

2-kings-17.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 730–721 BC.

2-kings-18.summary: Hezekiah rules Judah and trusts the LORD more than any king before him. He removes the high places and breaks Moses’s bronze serpent, which people worshiped. He rebels against Assyria. Samaria falls in his sixth year. In his fourteenth year Sennacherib takes Judah’s walled towns. Hezekiah sends tribute and strips gold from the temple doors. Assyria still sends an army and a spokesman to Jerusalem. He shouts in Hebrew that no god has saved any land from Assyria.

verse.text: Hezekiah king of Judah sent to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, “I have offended you. Withdraw from me. That which you put on me, I will bear.” The king of Assyria appointed to Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.

routes.title: An Assyrian army comes from Lachish

2-kings-18.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 726–697 BC.

2-kings-19.summary: Hezekiah tears his clothes and sends to the prophet Isaiah. Isaiah says not to fear the Assyrian’s words. The spokesman rejoins his king, who has left Lachish for Libnah. Sennacherib sends a letter mocking the LORD. Hezekiah spreads the letter out in the temple and prays. Isaiah answers that Assyria’s king will not enter the city or shoot an arrow there. That night the LORD’s angel strikes the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib goes home to Nineveh, where his sons kill him.

verse.text: So Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah; for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.

2-kings-19.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 726–697 BC.

2-kings-20.summary: Hezekiah falls sick, and Isaiah tells him he will die. He turns to the wall, prays, and weeps. Before Isaiah leaves the palace, the LORD sends him back. Hezekiah will live fifteen more years, and the city will be saved. As a sign the shadow moves back ten steps. Envoys come from the king of Babylon with letters and a gift. Hezekiah shows them all his treasures and weapons. Isaiah says all of it, and some of his sons, will go to Babylon.

verse.text: ‘Behold, the days come that all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have laid up in store to this day, will be carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left,’ says the LORD.

2-kings-20.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 726–697 BC.

2-kings-21.summary: Manasseh becomes king at twelve and rules fifty-five years. He rebuilds the high places his father Hezekiah destroyed. He sets up altars for Baal and for the stars inside the temple courts. He burns his son as an offering and uses sorcery. The prophets say Jerusalem will be wiped like a dish. Manasseh also sheds much innocent blood. His son Amon rules two years and is killed by his servants. The people make Amon’s son Josiah king.

verse.text: Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, until he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another; in addition to his sin with which he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the LORD’s sight.

2-kings-22.summary: Josiah becomes king at eight and does what is right. In his eighteenth year he orders repairs to the temple. The high priest Hilkiah finds the book of the law there. The scribe Shaphan reads it to the king, and Josiah tears his clothes. He sends five officials to ask the LORD about it. They go to the prophetess Huldah in Jerusalem. She says the book’s disaster will come on the city. Because Josiah humbled himself, he will not see it.

verse.text: So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe (now she lived in Jerusalem in the second quarter); and they talked with her.

2-kings-23.summary: Josiah reads the book of the covenant to all the people and renews the covenant. He removes Baal’s vessels and the Asherah pole from the temple. He defiles the high places from Geba to Beersheba. He destroys the altar at Bethel, as a man of God had foretold. He orders a Passover such as had not been kept since the judges. No king before him turned to the LORD as he did. Still the LORD’s anger against Judah remains. Pharaoh Necoh kills Josiah at Megiddo, and Egypt chooses the next king.

verse.text: Notwithstanding, the LORD didn’t turn from the fierceness of his great wrath, with which his anger burned against Judah, because of all the provocation with which Manasseh had provoked him.

2-kings-24.summary: Jehoiakim serves Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon for three years and then rebels. Raiders attack Judah, as the prophets had said. His son Jehoiachin rules three months. Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem, and the young king surrenders. Babylon takes the treasures of the temple and palace. Ten thousand people go into exile, including the king and his mother. Only the poorest remain in the land. Babylon makes Zedekiah king, and he too rebels.

verse.text: He carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valor, even ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and the smiths. No one remained except the poorest people of the land.

routes.title: Babylon takes treasure and deports Jehoiachin

2-kings-25.summary: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem for about two years, and famine grips the city. The wall is breached, and Zedekiah flees by night. He is caught, his sons are killed before him, and he is blinded. A month later the Babylonians burn the temple, the palace, and the houses. They break down the walls and carry off the bronze. Gedaliah is made governor and is soon murdered. The remaining people flee to Egypt. Years later Babylon’s new king frees Jehoiachin and feeds him at his table.

verse.text: In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, released Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison,

routes.title: Jerusalem is destroyed and a prisoner receives favor

1-chronicles-10.summary: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa. Saul’s three sons are killed, and archers wound him. He falls on his own sword. The Philistines strip him and put his head in the temple of Dagon. Men of Jabesh Gilead take the bodies and bury them. The writer says Saul died for his unfaithfulness. He did not keep the LORD’s word, and he consulted a medium. So the LORD gave the kingdom to David.

verse.text: and didn’t inquire of the LORD. Therefore he killed him, and turned the kingdom over to David the son of Jesse.

routes.title: Jabesh Gilead brings back the bodies

1-chronicles-11.summary: All Israel comes to Hebron and anoints David king. He captures Jebus, which is Jerusalem. Joab goes up first and becomes commander. The chapter then lists David’s mighty men. One stood his ground in a barley field against the Philistines. Three broke through enemy lines to bring David water from Bethlehem. Abishai and Benaiah are praised for their deeds. A long list of warriors follows, and it includes Uriah the Hittite.

verse.text: and said, “My God forbid me, that I should do this! Shall I drink the blood of these men who have put their lives in jeopardy?” For they risked their lives to bring it. Therefore he would not drink it. The three mighty men did these things.

routes.title: Three men fetch water from Bethlehem

1-chronicles-12.summary: Fighting men join David while he hides from Saul at Ziklag. Some are from Benjamin, Saul’s own tribe. Men of Gad cross the Jordan in flood to reach him. The Spirit moves Amasai to pledge loyalty and peace to David. More men desert to him from Manasseh. At Hebron every tribe sends armed men to make him king. They feast with David for three days. Neighbors from far in the north bring food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen.

verse.text: Moreover those who were near to them, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought bread on donkeys, on camels, on mules, and on oxen: supplies of flour, cakes of figs, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance; for there was joy in Israel.

routes.title: Fighters gather at Ziklag and Hebron

1-chronicles-13.summary: David consults his commanders and the whole assembly about the ark. All agree to bring it from Kiriath Jearim. They carry it on a new cart with music and singing. At a threshing floor the oxen stumble. Uzza puts out his hand to steady the ark, and God strikes him dead. David is angry and then afraid. He leaves the ark at the house of Obed-Edom. The LORD blesses that household for three months.

verse.text: David was afraid of God that day, saying, “How can I bring God’s ark home to me?”

routes.title: The ark sets out from Kiriath Jearim

1-chronicles-14.summary: King Hiram of Tyre sends cedar and builders for David’s house. David sees that the LORD has established him for Israel’s sake. He takes more wives and has more children in Jerusalem. The Philistines raid the Valley of Rephaim. David asks God, attacks, and wins. The Philistines raid the same valley again. David asks again and is told to circle behind them. He waits for the sound of marching in the trees and wins.

verse.text: David inquired again of God; and God said to him, “You shall not go up after them. Turn away from them, and come on them opposite the mulberry trees.

routes.title: David strikes from Gibeon to Gezer

1-chronicles-15.summary: David prepares a tent for the ark in Jerusalem. He says only Levites may carry it. He gathers the priests and Levites and tells them to make themselves holy. They carry the ark on poles on their shoulders, as Moses commanded. David appoints singers and players of cymbals, harps, and lyres. God helps the Levites, and they offer sacrifices. All Israel brings up the ark with shouting and trumpets. Michal sees David dancing and despises him.

verse.text: For because you didn’t carry it at first, the LORD our God broke out in anger against us, because we didn’t seek him according to the ordinance.”

1-chronicles-16.summary: The ark is set in its tent, and David offers sacrifices. He gives every person bread, meat, and raisins. He appoints Levites to thank and praise the LORD before the ark. Asaph and his brothers sing a psalm of thanks. It calls the nations to praise and recalls the covenant with Abraham. The people answer, “Amen.” David leaves Asaph to serve before the ark every day. Zadok and the priests offer the daily sacrifices at the tabernacle in Gibeon.

verse.text: So he left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the LORD’s covenant, to minister before the ark continually, as every day’s work required;

1-chronicles-17.summary: David tells Nathan that he lives in cedar while the ark sits in a tent. Nathan tells him to do what is in his heart. That night God gives Nathan a different message. David will not build the house. God took him from the sheep and will build him a house instead. A son will build the temple, and his throne will last forever. David sits before the LORD and asks who he is to receive this. He prays that God will do as he has said.

verse.text: “Go and tell David my servant, ‘The LORD says, “You shall not build me a house to dwell in;

1-chronicles-18.summary: David defeats the Philistines and takes Gath. He defeats Moab, and the Moabites bring tribute. He defeats Hadadezer of Zobah and the Syrians who come to help. He takes gold shields and a great amount of bronze. Solomon later uses that bronze for the temple. King Tou of Hamath sends gifts. David dedicates all the silver and gold to the LORD. Abishai defeats Edom, and the chapter lists David’s officers.

verse.text: King David also dedicated these to the LORD, with the silver and the gold that he carried away from all the nations: from Edom, from Moab, from the children of Ammon, from the Philistines, and from Amalek.

1-chronicles-19.summary: The king of Ammon dies, and David sends men to comfort his son Hanun. Hanun’s princes say the men have come to spy. Hanun shaves them and cuts off their clothes at the hips. David tells the shamed men to wait at Jericho. Ammon hires chariots and horsemen from Syria for a thousand talents of silver. Joab and Abishai fight on two fronts and win. The Syrians bring more troops from beyond the River. David defeats them, and they make peace.

verse.text: But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun, “Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Haven’t his servants come to you to search, to overthrow, and to spy out the land?”

1-chronicles-20.summary: In spring Joab leads the army against Ammon and besieges Rabbah. David stays in Jerusalem. Joab takes the city. David takes the heavy gold crown of its king and much plunder. He puts the people to work with saws, picks, and axes. Later wars with the Philistines follow. David’s men kill three giants, one of them Goliath’s brother. One giant has six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.

verse.text: At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab led out the army and wasted the country of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah, and overthrew it.

1-chronicles-21.summary: Satan moves David to count Israel. Joab objects but obeys, and he leaves out Levi and Benjamin. God is displeased and strikes Israel. The prophet Gad offers David three punishments. David chooses to fall into the LORD’s hand. A plague kills seventy thousand. David sees the angel standing over Jerusalem with a drawn sword. He buys Ornan’s threshing floor, builds an altar, and fire from heaven answers him.

verse.text: David said to God, “Isn’t it I who commanded the people to be counted? It is even I who have sinned and done very wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand, O LORD my God, be against me and against my father’s house; but not against your people, that they should be plagued.”

1-chronicles-22.summary: David says the threshing floor is the place for God’s house. He gathers stonecutters and stores up iron, bronze, and cedar. Solomon is young, so David prepares in great quantity. He tells Solomon that he wanted to build the house himself. The LORD refused because David had shed much blood. A son named Solomon, a man of rest, would build it. David hands over gold, silver, and workers. He orders Israel’s leaders to help his son.

verse.text: But the LORD’s word came to me, saying, ‘You have shed blood abundantly and have made great wars. You shall not build a house to my name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in my sight.

1-chronicles-23.summary: David is old and makes Solomon king. He counts the Levites aged thirty and above. There are thirty-eight thousand. Most will oversee the work of the LORD’s house. Others will be officers, judges, gatekeepers, and musicians. The families of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari are listed. The Levites will no longer carry the tabernacle. They will help the priests with courts, rooms, bread, flour, measures, and daily praise.

verse.text: Also the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all its vessels for its service.”

1-chronicles-24.summary: David organizes the priests, the sons of Aaron. Eleazar’s family has sixteen heads, and Ithamar’s has eight. They are divided by lot, since both families have leaders. A Levite scribe records the result before the king and the priests. Twenty-four divisions are named in order. The eighth lot falls to Abijah. The remaining Levites also cast lots for their duties. The chief’s household and the youngest brother’s are treated alike.

verse.text: These likewise cast lots even as their brothers the sons of Aaron in the presence of David the king, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites, the fathers’ households of the chief even as those of his younger brother.

1-chronicles-25.summary: David and his commanders set apart musicians for the temple. They come from the families of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun. They are to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals. Heman has fourteen sons and three daughters. All serve under their fathers’ direction. There are two hundred eighty-eight trained singers. They cast lots for their duties. Twenty-four groups of twelve are listed in order.

verse.text: They cast lots for their offices, all alike, the small as well as the great, the teacher as well as the student.

1-chronicles-26.summary: The chapter lists the gatekeepers by family. Obed-Edom has sixty-two able descendants, for God blessed him. One father makes a younger son chief. Lots decide which family guards each gate. Guards are posted daily on every side. Other Levites keep the treasuries and the dedicated gifts. These gifts include spoil given by Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab. Still others serve as officers and judges across Israel.

verse.text: Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God’s house and over the treasures of the dedicated things.

1-chronicles-27.summary: The chapter lists the army’s twelve divisions. Each has twenty-four thousand men and serves one month a year. A leader is named for each tribe. David did not count those under twenty, since God promised many descendants. Stewards manage the king’s storehouses, fields, vineyards, and olive trees. Others manage herds, camels, donkeys, and flocks. Two of these stewards are foreigners. The king’s counselors are named last.

verse.text: Now the children of Israel after their number, the heads of fathers’ households and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in any matter of the divisions which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year—of every division were twenty-four thousand.

1-chronicles-28.summary: David gathers Israel’s leaders in Jerusalem and stands to speak. He wanted to build a house for the ark. God refused him as a man of war and chose Solomon. David charges Solomon to know God and serve him with a whole heart. He gives him the plans for every room and court. He gives the weights of gold and silver for each lampstand, table, and bowl. He says all of it came in writing from the LORD’s hand. He tells Solomon to be strong and do the work.

verse.text: David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed, for the LORD God, even my God, is with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of the LORD’s house is finished.

1-chronicles-29.summary: David tells the assembly what he has given for the temple from his own treasure. The leaders give gold, silver, bronze, iron, and precious stones. The people rejoice because the gifts are given freely. David blesses the LORD before them all. He says everything in heaven and earth belongs to God. He asks God to keep the people’s hearts loyal and to help Solomon. Solomon is made king, and Zadok priest. David dies at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor.

verse.text: But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and we have given you of your own.

2-chronicles-1.summary: Solomon is established as king, and God is with him. He leads the assembly to Gibeon, where the tent of meeting stands. He offers a thousand burnt offerings on the bronze altar. That night God tells him to ask for whatever he wants. Solomon asks for wisdom and knowledge to lead the people. God gives him that, with riches and honor besides. Solomon gathers chariots and horsemen. He buys horses from Egypt and makes silver common in Jerusalem.

verse.text: Now give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people; for who can judge this great people of yours?”

2-chronicles-2.summary: Solomon decides to build a house for the LORD’s name and a palace. He writes to Huram king of Tyre for cedar and a master craftsman. He admits that even the highest heaven cannot contain God. He offers wheat, barley, wine, and oil for Tyre’s woodcutters. Huram praises the LORD and sends a craftsman of mixed descent. The logs will come by sea to Joppa. Solomon counts the foreigners living in Israel. He makes them carriers, stonecutters, and overseers.

verse.text: Solomon counted all the foreigners who were in the land of Israel, after the census with which David his father had counted them; and they found one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred.

2-chronicles-3.summary: Solomon begins to build the LORD’s house in Jerusalem. The site is Mount Moriah, at the threshing floor of Ornan. He starts in the fourth year of his reign. The main room is overlaid with fine gold and set with precious stones. The inner room holds two great cherubim whose wings span the width. A veil of blue, purple, and crimson hangs before it. Two tall pillars stand in front of the house. They are named Jachin and Boaz.

verse.text: Then Solomon began to build the LORD’s house at Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared to David his father, which he prepared in the place that David had appointed, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

2-chronicles-4.summary: Solomon makes a bronze altar twenty cubits square. He makes the great basin called the sea, resting on twelve oxen. He makes ten smaller basins and ten gold lampstands. He makes ten tables and a hundred gold bowls. He builds a court for the priests and a great outer court. Huram finishes the pots, shovels, pillars, and stands. The bronze is too much to weigh. The gold altar, tables, lamps, and doors complete the furnishings.

verse.text: He also made ten basins, and put five on the right hand and five on the left, to wash in them. The things that belonged to the burnt offering were washed in them, but the sea was for the priests to wash in.

2-chronicles-5.summary: The temple is finished, and Solomon brings in David’s dedicated treasures. The elders gather in Jerusalem at the feast. Levites carry the ark, and the king offers more sacrifices than can be counted. The priests set the ark under the cherubim’s wings. Only the two stone tablets are in it. Singers in fine linen stand with a hundred twenty priests blowing trumpets. They praise the LORD together, for his kindness lasts forever. A cloud fills the house, and the priests cannot stand to serve.

verse.text: when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD; and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, saying, “For he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever!” then the house was filled with a cloud, even the LORD’s house,

2-chronicles-6.summary: Solomon blesses the people and recalls the promise to David. He kneels on a bronze platform and spreads his hands. He says heaven cannot contain God, much less this house. He asks God to hear prayers made toward this place. He names sin, defeat, drought, famine, and sickness. He prays for the foreigner who comes from far away. He prays for Israel in battle and in exile. He asks God to arise and come to his resting place.

verse.text: “Moreover, concerning the foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, when he comes from a far country for your great name’s sake and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm, when they come and pray toward this house,

2-chronicles-7.summary: When Solomon finishes praying, fire from heaven burns up the offerings. The LORD’s glory fills the house, and the people bow to the ground. The king and people offer thousands of animals. They keep the feast for seven days and the dedication for seven more. The LORD appears to Solomon at night. He promises to hear and heal the land when his people humble themselves and pray. If they turn to other gods, he will uproot them. The house will become a warning to all who pass.

verse.text: But if you turn away and forsake my statutes and my commandments which I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and worship them,

2-chronicles-8.summary: Solomon spends twenty years building the temple and his palace. He rebuilds towns and settles Israelites in them. He fortifies cities for stores, chariots, and horsemen. The remaining Canaanite peoples are made forced laborers. He moves Pharaoh’s daughter out of David’s city. He offers sacrifices on the days and feasts that Moses commanded. He sets the priests, Levites, and gatekeepers in the order David gave. His ships sail with Huram’s sailors and bring gold from Ophir.

verse.text: even as the duty of every day required, offering according to the commandment of Moses on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts, three times per year, during the feast of unleavened bread, during the feast of weeks, and during the feast of booths.

2-chronicles-9.summary: The queen of Sheba comes to test Solomon with hard questions. He answers all of them. She sees his house, his table, his servants, and his offerings. She says the report did not tell half of his wisdom. She blesses God, who set him on God’s throne to do justice. She gives gold, spices, and precious stones and returns home. Solomon’s gold, ivory throne, and trading ships are described. He rules forty years and dies.

verse.text: Happy are your men, and happy are these your servants, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom.

routes.title: The queen of Sheba comes to Jerusalem

2-chronicles-10.summary: Rehoboam goes to Shechem, where all Israel has come to make him king. Jeroboam and the people ask him to lighten his father’s heavy yoke. He asks for three days. The old men who served Solomon advise kindness. He rejects their advice and asks the young men he grew up with. They tell him to promise a heavier yoke. He answers the people harshly. Israel rejects David’s house, and only Judah’s towns stay with him.

verse.text: They spoke to him, saying, “If you are kind to these people, please them, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever.”

2-chronicles-10.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 975–957 BC.

2-chronicles-11.summary: Rehoboam gathers one hundred eighty thousand soldiers to win back Israel. The prophet Shemaiah brings the LORD’s word against the war. The army listens and goes home. Rehoboam fortifies fifteen cities in Judah and Benjamin. Priests and Levites leave their lands in the north and come to Jerusalem. Jeroboam had removed them and made his own priests. Others who seek the LORD follow them. For three years they strengthen Rehoboam, and his family grows large.

verse.text: ‘The LORD says, “You shall not go up, nor fight against your brothers! Every man return to his house; for this thing is of me.” ’ ” So they listened to the LORD’s words, and returned from going against Jeroboam.

2-chronicles-11.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 975–957 BC.

2-chronicles-12.summary: When Rehoboam’s rule is strong, he and all Israel abandon the LORD’s law. In his fifth year Shishak king of Egypt attacks Jerusalem. Shemaiah says they left the LORD, so he has left them to Shishak. The king and the leaders humble themselves and say the LORD is right. The LORD grants some rescue and does not destroy them. Shishak takes the treasures of the temple and palace. Rehoboam replaces Solomon’s gold shields with bronze. He rules seventeen years in all.

verse.text: Nevertheless they will be his servants, that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.”

2-chronicles-12.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 975–957 BC.

2-chronicles-13.summary: Abijah king of Judah goes to war against Jeroboam. Judah’s army is half the size of Israel’s. Abijah stands on a hill and speaks to the northern army. He says God gave the kingdom to David’s sons. He says the north has golden calves and has driven out the LORD’s priests. Jeroboam sets an ambush behind Judah. Judah cries to the LORD, and the priests blow the trumpets. God defeats Israel, and Abijah takes Bethel and other towns.

verse.text: Behold, God is with us at our head, and his priests with the trumpets of alarm to sound an alarm against you. Children of Israel, don’t fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers; for you will not prosper.”

2-chronicles-13.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 957–955 BC.

2-chronicles-14.summary: Asa does what is good and right. He removes foreign altars and tells Judah to seek the LORD. The land has ten years of peace. He builds walled cities and trains a large army. Zerah the Cushite comes against him with a far greater force. Asa prays that the LORD helps the weak as easily as the strong. The LORD strikes the Cushites, and they flee. Judah carries home much plunder, with sheep and camels.

verse.text: Asa cried to the LORD his God, and said, “LORD, there is no one besides you to help, between the mighty and him who has no strength. Help us, LORD our God; for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this multitude. LORD, you are our God. Don’t let man prevail against you.”

2-chronicles-14.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 955–914 BC.

2-chronicles-15.summary: God’s Spirit comes on Azariah, who meets Asa after the victory. He says the LORD is with them while they are with him. Israel once lived long without a teaching priest or law. Asa takes courage and removes idols from the land. He repairs the LORD’s altar. Many come to him from the northern tribes. The people swear a covenant with shouting and trumpets and great joy. Asa even removes his grandmother from her position for her idol.

verse.text: When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominations out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from the hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed the LORD’s altar that was before the LORD’s porch.

2-chronicles-15.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 955–914 BC.

2-chronicles-16.summary: Baasha king of Israel fortifies Ramah to shut Judah in. Asa sends temple and palace treasure to the king of Syria. Syria attacks Israel’s northern towns, and Baasha stops building. The seer Hanani tells Asa he relied on Syria and not on the LORD. He reminds him of the victory over the Cushites. From now on Asa will have wars. Asa puts the seer in prison and mistreats some of the people. Late in life his feet are diseased, and he seeks only physicians.

verse.text: Then Asa was angry with the seer, and put him in the prison; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. Asa oppressed some of the people at the same time.

2-chronicles-16.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 955–914 BC.

2-chronicles-17.summary: Jehoshaphat becomes king and strengthens Judah against Israel. He follows the ways of David and does not seek the Baals. The LORD establishes his kingdom, and he grows rich. In his third year he sends officials, Levites, and priests through Judah. They carry the book of the LORD’s law and teach in every city. Fear of the LORD falls on the nearby kingdoms. Philistines and Arabs bring him tribute. He builds forts and keeps a large army.

verse.text: They taught in Judah, having the book of the LORD’s law with them. They went about throughout all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.

2-chronicles-17.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 914–893 BC.

2-chronicles-18.summary: Jehoshaphat is rich and allied to Ahab by marriage. Ahab asks him to help retake Ramoth Gilead. Four hundred prophets promise victory. Jehoshaphat asks for another, and Micaiah is called. Micaiah sees Israel scattered and describes a lying spirit in the prophets’ mouths. Ahab jails him and goes to battle in disguise. The enemy surrounds Jehoshaphat, and he cries out and is spared. A random arrow strikes Ahab, and he dies at sunset.

verse.text: The messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “Behold, the words of the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth. Let your word therefore, please be like one of theirs, and speak good.”

routes.title: Two kings go up to Ramoth Gilead

2-chronicles-18.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 914–893 BC.

2-chronicles-19.summary: Jehoshaphat returns safely, and the seer Jehu rebukes him for helping the wicked. Yet some good is found in him. The king travels among the people and brings them back to the LORD. He appoints judges in every fortified city. He tells them they judge for the LORD, not for man. In Jerusalem he sets up a court of Levites, priests, and family heads. The chief priest leads in the LORD’s matters. A leader of Judah handles the king’s matters.

verse.text: Now therefore let the fear of the LORD be on you. Take heed and do it; for there is no iniquity with the LORD our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of bribes.”

2-chronicles-19.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 914–893 BC.

2-chronicles-20.summary: A great army from Moab, Ammon, and Mount Seir comes against Judah. Jehoshaphat is afraid and calls a fast. All Judah gathers with wives and children. The king prays and admits they have no strength and no plan. The Spirit comes on Jahaziel, a Levite, who says the battle is God’s. Next morning singers march ahead of the army giving thanks. The enemy armies turn on one another. Judah gathers plunder for three days and blesses the LORD.

verse.text: Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no might against this great company that comes against us. We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”

2-chronicles-20.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 914–893 BC.

2-chronicles-21.summary: Jehoshaphat gives his sons gifts and cities and leaves the kingdom to Jehoram. Jehoram kills all his brothers and some of the princes. He marries Ahab’s daughter and follows Israel’s kings. The LORD spares David’s house because of the covenant. Edom and Libnah revolt. A letter from Elijah says Jehoram will die of disease. Raiders carry off his goods, wives, and sons. He dies in great pain, and no one regrets his death.

verse.text: Now when Jehoram had risen up over the kingdom of his father, and had strengthened himself, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Israel.

2-chronicles-21.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 893–878 BC.

2-chronicles-22.summary: Ahaziah becomes king of Judah. His mother Athaliah advises him to do evil. He joins Israel’s king in war and visits him at Jezreel. Jehu, who is destroying Ahab’s house, kills Ahaziah too. Athaliah then kills the royal children of Judah. Jehoshabeath, the king’s daughter, steals away the baby Joash. She hides him and his nurse in a bedroom. He stays hidden in God’s house for six years while Athaliah rules.

verse.text: But Jehoshabeath, the king’s daughter, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stealthily rescued him from among the king’s sons who were slain, and put him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest (for she was the sister of Ahaziah), hid him from Athaliah, so that she didn’t kill him.

2-chronicles-22.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 893–878 BC.

2-chronicles-23.summary: In the seventh year the priest Jehoiada makes a pact with the guard captains. They gather Levites and family heads from all Judah. Guards surround the young king with weapons from the temple. They crown Joash, hand him the testimony, and shout. Athaliah cries treason and is put to death outside the temple. Jehoiada makes a covenant with the people and the king. They tear down Baal’s temple. Gatekeepers are posted, and the city is quiet.

verse.text: Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, all the people, and the king, that they should be the LORD’s people.

2-chronicles-23.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 893–878 BC.

2-chronicles-24.summary: Joash does right all the days of the priest Jehoiada. He collects money in a chest and repairs the temple. Jehoiada dies very old and is buried among the kings. Then Judah’s princes persuade the king to leave the LORD’s house. Prophets warn them, and they do not listen. The Spirit comes on Zechariah, Jehoiada’s son, who rebukes the people. At the king’s command they stone him in the temple court. A small Syrian army defeats Judah, and Joash’s servants kill him.

verse.text: Thus Joash the king didn’t remember the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him, but killed his son. When he died, he said, “May the LORD look at it, and repay it.”

2-chronicles-24.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 878–841 BC.

2-chronicles-25.summary: Amaziah does right, but not with a whole heart. He hires a hundred thousand soldiers from Israel. A man of God says to send them home, and he obeys at a loss. He defeats Edom and then worships Edom’s gods. A prophet asks why he seeks gods that could not save their own people. The king threatens him into silence. Amaziah challenges Israel’s king and is badly beaten. Jerusalem’s wall is broken, and he later dies by conspiracy.

verse.text: As he talked with him, the king said to him, “Have we made you one of the king’s counselors? Stop! Why should you be struck down?” Then the prophet stopped, and said, “I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel.”

2-chronicles-25.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 841–811 BC.

2-chronicles-26.summary: Uzziah becomes king at sixteen and rules fifty-two years. He seeks God, and God gives him success. He defeats the Philistines, builds towers, digs cisterns, and loves farming. His army is large and has new war machines. When he is strong, his heart grows proud. He enters the temple to burn incense on the altar. Eighty priests confront him, and he becomes angry. A skin disease breaks out on his forehead, and he lives apart until he dies.

verse.text: They resisted Uzziah the king, and said to him, “It isn’t for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have trespassed. It will not be for your honor from the LORD God.”

2-chronicles-26.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 811–758 BC.

2-chronicles-27.summary: Jotham becomes king at twenty-five and rules sixteen years. He does what is right, as his father Uzziah did. Unlike his father he does not enter the LORD’s temple. The people still act corruptly. He builds the upper gate of the temple and much on the city wall. He builds towns in the hills and forts in the forests. He defeats Ammon, which pays him tribute. He grows strong because he orders his ways before the LORD.

verse.text: He did that which was right in the LORD’s eyes, according to all that his father Uzziah had done. However he didn’t enter into the LORD’s temple. The people still acted corruptly.

2-chronicles-27.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–742 BC.

2-chronicles-28.summary: Ahaz makes idols and burns his children as offerings. Syria defeats him and takes captives. Israel’s king kills many of Judah’s soldiers and carries off women and children. The prophet Oded meets the army at Samaria. He says they have killed in rage and must not enslave their kin. Four leaders of Ephraim agree and stop the army. They clothe, feed, and carry the captives back to Jericho. Ahaz then seeks Assyria’s help, worships Syria’s gods, and shuts the temple.

verse.text: Now hear me therefore, and send back the captives that you have taken captive from your brothers, for the fierce wrath of the LORD is on you.”

routes.title: The captives are returned at Jericho

2-chronicles-28.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 742–726 BC.

2-chronicles-29.summary: Hezekiah opens the temple doors in the first month of his reign. He tells the priests and Levites to make themselves and the house holy. They carry out the filth and finish in sixteen days. The king and the city leaders bring sin offerings for all Israel. Levites play the instruments David appointed, and the assembly bows. The people bring so many offerings that the priests need help. The Levites assist them. Hezekiah and the people rejoice at how quickly it was done.

verse.text: Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced because of that which God had prepared for the people; for the thing was done suddenly.

2-chronicles-29.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 726–697 BC.

2-chronicles-30.summary: Hezekiah invites all Israel and Judah to keep the Passover in Jerusalem. It is held in the second month because the priests were not ready. Couriers carry letters north to Ephraim and Manasseh. Many laugh at them, but some humble themselves and come. Many who come have not made themselves clean. They eat anyway, and Hezekiah prays for their pardon. The LORD hears him and heals the people. The feast is so glad that they keep it seven more days.

verse.text: For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet they ate the Passover other than the way it is written. For Hezekiah had prayed for them, saying, “May the good LORD pardon everyone

2-chronicles-30.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 726–697 BC.

2-chronicles-31.summary: After the feast the people break down the idols and altars across the land. Hezekiah sets the priests and Levites in their turns of service. He gives from his own herds for the regular offerings. He tells the people to give the priests’ and Levites’ share. They bring grain, wine, oil, and honey in heaps for four months. The chief priest says there is enough and plenty left over. Storerooms are prepared and keepers named. Men are chosen to hand out portions fairly in every town.

verse.text: and those who were listed by genealogy of all their little ones, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, through all the congregation; for in their office of trust they sanctified themselves in holiness.

2-chronicles-31.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 726–697 BC.

2-chronicles-32.summary: Sennacherib of Assyria invades Judah and camps against its walled cities. Hezekiah stops the springs outside Jerusalem and repairs the wall. He makes weapons and tells the people that a greater one is with them. Assyrian officers shout insults at the people on the wall. Hezekiah and Isaiah cry to heaven. An angel destroys the Assyrian commanders, and Sennacherib goes home in shame. Later Hezekiah is sick, grows proud, and humbles himself. He also brings water down to the west side of David’s city.

verse.text: He took courage, built up all the wall that was broken down, and raised it up to the towers, with the other wall outside, and strengthened Millo in David’s city, and made weapons and shields in abundance.

2-chronicles-32.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 726–697 BC.

2-chronicles-33.summary: Manasseh rules fifty-five years and does great evil. He rebuilds the high places and sets an idol in God’s house. He burns his sons, uses sorcery, and ignores every warning. Assyrian commanders capture him and take him to Babylon in chains. In distress he humbles himself and prays. God hears and brings him back to Jerusalem. He removes the idols and repairs the LORD’s altar. His son Amon does evil, does not humble himself, and is killed.

verse.text: When he was in distress, he begged the LORD his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.

2-chronicles-34.summary: Josiah becomes king at eight. At sixteen he begins to seek God, and at twenty he clears away the idols. He carries the reform into the northern lands. In his eighteenth year he repairs the temple with honest workmen. While the money is brought out, the priest Hilkiah finds the book of the law. The king hears it and tears his clothes. His officials consult the prophetess Huldah, who confirms the coming disaster. Josiah gathers the people and renews the covenant.

verse.text: So Hilkiah and those whom the king had commanded went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe (now she lived in Jerusalem in the second quarter), and they spoke to her to that effect.

2-chronicles-35.summary: Josiah keeps the Passover in Jerusalem on the proper day. He sets the priests and Levites in their places. He and his officials give thousands of animals for the people. No Passover like it had been kept since Samuel’s time. Later Pharaoh Neco marches north to fight at Carchemish. Josiah goes out against him. Neco says God sent him and warns Josiah to turn back. Josiah fights in disguise, is shot by archers, and dies in Jerusalem.

verse.text: Nevertheless Josiah would not turn his face from him, but disguised himself, that he might fight with him, and didn’t listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God, and came to fight in the valley of Megiddo.

2-chronicles-36.summary: Judah’s last four kings rule under Egypt and then Babylon. Zedekiah will not humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah. He breaks an oath he swore by God to Nebuchadnezzar. The LORD sends messengers again and again, out of pity for his people. They mock the prophets until there is no remedy. The Babylonians kill, burn the temple, and break down Jerusalem’s wall. The survivors become servants in Babylon for seventy years. Then Cyrus king of Persia permits the people to go up and rebuild.

verse.text: “Cyrus king of Persia says, ‘The LORD, the God of heaven, has given all the kingdoms of the earth to me; and he has commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever there is among you of all his people, the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up.’ ”

routes.title: Cyrus calls the people to go up

ezra-1.summary: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the LORD stirs the king’s spirit. Cyrus sends a written order through his kingdom. He says the God of heaven has told him to build a house in Jerusalem. Any of God’s people may go up and build it. Their neighbors are to help with silver, gold, goods, and animals. Family heads, priests, and Levites prepare to go. Cyrus brings out the temple vessels that Nebuchadnezzar took. They are counted out to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.

verse.text: Whoever there is among you of all his people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel (he is God), which is in Jerusalem.

routes.title: The captives go up from Babylon

ezra-1.dateDetail: Ezra 6 ends a few years later, when the temple is finished.

ezra-2.summary: This chapter lists the people who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and Jeshua. Families are counted by ancestor and by home town. Priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants follow. Some families cannot prove that they belong to Israel. Some priests cannot find their family records. The governor bars them from the holy food until a priest can decide. The whole company numbers 42,360, with servants and singers besides. Family heads give gold, silver, and priestly garments for the work.

verse.text: These sought their place among those who were registered by genealogy, but they were not found; therefore they were deemed disqualified and removed from the priesthood.

ezra-2.dateDetail: Ezra 6 ends a few years later, when the temple is finished.

ezra-3.summary: In the seventh month the people gather in Jerusalem as one. Jeshua and Zerubbabel build the altar on its old base. They fear the neighboring peoples and offer sacrifices morning and evening. They keep the Feast of Booths before any foundation is laid. They pay masons and carpenters and order cedar from Lebanon. In the second year the builders lay the temple’s foundation. Priests blow trumpets, and Levites sing that the LORD is good. Old men who saw the first house weep while others shout for joy.

verse.text: But many of the priests and Levites and heads of fathers’ households, the old men who had seen the first house, when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, wept with a loud voice. Many also shouted aloud for joy,

ezra-3.dateDetail: Ezra 6 ends a few years later, when the temple is finished.

ezra-4.summary: Neighbors of Judah and Benjamin offer to help build the temple. Zerubbabel and the leaders refuse. The neighbors then discourage the builders and hire advisers against them. This continues from the reign of Cyrus to that of Darius. Later, officials write to King Artaxerxes about Jerusalem’s walls. They call it a rebellious city that will stop paying taxes. The king searches the records and orders the building to stop. Work on God’s house ceases until the second year of Darius.

verse.text: Make a decree now to cause these men to cease, and that this city not be built until a decree is made by me.

ezra-4.dateDetail: Ezra 6 ends a few years later, when the temple is finished.

ezra-5.summary: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah speak to the Jews in God’s name. Zerubbabel and Jeshua begin again to build the house. Tattenai, the governor west of the River, asks who authorized them. He takes down the builders’ names. The work continues while he writes to King Darius. His letter reports the elders’ answer in full. They say Cyrus ordered the house rebuilt and returned its vessels. Tattenai asks the king to search the royal archives.

verse.text: Thus they returned us answer, saying, “We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth and are building the house that was built these many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and finished.

routes.title: A letter asks for a search

ezra-5.dateDetail: Ezra 6 ends a few years later, when the temple is finished.

ezra-6.summary: Darius orders a search of the archives. A scroll is found in the fortress of Achmetha in Media. It records Cyrus’s decree, with the temple’s size and the crown’s payment. Darius tells Tattenai to leave the work alone. He orders the costs paid from the region’s taxes. He supplies animals, wheat, salt, wine, and oil for the offerings. The elders finish the house in the sixth year of Darius. They dedicate it with joy and keep the Passover.

verse.text: A scroll was found at Achmetha, in the palace that is in the province of Media, and in it this was written for a record:

ezra-6.dateDetail: Ezra 6 ends a few years later, when the temple is finished.

ezra-7.summary: Years later Ezra comes up from Babylon. He is a priest of Aaron’s line and a scribe skilled in Moses’s law. King Artaxerxes grants all he asks. The journey takes about four months. The king’s letter lets any Israelite go with him. It sends silver and gold for offerings and frees temple workers from tax. It tells Ezra to appoint judges and teach God’s laws. Ezra blesses the LORD, who put this in the king’s heart.

verse.text: For Ezra had set his heart to seek the LORD’s law, and to do it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel.

ezra-8.summary: Ezra lists the family heads who travel with him. At the river Ahava he finds no Levites in the camp. He sends for some, and Levites and temple servants join. He calls a fast and asks God for a safe road. He is ashamed to ask the king for soldiers. He weighs the silver, gold, and vessels into the hands of twelve priests. They reach Jerusalem safely. On the fourth day everything is weighed again and written down.

verse.text: Watch and keep them until you weigh them before the chiefs of the priests, the Levites, and the princes of the fathers’ households of Israel at Jerusalem, in the rooms of the LORD’s house.”

routes.title: From the Ahava camp to Jerusalem

ezra-9.summary: Leaders tell Ezra that the people have married among the neighboring peoples. Priests, Levites, and officials are among them. Ezra tears his clothes and sits appalled until the evening offering. Then he kneels and prays. He says the people’s guilt has grown up to the heavens. God has given them a little relief and a foothold in his holy place. They are still servants under Persia’s kings. He asks how they can break the commandments again.

verse.text: For we are bondservants; yet our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but has extended loving kindness to us in the sight of the kings of Persia, to revive us, to set up the house of our God, and to repair its ruins, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.

ezra-10.summary: While Ezra prays and weeps, a large crowd gathers and weeps with him. Shecaniah proposes a covenant to send away the foreign wives and their children. Ezra makes the leaders swear to it. All the men are called to Jerusalem within three days. They sit in the open square, trembling in heavy rain. Family heads are chosen to examine each case. The work takes three months. The book ends with a list of the men, and some had children.

verse.text: Now therefore let’s make a covenant with our God to put away all the wives and those who are born of them, according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God. Let it be done according to the law.

nehemiah-1.summary: Nehemiah serves in the Persian fortress of Susa. His brother Hanani arrives with men from Judah. They report that the survivors are in great trouble. Jerusalem’s wall is broken, and its gates are burned. Nehemiah sits down and weeps, fasts, and prays for days. He confesses the sins of Israel, his family, and himself. He recalls God’s promise to gather those who return to him. He asks for favor before the king, whose cupbearer he is.

verse.text: Lord, I beg you, let your ear be attentive now to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayer of your servants who delight to fear your name; and please prosper your servant today, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man.” Now I was cup bearer to the king.

nehemiah-2.summary: Four months later Nehemiah serves wine to the king with a sad face. The king asks why, and Nehemiah is very afraid. He says his fathers’ city lies in ruins. He prays quickly and asks to be sent to rebuild it. He asks for letters to governors and for timber from the king’s forest. The king grants it and sends officers with him. In Jerusalem he inspects the walls by night. He tells the leaders, and they agree to build despite mockery.

verse.text: and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king’s forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel by the temple, for the wall of the city, and for the house that I will occupy.” The king granted my requests, because of the good hand of my God on me.

nehemiah-3.summary: The high priest and his fellow priests rebuild the Sheep Gate. The chapter then moves around the wall section by section. Each group is named with the part it repairs. Goldsmiths, perfume makers, and merchants work beside district rulers. One ruler repairs his section with his daughters. Many people repair the wall opposite their own houses. The men of Tekoa repair two sections. Their nobles, however, refuse to work.

verse.text: Next to them, the Tekoites made repairs; but their nobles didn’t put their necks to the Lord’s work.

nehemiah-4.summary: Sanballat and Tobiah mock the builders and their wall. Nehemiah prays, and the wall rises to half its height. The enemies plot to attack Jerusalem. The people pray and post a guard day and night. Workers grow tired, and neighbors warn of raids ten times. Nehemiah stations families with swords, spears, and bows. Half his men work while half hold weapons. A trumpeter stays beside him, and they work from dawn until the stars appear.

verse.text: Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, rally there to us. Our God will fight for us.”

nehemiah-5.summary: A great outcry rises from the people and their wives against fellow Jews. Some have pledged fields and houses to buy grain in the famine. Some have borrowed to pay the king’s tax. Their children are being sold as servants. Nehemiah is very angry and accuses the nobles of charging interest. He says the community has been buying back Jews sold abroad. The nobles are silent and then promise to restore everything. As governor Nehemiah refuses the food allowance and feeds many at his own cost.

verse.text: Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brothers, our children as their children. Behold, we bring our sons and our daughters into bondage to be servants, and some of our daughters have been brought into bondage. It is also not in our power to help it, because other men have our fields and our vineyards.”

nehemiah-6.summary: The wall is nearly finished, with only the gate doors missing. Sanballat and Geshem invite Nehemiah to a meeting four times, meaning harm. He answers that he is doing a great work and cannot come down. A fifth letter accuses him of planning to be king. A hired prophet urges him to hide inside the temple. Nehemiah refuses and sees the plot. The wall is finished in fifty-two days, and the enemies lose heart. Yet Judah’s nobles keep exchanging letters with Tobiah.

verse.text: Moreover in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah’s letters came to them.

nehemiah-7.summary: The wall is built, and the doors are hung. Nehemiah puts his brother Hanani and a trusted commander over Jerusalem. The gates are to stay shut until the sun is hot. Residents stand guard, each near his own house. The city is wide, but few people live in it. God moves Nehemiah to register the people by families. He finds the record of those who first returned. The list of families, numbers, and gifts follows.

verse.text: Now the city was wide and large; but the people were few therein, and the houses were not built.

nehemiah-8.summary: In the seventh month all the people gather at the Water Gate. They ask Ezra to bring the book of the law of Moses. He reads from early morning until noon on a wooden platform. Men, women, and all who can understand listen. Levites explain the reading, and the people weep. The leaders tell them not to grieve, since the day is holy. On the second day they read about the Feast of Booths. They build shelters of branches and keep the feast with great joy.

verse.text: They read in the book, in the law of God, distinctly; and they gave the sense, so that they understood the reading.

nehemiah-9.summary: On the twenty-fourth day the people fast in sackcloth. They read the law for a quarter of the day and confess for another quarter. The Levites lead a long prayer. It recalls creation, Abraham, Egypt, the sea, Sinai, and the manna. It admits that the fathers rebelled again and again. Each time God was merciful and did not abandon them. The prayer says God has been just and the people have done wrong. They are servants in their own land, so they make a written agreement.

verse.text: “Behold, we are servants today, and as for the land that you gave to our fathers to eat its fruit and its good, behold, we are servants in it.

nehemiah-10.summary: The agreement is sealed by Nehemiah, the priests, the Levites, and the leaders. The rest of the people join with an oath. They will not marry their children to the peoples of the land. They will not buy on the Sabbath, and they will cancel debts every seventh year. Each will pay a yearly sum for the temple’s service. They cast lots for bringing wood to the altar. They promise firstfruits and tithes for the priests and Levites. They say they will not neglect the house of their God.

verse.text: For the children of Israel and the children of Levi shall bring the wave offering of the grain, of the new wine, and of the oil, to the rooms where the vessels of the sanctuary are, and the priests who minister, with the gatekeepers and the singers. We will not forsake the house of our God.

nehemiah-11.summary: The leaders live in Jerusalem. The other people cast lots to bring one family in ten into the city. The other nine stay in their towns. The people bless those who volunteer to move. The chapter lists the families of Judah and Benjamin who settle there. It lists priests, Levites, gatekeepers, and singers. An official at the king’s side handles the people’s affairs. The villages of Judah and Benjamin are named last.

verse.text: The people blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves to dwell in Jerusalem.

nehemiah-12.summary: The chapter lists the priests and Levites from the first return onward. For the wall’s dedication the Levites and singers are gathered from their villages. Priests and Levites purify themselves, the people, the gates, and the wall. Two large choirs walk along the top of the wall in opposite directions. Ezra leads one, and Nehemiah follows the other. They meet at the temple and sing loudly. The people offer great sacrifices and rejoice. Men are appointed that day over the storerooms for offerings.

verse.text: They offered great sacrifices that day, and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy; and the women and the children also rejoiced, so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard even far away.

nehemiah-13.summary: The law is read, and the people separate from foreigners. Nehemiah has been away at the king’s court. On his return he finds Tobiah in a temple storeroom and throws him out. The Levites have not been paid and have gone back to their fields. Traders are selling on the Sabbath, so he shuts the gates. Jews have married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. He rebukes them harshly and drives out a priest’s son. He ends by asking God to remember him for good.

verse.text: I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given them, so that the Levites and the singers, who did the work, had each fled to his field.

esther-1.summary: King Ahasuerus rules one hundred twenty-seven provinces from India to Ethiopia. In his third year he displays his wealth for six months. He then gives a seven-day feast in the palace garden. Queen Vashti holds a feast for the women. On the seventh day the king, merry with wine, sends for her. She refuses to come. His advisers fear that all wives will now despise their husbands. A royal law removes Vashti and orders every man to rule his house.

verse.text: When the king’s decree which he shall make is published throughout all his kingdom (for it is great), all the wives will give their husbands honor, both great and small.”

esther-2.summary: The king’s servants propose gathering beautiful young women for him to choose from. Mordecai, a Jew of Benjamin, lives in Susa. He has raised his orphaned cousin Esther as a daughter. Esther is taken to the palace and wins the keeper’s favor. She does not reveal her people, as Mordecai told her. After a year of preparation she goes to the king. He loves her more than the others and makes her queen. Mordecai uncovers a plot to kill the king, and it is written in the records.

verse.text: Esther had not yet made known her relatives nor her people, as Mordecai had commanded her; for Esther obeyed Mordecai, like she did when she was brought up by him.

esther-3.summary: The king promotes Haman the Agagite above all the officials. Everyone at the gate bows to him except Mordecai. Haman learns Mordecai is a Jew and decides to destroy all Jews. He casts lots to choose a day. He tells the king that a certain people ignores the king’s laws. He offers a huge sum, and the king gives him his ring. Letters go to every province to kill all Jews on one day. The king and Haman sit down to drink, and Susa is confused.

verse.text: Then the king’s scribes were called in on the first month, on the thirteenth day of the month; and all that Haman commanded was written to the king’s local governors, and to the governors who were over every province, and to the princes of every people, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in their language. It was written in the name of King Ahasuerus, and it was sealed with the king’s ring.

esther-4.summary: Mordecai tears his clothes and wails in sackcloth at the king’s gate. Jews in every province fast and weep. Esther sends a servant to learn what has happened. Mordecai sends a copy of the decree and asks her to plead with the king. She answers that anyone who approaches unsummoned may die. Mordecai replies that she will not escape in the palace. Esther asks all the Jews of Susa to fast three days. She will go to the king: “If I perish, I perish.”

verse.text: For if you remain silent now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”

esther-5.summary: On the third day Esther puts on royal robes and stands in the inner court. The king holds out his golden scepter and offers her up to half the kingdom. She invites him and Haman to a banquet. At the banquet she invites them to a second one tomorrow. Haman leaves happy until he sees Mordecai, who will not rise. At home he boasts of his riches, sons, and honors. He says none of it satisfies him while Mordecai sits at the gate. His wife suggests a gallows fifty cubits high.

verse.text: Yet all this avails me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.”

esther-6.summary: That night the king cannot sleep and has the royal records read to him. He hears how Mordecai exposed the plot against him. He learns that Mordecai received nothing. Haman arrives to ask for Mordecai’s death. The king asks how to honor a man the king favors. Haman thinks this means himself and describes a royal robe and horse. The king tells him to do all this for Mordecai. Haman leads Mordecai through the city and goes home in mourning.

verse.text: On that night, the king couldn’t sleep. He commanded the book of records of the chronicles to be brought, and they were read to the king.

esther-7.summary: The king and Haman come to Esther’s second banquet. The king again asks what she wants. She asks for her life and the life of her people. They have been sold to be destroyed. The king asks who has dared to do this. Esther answers, “An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!” The king storms out and returns to find Haman fallen on Esther’s couch. Haman is hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai.

verse.text: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for male and female slaves, I would have held my peace, although the adversary could not have compensated for the king’s loss.”

esther-8.summary: The king gives Haman’s estate to Esther and his ring to Mordecai. Esther falls at the king’s feet and weeps. She begs him to cancel Haman’s letters. The king says a sealed decree cannot be reversed. He lets them write a new one in his name. It allows the Jews in every city to gather and defend their lives. Couriers ride out on royal horses. Mordecai leaves in royal robes, and Susa rejoices.

verse.text: Write also to the Jews as it pleases you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring; for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may not be reversed by any man.”

esther-9.summary: On the thirteenth day of Adar the Jews gather and strike those who attack them. Officials help them out of fear of Mordecai. In Susa they kill five hundred men and Haman’s ten sons. Esther asks for a second day in Susa. Across the provinces seventy-five thousand enemies die. The Jews take no plunder. They rest and feast on the next day. Mordecai and Esther write letters that make the feast of Purim yearly.

verse.text: as the days in which the Jews had rest from their enemies, and the month which was turned to them from sorrow to gladness, and from mourning into a holiday; that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, and of sending presents of food to one another, and gifts to the needy.

esther-10.summary: King Ahasuerus lays a tax on the land and the coasts. His acts of power are written in the royal records. The records also tell of the greatness of Mordecai. Mordecai the Jew is second to the king. He is great among the Jews and well liked by his many kin. He seeks the good of his people. He speaks peace to all their children.

verse.text: For Mordecai the Jew was next to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews and accepted by the multitude of his brothers, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his descendants.

psalms-2.summary: Nations and kings plot against the LORD and his anointed king. The one enthroned in heaven laughs at them. He says he has set his king on Zion, his holy hill. The king reports God’s decree: “You are my son.” The nations are promised to him as an inheritance. The poem then warns the kings of the earth to be wise. They should serve the LORD with fear. All who take refuge in him are blessed.

verse.text: Now therefore be wise, you kings. Be instructed, you judges of the earth.

psalms-2.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-8.summary: The poem begins and ends by praising the LORD’s majestic name. His glory is above the heavens. Even the mouths of infants serve as his strength. The speaker looks at the moon and the stars. He asks what a human being is that God should care. Yet God made humans a little lower than the heavenly beings. He crowned them with glory and honor. He put flocks, wild animals, birds, and fish under their care.

verse.text: what is man, that you think of him? What is the son of man, that you care for him?

psalms-8.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-9.summary: The speaker thanks the LORD with his whole heart. His enemies fell back when God judged from the throne. The LORD rules forever and judges the world rightly. He is a high tower for the oppressed. He does not forget the cry of the afflicted. The speaker asks to be lifted from the gates of death. Nations sink in the pit they dug. He asks God to let the nations know they are only human.

verse.text: For the needy shall not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.

psalms-9.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-14.summary: The fool says in his heart that there is no God. People are corrupt, and no one does good. The LORD looks down from heaven to see whether anyone seeks him. All have turned aside. Evildoers eat up God’s people as they eat bread. They do not call on the LORD. Yet God is with the righteous, and he is the refuge of the poor. The speaker longs for Israel’s rescue to come from Zion.

verse.text: Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and don’t call on the LORD?

psalms-14.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-20.summary: The people pray for their king before a battle. They ask the LORD to answer him in the day of trouble. They ask God to send help from the sanctuary and remember his offerings. They will shout for joy at his victory. A single voice says the LORD saves his anointed. Some trust in chariots and horses. The people trust in the name of the LORD. They ask the King to answer when they call.

verse.text: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.

psalms-20.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-22.summary: The speaker cries, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” He calls day and night and gets no answer. He recalls that his fathers trusted God and were rescued. People mock him and shake their heads. He is poured out like water, and his bones are out of joint. Men stare at him and cast lots for his clothing. He begs God not to be far away. Then he praises God, and the ends of the earth turn to the LORD.

verse.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, and from the words of my groaning?

psalms-22.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-48.summary: The LORD is great in the city of our God. Mount Zion is beautiful and is the joy of the whole earth. God has made himself known in her fortresses as a refuge. Kings gathered against her, saw her, and fled in panic. The people have heard of this, and now they have seen it. They think about God’s kindness inside his temple. They are told to walk around Zion and count her towers. They must tell the next generation that this God is their God.

verse.text: Notice her bulwarks. Consider her palaces, that you may tell it to the next generation.

psalms-48.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-50.summary: The heading names Asaph. God, the LORD, calls heaven and earth as witnesses while he judges his people. He does not fault their sacrifices. But he needs no bull from their stalls, since every animal is his. If he were hungry, he would not tell them. He asks for thanks, kept vows, and prayer in trouble. He rebukes the wicked who recite his laws and join with thieves. They thought he was like them, because he kept silent.

verse.text: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all that is in it.

psalms-50.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-51.summary: The heading sets this prayer after Nathan confronted David about Bathsheba. The speaker asks God for mercy and to blot out his wrongs. He knows his sin, and it is always before him. He asks to be washed whiter than snow. He asks God to create a clean heart in him. He asks not to be cast from God’s presence. Then he will teach other wrongdoers God’s ways. God wants a broken and humble heart more than a burnt offering.

verse.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.

psalms-51.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-53.summary: This poem is nearly the same as Psalm 14. The fool says in his heart that there is no God. People are corrupt, and no one does good. God looks down to see whether anyone seeks him. Everyone has turned away. Evildoers eat up God’s people like bread and never call on him. Then great terror falls on them where no terror was. The speaker longs for Israel’s rescue to come from Zion.

verse.text: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and don’t call on God?

psalms-53.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-56.summary: The heading says the Philistines seized David in Gath. The speaker asks for mercy, since men attack him all day. When he is afraid, he puts his trust in God. He asks what mere flesh can do to him. His enemies twist his words and watch his steps. He says God has counted his wanderings. God keeps his tears in a bottle and writes them in a book. He knows that God is for him.

verse.text: You count my wanderings. You put my tears into your container. Aren’t they in your book?

psalms-56.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-60.summary: The heading sets this prayer when David fought Aram and Joab struck Edom. The people say God has rejected them and broken their defenses. He has shaken the land and made them stagger. They ask him to save with his right hand. God has spoken: Shechem, Gilead, Ephraim, and Judah are his. Moab, Edom, and Philistia are under him. Yet God has not gone out with their armies. They ask for his help, since human help is worthless.

verse.text: Haven’t you, God, rejected us? You don’t go out with our armies, God.

psalms-60.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-65.summary: Praise waits for God in Zion. He hears prayer, and all people come to him. He forgives the sins that overwhelm them. He set the mountains in place and stills the roaring seas. He visits the earth and waters it. He drenches the furrows and softens the ground with showers. He crowns the year with goodness. The pastures and valleys are covered with flocks and grain, and they sing.

verse.text: You visit the earth, and water it. You greatly enrich it. The river of God is full of water. You provide them grain, for so you have ordained it.

psalms-65.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-68.summary: God rises, and his enemies scatter like smoke. The righteous sing to the one who rides through the deserts. He is a father to orphans and a defender of widows. He gives the lonely a home and leads prisoners out. He marched before his people, and Sinai shook. Kings and armies flee. A procession of singers, musicians, and young women enters the sanctuary. Kings bring gifts, and God gives strength to his people.

verse.text: A father of the fatherless, and a defender of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.

psalms-68.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-69.summary: The speaker cries that the waters have reached his neck. He sinks in deep mud, and his throat is dry from calling. Many hate him without cause. He bears insult for God’s sake and is a stranger to his brothers. People at the gate talk about him, and drunkards sing about him. Insult has broken his heart. He looked for pity and found none. He asks God to answer, and he promises a song of thanks.

verse.text: Reproach has broken my heart, and I am full of heaviness. I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; for comforters, but I found none.

psalms-69.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-74.summary: The heading names Asaph. The people ask God why he has rejected them. Enemies have ruined everything in the sanctuary. They hacked the carved wood with axes and burned the holy place. They burned every meeting place in the land. No signs are seen, no prophet remains, and no one knows how long. The people recall that God divided the sea and crushed the sea monsters. They ask him to remember his covenant and defend his cause.

verse.text: We see no miraculous signs. There is no longer any prophet, neither is there among us anyone who knows how long.

psalms-74.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.
