psalms-76.summary: The heading names Asaph. God is known in Judah, and his dwelling is in Zion. There he broke the flaming arrows, the shield, and the sword. Brave soldiers lay stunned, and at his rebuke horse and chariot fell still. No one can stand when he is angry. The earth feared and was quiet when God rose to judge. He rose to save all the afflicted of the earth. Rulers should bring gifts to the one who humbles princes.

verse.text: when God arose to judgment, to save all the afflicted ones of the earth. Selah.

psalms-76.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-78.summary: The heading names Asaph. The poet asks the people to listen, for fathers must tell children the LORD’s deeds. Then each generation will hope in God and not be stubborn. He recalls the sea, the cloud, water from the rock, and manna. The people still tested God and forgot his works. God was merciful and remembered that they were only flesh. He left Shiloh and let the ark be captured. He chose Judah, Mount Zion, and David the shepherd.

verse.text: that the generation to come might know, even the children who should be born; who should arise and tell their children,

psalms-78.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-79.summary: The heading names Asaph. The nations have invaded God’s land, defiled his temple, and left Jerusalem in ruins. The bodies of God’s servants are left for birds and animals. Neighbors mock the survivors. The people ask how long God will be angry. They ask him not to hold their earlier sins against them. They ask for help and forgiveness for the sake of his name. Then his people, his flock, will thank him forever.

verse.text: Help us, God of our salvation, for the glory of your name. Deliver us, and forgive our sins, for your name’s sake.

psalms-79.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-80.summary: The heading names Asaph. The people call on the Shepherd of Israel to shine and save them. Three times they ask God to restore them and let his face shine. He has fed them with tears. They recall that God brought a vine out of Egypt and planted it. It filled the land and shaded the mountains. Now its walls are broken, passersby pick its fruit, and a wild boar tears it. They ask God to look down and care for this vine.

verse.text: Turn again, we beg you, God of Armies. Look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vine,

psalms-80.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-81.summary: The heading names Asaph. The poem opens with a call to sing and play at the festival. Trumpets sound at the new moon, as Israel’s law requires, and then God speaks. He lifted the burden from Israel’s shoulder in Egypt. He tells his people to have no foreign god. He brought them out of Egypt and will fill their open mouths. But the people would not listen, so he let them follow their own plans. If they would listen, he would feed them with the finest wheat.

verse.text: I am the LORD, your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.

psalms-81.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-83.summary: The heading names Asaph. The people ask God not to stay silent. Enemies are plotting to wipe out Israel’s name. Ten peoples have joined together, from Edom and Moab to Tyre and Assyria. The people ask God to treat them as he treated Midian and Sisera. They ask that the enemies be like windblown dust and their faces filled with shame. Then they may seek his name. Let them know that the LORD alone is Most High.

verse.text: Fill their faces with confusion, that they may seek your name, LORD.

psalms-83.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-84.summary: The speaker loves the LORD’s dwelling and longs for its courts. Even the sparrow and the swallow have nests near God’s altars. Those who live in God’s house are blessed. So are those who set their hearts on the road to Zion. They pass through a dry valley and make it a place of springs. A day in God’s courts is better than a thousand elsewhere. The speaker would choose to be a doorkeeper there. The LORD is a sun and shield.

verse.text: For a day in your courts is better than a thousand. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.

psalms-84.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-87.summary: The LORD loves the gates of Zion, and glorious things are said of the city. God lists nations among those who know him. He names Egypt, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia. Of each one it is said, “This one was born there.” The Most High himself will establish Zion. When he registers the peoples, he records them as born in her. Singers and dancers say all their springs are in her.

verse.text: Yes, of Zion it will be said, “This one and that one was born in her;” the Most High himself will establish her.

psalms-87.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-89.summary: The heading names Ethan the Ezrahite. The poet sings of the LORD’s kindness and faithfulness. God swore that David’s line and throne would last forever. The heavens praise him, and justice is the base of his throne. If David’s sons sin, God will punish them and still keep his kindness. Then the poem turns. God has rejected his anointed and thrown the crown in the dust. Walls are broken, enemies rejoice, and the poet asks where the former kindness is.

verse.text: Lord, where are your former loving kindnesses, which you swore to David in your faithfulness?

psalms-89.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-97.summary: The LORD reigns, and the earth should be glad. Clouds and darkness surround him. Justice is the base of his throne. Fire goes before him, and the mountains melt like wax. The heavens declare his justice. All who worship idols are put to shame. Those who love the LORD must hate evil. Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the honest in heart.

verse.text: You who love the LORD, hate evil! He preserves the souls of his saints. He delivers them out of the hand of the wicked.

psalms-97.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-99.summary: The LORD reigns, and the peoples tremble. He sits enthroned above the cherubim. He is holy. The King loves justice and has established fairness in Israel. Moses, Aaron, and Samuel called on him, and he answered. He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud. He forgave them, and he also punished their wrongs. The people are called to worship at his holy hill.

verse.text: You answered them, LORD our God. You are a God who forgave them, although you took vengeance for their doings.

psalms-99.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-102.summary: The heading calls this the prayer of a suffering person who is faint. His days vanish like smoke, and his heart is withered like grass. He is like a lonely bird on a roof. His enemies mock him, and he eats ashes with his bread. Yet the LORD sits enthroned forever. He will rise and have mercy on Zion. This will be written for a generation still to come. The heavens will wear out like clothing, but God stays the same.

verse.text: This will be written for the generation to come. A people which will be created will praise the LORD,

psalms-102.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-105.summary: The poem calls the people to remember the LORD’s wonders. He made a covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and promised them a land. When they were few, he protected them. He sent Joseph ahead as a slave, and Joseph rose to rule Egypt. Israel grew there and was hated. God sent Moses, Aaron, and the plagues. He brought his people out with joy and fed them in the desert. He gave them lands so that they would keep his laws.

verse.text: He sent a man before them. Joseph was sold for a slave.

psalms-105.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-106.summary: The poem begins with praise and a prayer to be remembered. Then it confesses: we have sinned as our fathers did. The fathers forgot God’s wonders at the Red Sea. They craved food in the desert and envied Moses. They made a calf at Horeb, and Moses stood in the gap for them. They joined in the worship of Baal and later sacrificed their children. God gave them over to the nations many times. Yet he heard their cry and remembered his covenant.

verse.text: We have sinned with our fathers. We have committed iniquity. We have done wickedly.

psalms-106.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-108.summary: The speaker’s heart is steady, and he will sing and wake the dawn. He will give thanks among the nations. God’s kindness is higher than the heavens. He asks God to save with his right hand. God has spoken: Shechem, Gilead, Ephraim, and Judah are his. Moab, Edom, and Philistia are under him. Yet God has not gone out with their armies. With God they will still do bravely.

verse.text: God has spoken from his sanctuary: “In triumph, I will divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of Succoth.

psalms-108.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-110.summary: The LORD tells the speaker’s lord to sit at his right hand. His enemies will become his footstool. The LORD will extend his rule from Zion. His people offer themselves freely on the day of battle. The LORD has sworn an oath and will not change it. This ruler is a priest forever, like Melchizedek. The Lord at his right hand will shatter kings. He will judge the nations and lift up his head.

verse.text: The LORD has sworn, and will not change his mind: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

psalms-110.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-114.summary: Israel went out of Egypt, from a people of foreign speech. Judah became God’s sanctuary. The sea saw it and fled, and the Jordan turned back. The mountains skipped like rams and the hills like lambs. The poet asks the sea and the river why they ran. He asks the mountains why they skipped. The earth should tremble before the God of Jacob. He turned the rock into a pool of water.

verse.text: What was it, you sea, that you fled? You Jordan, that you turned back?

psalms-114.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-116.summary: The speaker loves the LORD, who heard his cry. The cords of death had wrapped around him. He called on the LORD’s name and was saved. God rescued his life from death, his eyes from tears, and his feet from falling. He asks what he can give back to the LORD. He will lift the cup of salvation and call on the LORD’s name. He will keep his vows before all the people. He will offer thanks in the courts of the LORD’s house.

verse.text: What will I give to the LORD for all his benefits toward me?

psalms-116.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-122.summary: The speaker was glad when people said, “Let’s go to the LORD’s house.” Now his feet stand inside Jerusalem’s gates. The city is built firmly together. The tribes go up there to give thanks to the LORD. Thrones for judgment stand there, the thrones of David’s house. He calls for prayer for Jerusalem’s peace. He wishes peace within its walls. He seeks its good for the sake of his family and the LORD’s house.

verse.text: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem. Those who love you will prosper.

psalms-122.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-125.summary: Those who trust the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved. Mountains surround Jerusalem. In the same way the LORD surrounds his people now and forever. Wicked rule will not stay over the land of the righteous. Otherwise the righteous might turn to doing wrong. The poet asks the LORD to do good to the good. Those who turn to crooked ways will be led away. Peace be on Israel.

verse.text: As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds his people from this time forward and forever more.

psalms-125.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-126.summary: When the LORD brought back Zion’s captives, the people were like dreamers. Their mouths were full of laughter and song. The nations said the LORD had done great things for them. The people agree and are glad. They ask the LORD to restore them again like streams in the Negev. Those who sow in tears will reap with joy. The one who goes out weeping with seed will return with sheaves.

verse.text: Restore our fortunes again, LORD, like the streams in the Negev.

psalms-126.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-128.summary: Everyone who fears the LORD and walks in his ways is blessed. He will eat what his own hands have worked for. His wife will be like a fruitful vine in his house. His children will be like olive shoots around his table. The poem asks the LORD to bless him from Zion. May he see Jerusalem’s good all his life. May he see his children’s children. Peace be on Israel.

verse.text: Your wife will be as a fruitful vine in the innermost parts of your house, your children like olive shoots around your table.

psalms-128.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-129.summary: Israel says it has been attacked many times since its youth. Yet its enemies have not won. Plowmen plowed its back and made their furrows long. The LORD is just and has cut the cords of the wicked. May all who hate Zion be turned back. May they be like grass on a roof that withers before it grows. No reaper fills his hands with it. No passerby gives it a blessing.

verse.text: The plowers plowed on my back. They made their furrows long.

psalms-129.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-132.summary: The poem asks the LORD to remember David and his hardships. David swore not to rest until he found a place for the LORD. The people heard of the ark and went to worship at his footstool. They ask the LORD to arise and come to his resting place. The LORD swore that David’s sons would sit on his throne. The LORD has chosen Zion for his home. He will bless her food and satisfy her poor with bread. He will make David’s strength grow there.

verse.text: For the LORD has chosen Zion. He has desired it for his habitation.

psalms-132.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-133.summary: The poem says how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in unity. It is like fine oil poured on the head. The oil runs down Aaron’s beard to the collar of his robes. It is like the dew of Mount Hermon falling on the hills of Zion. There the LORD commands his blessing. That blessing is life forever.

verse.text: It is like the precious oil on the head, that ran down on the beard, even Aaron’s beard, that came down on the edge of his robes,

psalms-133.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-134.summary: This is the last of the songs of ascents. It calls the LORD’s servants to bless him. They stand in the LORD’s house by night. They are told to lift their hands toward the holy place. Then a blessing is spoken in return. May the LORD, who made heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.

verse.text: May the LORD bless you from Zion, even he who made heaven and earth.

psalms-134.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-135.summary: The poem calls the LORD’s servants to praise his name. He chose Jacob for himself. He does whatever he pleases in heaven, earth, and sea. He brings clouds, lightning, and wind. He struck Egypt’s firstborn and defeated great kings. He gave their land to Israel. The idols of the nations are silver and gold, made by hands. Israel, Aaron’s house, and Levi’s house are called to bless the LORD.

verse.text: The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.

psalms-135.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-136.summary: The poem calls the people to thank the LORD, for he is good. Every line ends with “for his loving kindness endures forever.” He alone does great wonders. He made the heavens, the earth, the sun, and the moon. He brought Israel out of Egypt and divided the Red Sea. He led his people through the desert and struck down kings. He remembered them when they were low. He gives food to every creature.

verse.text: who remembered us in our low estate, for his loving kindness endures forever;

psalms-136.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-137.summary: The exiles sat by the rivers of Babylon and wept for Zion. They hung their harps on the trees. Their captors asked them for a song of Zion. They ask how they can sing the LORD’s song in a foreign land. The speaker swears never to forget Jerusalem. He asks the LORD to remember what Edom said when the city fell. He speaks of Babylon’s coming ruin. The poem ends with fierce words about repayment.

verse.text: How can we sing the LORD’s song in a foreign land?

psalms-137.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-146.summary: The speaker will praise the LORD as long as he lives. He warns against trusting in princes. A human ruler dies, and his plans die that day. The one whose help is the God of Jacob is blessed. God made heaven, earth, and sea and keeps faith forever. He gives justice to the oppressed and food to the hungry. He frees prisoners and opens blind eyes. He guards foreigners, orphans, and widows.

verse.text: Don’t put your trust in princes, in a son of man in whom there is no help.

psalms-146.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-147.summary: It is good to sing praise to the LORD. He builds up Jerusalem and gathers Israel’s outcasts. He heals the brokenhearted and binds their wounds. He counts the stars and names each one. He covers the sky with clouds and feeds animals and young ravens. He takes no pleasure in a horse’s strength. He sends snow, frost, and hail, and his word melts them. He has given his word to Israel.

verse.text: He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.

psalms-147.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

psalms-149.summary: The poem calls for a new song in the gathering of the faithful. Israel should rejoice in its Maker. The people praise with dancing, tambourine, and lyre. The LORD takes pleasure in his people and honors the humble with victory. The faithful sing for joy on their beds. Praise is in their mouths and a two-edged sword in their hands. They are to carry out the judgment that is written. This is the honor of all his faithful ones.

verse.text: May the high praises of God be in their mouths, and a two-edged sword in their hand,

psalms-149.dateDetail: The Church chronology does not date the psalms.

ecclesiastes-1.summary: These are the words of the Preacher, a son of David and king in Jerusalem. He says everything is vapor. He asks what people gain from all their work under the sun. Generations come and go, and the earth stays. The sun rises and sets, and rivers run to a sea that never fills. Nothing is new, and earlier people are forgotten. He set his mind to study all that is done. He found that much wisdom brings much grief.

verse.text: That which has been is that which shall be, and that which has been done is that which shall be done; and there is no new thing under the sun.

ecclesiastes-1.dateDetail: The setting follows Ecclesiastes 1:1, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

ecclesiastes-2.summary: The Preacher tests pleasure, laughter, and wine. He builds houses, plants vineyards, and makes gardens and pools. He gathers servants, herds, silver, gold, and singers. He denies himself nothing his eyes want. Then he looks at it all and finds it empty. Wisdom is better than folly, yet the wise and the fool both die. He hates his work, since he must leave it to someone else. He concludes that enjoying food and work is a gift from God.

verse.text: I hated all my labor in which I labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.

ecclesiastes-2.dateDetail: The setting follows Ecclesiastes 1:1, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

song-of-solomon-1.summary: The book is called the Song of songs. A woman speaks first and longs for her lover’s kisses. She says his love is better than wine and his name is like perfume. She tells the women of Jerusalem that she is dark and lovely. The sun has darkened her, since her brothers made her tend the vineyards. She asks her lover where he pastures his flock. He praises her beauty and compares her to a fine mare. She says he is like a bundle of myrrh and a cluster of henna.

verse.text: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance. Your name is oil poured out, therefore the virgins love you.

song-of-solomon-1.dateDetail: The setting follows Song of Solomon 1:1, which names Solomon.

song-of-solomon-2.summary: The woman calls herself a flower of the plain. Her lover says she is a lily among thorns. She says he is an apple tree among the trees of the forest. She asks the women of Jerusalem not to stir up love before its time. She hears him coming, leaping over the hills. He looks through the window and calls her to come away. Winter is past, the flowers appear, and the doves are heard. She says her beloved is hers and she is his.

verse.text: For behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone.

song-of-solomon-2.dateDetail: The setting follows Song of Solomon 1:1, which names Solomon.

song-of-solomon-3.summary: At night on her bed the woman looks for the one she loves. She does not find him. She gets up and searches the streets and squares. The watchmen find her, and she asks whether they have seen him. Just past them she finds him and holds him. She will not let go until she brings him to her mother’s house. Then a grand procession comes up from the wilderness. It is Solomon’s carriage, guarded by sixty armed men.

verse.text: I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.

song-of-solomon-3.dateDetail: The setting follows Song of Solomon 1:1, which names Solomon.

song-of-solomon-4.summary: The man praises the woman’s beauty part by part. Her eyes are doves, and her hair is like goats on a hillside. Her neck is like a tower hung with shields. One glance from her has captured his heart. Her love is better than wine, and her lips drip honey. He calls her a locked garden and a sealed spring. The garden holds pomegranates, nard, saffron, cinnamon, and myrrh. She calls the winds to blow and invites him into the garden.

verse.text: My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.

song-of-solomon-4.dateDetail: The setting follows Song of Solomon 1:1, which names Solomon.

song-of-solomon-5.summary: The man says he has come into his garden. Then the woman tells of a night when her heart was awake. Her beloved knocked and asked her to open. She had undressed and washed her feet, and she hesitated. When she opened the door, he was gone. She searched and called, and he did not answer. The watchmen found her, beat her, and took her cloak. The women ask what makes him special, and she describes him from head to foot.

verse.text: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.

song-of-solomon-5.dateDetail: The setting follows Song of Solomon 1:1, which names Solomon.

song-of-solomon-6.summary: The women of Jerusalem ask where her beloved has gone. They offer to look for him with her. She answers that he has gone down to his garden. She says she is his and he is hers. He praises her as beautiful as a great city and awesome as an army. Her eyes overwhelm him. A king may have many queens, but she is his only one. She went down to the orchard to see whether the vines had budded.

verse.text: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine. He browses among the lilies.

song-of-solomon-6.dateDetail: The setting follows Song of Solomon 1:1, which names Solomon.

song-of-solomon-7.summary: The man praises the woman from her feet to her head. Her neck is like an ivory tower, and her eyes are like pools. Her hair holds a king captive. She is like a palm tree, and he will climb it. She says she belongs to her beloved and his desire is for her. She invites him to go out to the fields and stay in the villages. They will rise early to see whether the vines have budded. There she will give him her love.

verse.text: Come, my beloved! Let’s go out into the field. Let’s lodge in the villages.

song-of-solomon-7.dateDetail: The setting follows Song of Solomon 1:1, which names Solomon.

song-of-solomon-8.summary: The woman wishes she could kiss her lover in public without scorn. She asks again that love not be stirred before its time. She asks him to set her as a seal on his heart and arm. Love is as strong as death, and its flame is a mighty fire. Her brothers discuss how to guard their little sister. She answers that she is a wall and has found peace. Solomon rents out a vineyard for silver, but her vineyard is her own. She calls her beloved to hurry like a gazelle.

verse.text: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.

song-of-solomon-8.dateDetail: The setting follows Song of Solomon 1:1, which names Solomon.

isaiah-1.summary: Isaiah sees a vision about Judah and Jerusalem. God says his people have left him. Their cities are burned, and strangers take their land. Jerusalem is left alone. The people still bring offerings and pray. God refuses their worship and tells them to do right. He gives them a choice: obey and eat well, or refuse and face the sword. He promises to give the city fair judges again.

verse.text: Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Defend the fatherless. Plead for the widow.”

isaiah-2.summary: Isaiah sees what will happen in later days. The LORD’s mountain stands above all other hills. Many peoples go up to learn his ways. He settles their disputes, and they turn swords into plow blades. Then the vision turns to Jacob’s people now. Their land is full of silver, horses, and idols. A day of the LORD will bring down every proud thing. People will throw their idols to moles and bats.

verse.text: He will judge between the nations, and will decide concerning many peoples. They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

isaiah-3.summary: The LORD takes bread, water, and leaders away from Jerusalem and Judah. Soldiers, judges, prophets, and elders are gone. Boys rule, and neighbors hurt each other. One man begs his brother to rule the ruin, and the brother refuses. Then the LORD stands up as judge. He charges the elders and leaders with robbing the poor. He also says the proud women of Zion will lose their fine things. The city gates mourn, and the men fall in war.

verse.text: What do you mean that you crush my people, and grind the face of the poor?” says the Lord, GOD of Armies.

isaiah-4.summary: Verse 1 ends the war scene from chapter 3. So few men are left that seven women ask one man for his name. Then the picture changes. The LORD’s branch and the land’s fruit become the pride of the survivors. Those left in Jerusalem are called holy. The Lord washes the city’s filth and blood away with justice and burning. He covers Mount Zion with cloud by day and fire by night. A shelter gives shade from heat and cover from storm.

verse.text: There will be a pavilion for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for a refuge and for a shelter from storm and from rain.

isaiah-5.summary: A singer begins a love song about a friend’s vineyard. The owner dug, cleared stones, planted good vines, and built a tower. The vines gave wild grapes. The owner asks Judah to judge, then says he will break down its wall. Verse 7 names the vineyard: Israel and Judah. Six cries of “Woe” name land grabbers, heavy drinkers, and judges who take bribes. The LORD’s anger burns, and his hand stays stretched out. He whistles for a far nation, and its army comes fast.

verse.text: For the vineyard of the LORD of Armies is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant. He looked for justice, but behold, oppression, for righteousness, but behold, a cry of distress.

isaiah-6.summary: Isaiah tells what he saw in the year King Uzziah died. The Lord sits on a high throne in the temple. Six-winged beings called seraphim call out, “Holy, holy, holy.” The doorposts shake, and smoke fills the house. Isaiah says he is ruined because his lips are unclean. A seraph touches his mouth with a hot coal and says his sin is forgiven. The Lord asks whom to send, and Isaiah offers to go. His message will not be understood until the land lies empty.

verse.text: I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am. Send me!”

isaiah-7.summary: The kings of Syria and Israel march against King Ahaz in Jerusalem. Ahaz and his people shake with fear. The LORD sends Isaiah and his son to meet Ahaz by the upper pool. Isaiah says the two kings are only smoking stubs, and their plan will fail. The LORD offers Ahaz a sign, but Ahaz refuses to ask. Isaiah gives one anyway: the virgin will bear a son named Immanuel. Before the boy can choose good, both enemy lands will be empty. Then the LORD will bring the king of Assyria on Judah.

verse.text: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If you will not believe, surely you shall not be established.’ ”

isaiah-8.summary: Isaiah writes the name Maher Shalal Hash Baz on a large tablet. The prophetess bears Isaiah a son, and the boy gets that name. Before the boy can talk, Assyria will plunder Damascus and Samaria. The people refused the quiet waters of Shiloah. So the king of Assyria will come like a flood, up to Judah’s neck. The LORD warns Isaiah not to share the people’s fears. Isaiah seals the teaching among his followers and waits. People who ask the dead for help will find only darkness.

verse.text: “Don’t call a conspiracy all that this people call a conspiracy. Don’t fear their threats or be terrorized.

isaiah-9.summary: The gloom over Zebulun and Naphtali ends. People who walked in darkness see a great light. The oppressor’s rod breaks, and armor and bloody clothes burn. A child is born who will rule on David’s throne. His names include Wonderful Counselor and Prince of Peace. Then the word turns against Israel and Samaria. They boast that they will rebuild with cut stone. Enemies, lying leaders, and fighting between tribes follow, and the LORD’s hand stays stretched out.

verse.text: Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on David’s throne, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will perform this.

isaiah-10.summary: The chapter opens with woe to lawmakers who rob widows and the fatherless. Then the LORD calls Assyria the rod of his anger. He sends Assyria against a people who anger him. But Assyria’s king plans to destroy many nations and boasts of his own strength. The LORD will punish that pride after his work on Jerusalem. A remnant of Israel will return and lean on the LORD. An army marches town by town toward Jerusalem. Then the LORD cuts down the tall trees.

verse.text: Should an ax brag against him who chops with it? Should a saw exalt itself above him who saws with it? As if a rod should lift those who lift it up, or as if a staff should lift up someone who is not wood.

isaiah-11.summary: A shoot grows from the stock of Jesse. The LORD’s Spirit rests on him with wisdom, counsel, and might. He does not judge by what he sees or hears. He judges the poor with fairness and strikes the wicked with his words. Wolf and lamb, cow and bear, child and snake live without harm. The nations look for this root of Jesse. The Lord gathers his scattered people from Assyria, Egypt, and far lands. Ephraim and Judah stop fighting each other, and a road opens for those who return.

verse.text: but he will judge the poor with righteousness, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.

isaiah-12.summary: This chapter is a short song for “that day.” The singer thanks the LORD because his anger has turned away. The singer says, “God is my salvation,” and will trust without fear. The people draw water with joy from the wells of salvation. They tell the nations what the LORD has done. Zion is told to shout, because the Holy One of Israel is great among them.

verse.text: Therefore with joy you will draw water out of the wells of salvation.

isaiah-13.summary: Isaiah sees a message about Babylon. A banner goes up, and the LORD gathers an army from far lands. The day of the LORD comes with anger. Hands go weak, hearts melt, and the sun, moon, and stars go dark. The LORD says he will punish evil and end the pride of the proud. He stirs up the Medes, who do not care for silver or gold. Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, will fall like Sodom and Gomorrah. Only wild animals will live there.

verse.text: I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity. I will cause the arrogance of the proud to cease, and will humble the arrogance of the terrible.

isaiah-13.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-14.summary: The LORD will have compassion on Jacob and settle Israel in its own land. Then Israel will sing a taunt against the king of Babylon. The whole earth rests and sings. Dead kings in Sheol, the place of the dead, say he is weak like them. He said he would rise above the stars. He is thrown out without a tomb. The LORD also swears to break Assyria in his land. A last message warns Philistia not to rejoice.

verse.text: that you will take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and say, “How the oppressor has ceased! The golden city has ceased!”

isaiah-14.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-15.summary: This is a message about Moab. Two Moabite cities, Ar and Kir, fall in one night. People go up to the high places to weep. They shave their heads, cut their beards, and wear rough sackcloth. The cry spreads from town to town, and soldiers shake. The speaker says, “My heart cries out for Moab!” Nobles flee to Zoar, weeping as they climb. The waters dry up or run with blood, and more trouble is coming.

verse.text: My heart cries out for Moab! Her nobles flee to Zoar, to Eglath Shelishiyah; for they go up by the ascent of Luhith with weeping; for on the way to Horonaim, they raise up a cry of destruction.

routes.title: Weeping on the ascent of Luhith
Distress on the road to Horonaim

isaiah-16.summary: Moab is told to send lambs to the ruler on Mount Zion. Moab’s women are like birds pushed from a nest at the Arnon river crossings. A voice asks for shelter: hide the outcasts and do not betray them. A throne will stand in David’s tent, with a judge who seeks justice. But Moab’s pride is well known, and its boasts are empty. Its vines and harvest songs stop, and the speaker weeps for them. Moab’s prayers at its high place will not work. Within three years its glory will be small.

verse.text: Let my outcasts dwell with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortionist is brought to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.

isaiah-17.summary: This is a message about Damascus. Damascus will stop being a city and become a heap of ruins. Ephraim loses its fortress too. Jacob’s glory grows thin, like a field after harvest. Only a few olives stay on the highest branches. In that day people will look to their Maker, not to altars they made. They forgot the God who saved them, so their planting gives no harvest. Many nations roar like the sea, but by morning they are gone.

verse.text: In that day, people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will have respect for the Holy One of Israel.

isaiah-18.summary: The message speaks to a land beyond the rivers of Ethiopia. It sends messengers in papyrus boats. They go to a tall, smooth people whose land the rivers divide. All the world is told to watch for a banner and listen for a trumpet. The LORD says he will stay still and watch, like heat in sunshine. Before the harvest he cuts off the branches and leaves them for birds and animals. Then that tall people will bring a gift to the LORD at Mount Zion.

verse.text: In that time, a present will be brought to the LORD of Armies from a people tall and smooth, even from a people awesome from their beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of the LORD of Armies, Mount Zion.

isaiah-19.summary: This is a message about Egypt. The LORD rides a swift cloud to Egypt, and its idols shake. Egyptians fight each other, and a cruel king rules them. The Nile dries up, and fishermen and weavers lose their work. Pharaoh’s wise men give foolish advice. Then five Egyptian cities swear to the LORD, and an altar to him stands there. The LORD strikes Egypt and heals it. A highway joins Egypt and Assyria, and the LORD blesses both with Israel.

verse.text: because the LORD of Armies has blessed them, saying, “Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance.”

isaiah-20.summary: Assyria’s commander takes the city of Ashdod for King Sargon. At that time the LORD tells Isaiah to take off his sackcloth and sandals. Isaiah walks naked and barefoot for three years. The LORD says this is a sign about Egypt and Ethiopia. Assyria’s king will lead their captives away the same way, young and old. People who trusted Egypt and Ethiopia will be ashamed. The people of the coast will ask how they can escape.

verse.text: They will be dismayed and confounded, because of Ethiopia their expectation, and of Egypt their glory.

isaiah-21.summary: Three short messages follow. In the first, Isaiah sees a hard vision and shakes with pain. A watchman stands at his post day and night. He sees riders in pairs and hears, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon.” In the second, a voice from Seir asks the watchman about the night. He answers that morning comes, and also night. In the third, people of Tema bring water and bread to those fleeing battle. Within a year the glory of Kedar will fail.

verse.text: They brought water to him who was thirsty. The inhabitants of the land of Tema met the fugitives with their bread.

isaiah-22.summary: This message is about the “valley of vision,” and it speaks to Jerusalem. The people are on the rooftops shouting, but their rulers fled and were captured. The speaker weeps for the city. Enemy chariots fill the valleys. The people check weapons, break down houses to fix the wall, and store water. They do not look to the one who planned it. They feast and say, “Let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die.” Then Shebna the palace manager loses his place to Eliakim.

verse.text: You also made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you didn’t look to him who had done this, neither did you have respect for him who planned it long ago.

isaiah-23.summary: This is a message about Tyre. Ships of Tarshish are told to howl, because Tyre’s harbor and houses are gone. Tyre was the market of nations, and grain from the Nile made it rich. Its traders were like princes. Who planned its fall? The LORD of Armies planned it, to shame the pride of all glory. Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years. Then it trades again, and its earnings feed those who live before the LORD.

verse.text: The LORD of Armies has planned it, to stain the pride of all glory, to bring into contempt all the honorable of the earth.

isaiah-24.summary: The LORD empties the earth and scatters its people. Priest and people, master and servant, lender and borrower all share the same end. The earth mourns because its people broke the laws and the everlasting covenant. Wine, music, and joy stop, and the city is broken. A few remain, like olives after shaking, and they sing from far coasts. The speaker still cries, “Woe is me!” The earth sways like a drunk man and falls. The LORD punishes powers above and kings below, and he reigns on Mount Zion.

verse.text: The earth also is polluted under its inhabitants, because they have transgressed the laws, violated the statutes, and broken the everlasting covenant.

isaiah-24.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-25.summary: The speaker praises the LORD for wonderful things planned long ago. The LORD turned a strong city into a heap. He has been a stronghold for the poor and shade from the heat. On this mountain he will make a rich feast for all peoples. He will destroy the veil that covers all nations. He swallows up death forever and wipes tears from all faces. The people say they waited for this God, and he will save them. Moab’s pride is brought down to the dust.

verse.text: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for the LORD has spoken it.

isaiah-25.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-26.summary: Judah will sing this song in that day. The singers have a strong city, and salvation is its walls. The LORD keeps a steady mind in peace because it trusts him. He brought the high city down, and the feet of the poor walk on it. The singers say they waited for the LORD through the night. Other lords ruled them, and their own efforts gave birth only to wind. Then comes a promise: “Your dead shall live.” The people are told to hide a little while until the anger passes.

verse.text: Your dead shall live. Their dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.

isaiah-26.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-27.summary: In that day the LORD kills leviathan, the twisting serpent of the sea. In a new vineyard song, the LORD keeps the vineyard and waters it. He says he has no anger. Thorns may be burned or may make peace with him. Jacob will take root, and Israel will fill the world with fruit. Jacob’s sin is forgiven when the altar stones are crushed like chalk. The strong city lies empty. A great trumpet calls the lost from Assyria and Egypt to worship in Jerusalem.

verse.text: In days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will blossom and bud. They will fill the surface of the world with fruit.

isaiah-27.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-28.summary: Woe comes to Ephraim’s drunk leaders, whose crown is a fading flower. A strong one from the Lord will throw it down like a hailstorm. Priests and prophets stagger with drink too. They ask if the teaching is for small children: “line on line, here a little.” Jerusalem’s rulers say they made a covenant with death. The Lord GOD lays a tested cornerstone in Zion and measures with justice. Hail will sweep away their shelter of lies. A farmer does not plow or thresh forever, and this wisdom comes from the LORD.

verse.text: Therefore the Lord GOD says, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. He who believes shall not act hastily.

isaiah-29.summary: Woe comes to Ariel, the city where David camped. The LORD will camp against it, and its voice will whisper from the dust. Then its enemies blow away like chaff, like a dream after waking. The prophets are in a deep sleep, and the vision is like a sealed book. The Lord says this people honors him with lips while their hearts are far away. He will do a wonder, and the wisdom of the wise will fail. In a little while the deaf will hear and the blind will see. The humble will rejoice, and Jacob will no longer be ashamed.

verse.text: The Lord said, “Because this people draws near with their mouth and honors me with their lips, but they have removed their heart far from me, and their fear of me is a commandment of men which has been taught;

isaiah-30.summary: The LORD says woe to rebellious children who go to Egypt without asking him. Their envoys carry treasure through a desert, but Egypt’s help is empty. The people tell the prophets to say only pleasant things. So their sin is like a bulging wall that breaks at once. The Lord GOD offered rescue through returning and rest, and they refused. Still the LORD waits to be gracious. A voice will say, “This is the way.” He will heal his people and strike Assyria with his rod.

verse.text: For thus said the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused,

isaiah-31.summary: Woe comes to those who go down to Egypt for help. They trust many chariots and strong horsemen and do not seek the LORD. The Egyptians are men and not God, and their horses are flesh. When the LORD stretches out his hand, helper and helped fall together. The LORD will fight for Mount Zion like a lion over its prey. He will guard Jerusalem like hovering birds. Israel is called to return and throw away its idols. The Assyrian will fall by a sword that is not a man’s.

verse.text: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the LORD stretches out his hand, both he who helps shall stumble, and he who is helped shall fall, and they all shall be consumed together.

isaiah-32.summary: A king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule with justice. Each will be like shelter from wind and water in a dry place. Eyes will see, ears will listen, and fools will no longer be called noble. Then the speaker warns the women who feel safe. In little more than a year the grape harvest will fail. Thorns will grow, and the palace and city will be empty. This lasts until the Spirit is poured out from on high. Then justice lives in the land, and its fruit is peace and safe homes.

verse.text: The work of righteousness will be peace, and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.

isaiah-33.summary: Woe comes to a destroyer who has not yet been destroyed. The people ask the LORD to be gracious, because they have waited for him. Envoys of peace weep, the roads are empty, and the land withers. The LORD says, “Now I will arise.” Sinners in Zion ask who can live with the burning fire. The answer is one who walks rightly, refuses bribes, and turns from bloodshed. That person will see the king and a quiet Jerusalem. The LORD is judge, lawgiver, and king, and he will save.

verse.text: For the LORD is our judge. The LORD is our lawgiver. The LORD is our king. He will save us.

isaiah-34.summary: All nations are called to listen. The LORD is angry with the nations and their armies. The sky rolls up like a scroll, and its stars fade like leaves. His sword comes down on Edom, with a great slaughter at Bozrah. The LORD has a day of vengeance for Zion’s cause. Edom’s streams turn to pitch, and its smoke rises forever. Owls, ravens, jackals, and snakes take over its palaces. The LORD’s book says not one of these animals will be missing.

verse.text: For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.

isaiah-34.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-35.summary: The desert will be glad and bloom. It will see the glory of the LORD. Weak hands and shaking knees are to be made strong. The fearful are told that God will come and save them. Then the blind see, the deaf hear, the lame leap, and the mute sing. Water breaks out in the dry land. A road called the Holy Way runs through it, and no lion is there. The LORD’s ransomed people come to Zion singing, and sorrow flees.

verse.text: Then the LORD’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”

isaiah-35.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-36.summary: In King Hezekiah’s fourteenth year, Sennacherib of Assyria captures Judah’s walled cities. He sends his officer Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem with a large army. Rabshakeh stops by the water channel of the upper pool. Three of Hezekiah’s officials come out to meet him. Assyrian palace reliefs also show Lachish.

verse.text: Behold, you trust in the staff of this bruised reed, even in Egypt, which if a man leans on it, it will go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

isaiah-37.summary: Hezekiah tears his clothes, goes to the LORD’s house, and sends to Isaiah. Isaiah says not to fear: the king of Assyria will hear news and go home. Sennacherib sends a letter that mocks Hezekiah’s God. Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD. His prayer admits Assyria’s victories and says the fallen gods were wood and stone. He asks God to save Judah so all kingdoms know the LORD alone is God.

verse.text: Now therefore, LORD our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are the LORD, even you only.”

isaiah-38.summary: Hezekiah is sick and near death. Isaiah tells him to set his house in order. Hezekiah turns to the wall, prays, and weeps. The LORD sends Isaiah back: he has heard, and he adds fifteen years. He also promises to defend the city from Assyria. As a sign, the shadow goes back ten steps on the sundial of Ahaz. Verse 6 shows why chapter order may differ from the order of events.

verse.text: Lord, men live by these things; and my spirit finds life in all of them. You restore me, and cause me to live.

isaiah-39.summary: The king of Babylon sends letters and a gift after Hezekiah’s sickness. Hezekiah is pleased and shows the envoys all his treasure and weapons. Isaiah asks where the men came from and what they saw. Hezekiah says they came from Babylon and saw everything. Isaiah gives the LORD’s word: all of it will be carried to Babylon. Some of Hezekiah’s own sons will serve in Babylon’s palace. Hezekiah calls the word good, because there will be peace in his days. McClellan compares this warning with Isaiah 40. Isaiah 40 speaks as if the exile has already happened. He uses this change to support a later date for Isaiah 40–55. Scholars often call this section Second Isaiah.

verse.text: ‘Behold, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have stored up until today, will be carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left,’ says the LORD.

isaiah-40.summary: God says, “Comfort, comfort my people.” Jerusalem’s hard service is over, and her sin is pardoned. A voice calls for a level road in the desert for the LORD. Another voice says people are like grass, but God’s word stands forever. Zion is told to say, “Behold, your God!” He comes with power and carries lambs like a shepherd. No one taught him, and no nation or idol compares with him. Jacob says God has missed his case, yet those who wait gain new strength.

verse.text: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable.

isaiah-40.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-41.summary: The LORD calls the far coasts to meet him in court. He asks who raised up a conqueror from the east. The answer is the LORD, the first and with the last. The nations are afraid, and their workers nail idols down so they will not fall. The LORD calls Israel his servant, chosen and not thrown away. He tells Israel not to fear, because he will help and hold it up. He will give water to the poor and trees to the desert. He dares the idols to tell the future, and they cannot.

verse.text: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.

isaiah-41.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-42.summary: The LORD presents his servant and puts his Spirit on him. The servant brings justice to the nations without shouting in the street. He does not break a bruised reed or put out a weak wick. He is a light for the nations, to open blind eyes and free prisoners. All the earth is called to sing a new song. The LORD, long silent, goes out like a warrior and leads the blind. Then he calls his own servant blind and deaf. Israel was robbed because it would not walk in his ways.

verse.text: He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a dimly burning wick. He will faithfully bring justice.

isaiah-42.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-43.summary: The LORD who made Jacob says not to fear. He has redeemed Israel, called it by name, and says, “You are mine.” He will be with them through water and fire. He will gather their children from east, west, north, and south. The nations are called to court, and Israel is the LORD’s witness. For Israel’s sake he sends to Babylon. He is doing a new thing: a road and rivers in the desert. Israel wore him out with sins, yet he blots them out for his own sake.

verse.text: But now the LORD who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.

isaiah-43.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-44.summary: The LORD tells Jacob his servant not to fear. He will pour water on dry ground and his Spirit on their children. He is the first and the last, and there is no other God. Then the chapter describes an idol maker. He burns half a tree to cook and bows to the other half. No one stops to think that it is a block of wood. The LORD tells Israel he has wiped out its sins like a cloud. He says Jerusalem will be built, and he names Cyrus as his shepherd.

verse.text: who says of Cyrus, ‘He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure,’ even saying of Jerusalem, ‘She will be built;’ and of the temple, ‘Your foundation will be laid.’ ”

isaiah-44.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-45.summary: The LORD speaks to Cyrus, his anointed, and holds his right hand. He will open gates before Cyrus and give him hidden treasure. He does this for Jacob’s sake, though Cyrus has not known him. The LORD says he forms light and darkness, peace and trouble. Woe comes to anyone who argues with his Maker, like clay with a potter. Cyrus will build the city and free the exiles without payment. The LORD did not speak in secret. He calls all the ends of the earth to look to him and be saved.

verse.text: The LORD says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held to subdue nations before him and strip kings of their armor, to open the doors before him, and the gates shall not be shut:

isaiah-45.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-46.summary: Bel and Nebo bow down. Animals carry their idols as heavy loads, and the idols go into captivity. The LORD tells Jacob’s house that he has carried them from birth. He will carry them to old age and gray hair. People pay a goldsmith to make a god, then lift it on their shoulders. It stands where they set it and cannot answer. The LORD declares the end from the beginning. He calls a bird of prey from the east and brings salvation to Zion.

verse.text: Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.

isaiah-46.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-47.summary: Babylon is told to come down and sit in the dust. She will grind flour at the millstones and be called tender no more. The LORD says he gave his people into her hand, and she showed no mercy. She laid a heavy yoke even on the old. She said, “I will be a princess forever.” In one day she will lose both children and husband. Her spells and star readers cannot save her. They burn like stubble, and no one is left to help.

verse.text: For you have trusted in your wickedness. You have said, ‘No one sees me.’ Your wisdom and your knowledge has perverted you. You have said in your heart, ‘I am, and there is no one else besides me.’

isaiah-47.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-48.summary: The LORD speaks to Jacob’s house, who swear by his name but not in truth. He told them things long ago so they could not credit an idol. Now he tells new things they have not heard. He holds back his anger for his own name’s sake. He has tested them in the furnace of suffering. He says their peace would have been like a river if they had listened. Then the order comes: leave Babylon and shout that the LORD has redeemed Jacob. There is no peace for the wicked.

verse.text: Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! With the sound of joyful shouting announce this, tell it even to the end of the earth; say, “The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob!”

isaiah-48.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-49.summary: The servant speaks to far peoples. The LORD called him before birth and made his mouth like a sharp sword. The servant says he has worked for nothing, yet his reward is with God. The LORD says restoring Israel is too small a task. The servant will be a light to the nations. Captives will come out and be led by springs of water. Zion says the LORD has forgotten her. He answers that a mother may forget her baby, but he will not forget Zion.

verse.text: “Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you!

isaiah-49.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-50.summary: The LORD asks for the divorce paper and the name of any lender he owed. He says the people were sold for their own sins. He asks why no one answered when he called. Then a servant speaks. The Lord GOD wakes his ear each morning and gives him words for the weary. He gave his back to those who beat him and did not hide from spitting. He sets his face like flint, because the Lord GOD will help him. Those who fear the LORD are told to trust him in the dark.

verse.text: The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of those who are taught, that I may know how to sustain with words him who is weary. He awakens morning by morning, he awakens my ear to hear as those who are taught.

isaiah-50.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-51.summary: The LORD speaks to those who seek him. Look to Abraham and Sarah, he says: Abraham was one, and God made him many. The LORD will comfort Zion and make her desert like Eden. The sky will fade like smoke, but his salvation lasts forever. A voice calls the LORD’s arm to wake, as when it dried the sea. The LORD asks why they fear men who die like grass. Jerusalem has drunk the cup of his anger to the bottom. He takes the cup from her hand and gives it to those who hurt her.

verse.text: For the LORD has comforted Zion. He has comforted all her waste places, and has made her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD. Joy and gladness will be found in them, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody.

isaiah-51.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-52.summary: Zion is told to wake, put on fine clothes, and shake off the dust. The LORD says she was sold for nothing and will be bought back without money. His people were taken away, and his name is mocked all day. So they will know his name. A messenger runs on the mountains with good news: “Your God reigns!” The watchmen sing as the LORD returns to Zion. The people leave without rushing, with the LORD ahead and behind. The LORD says his marred servant will be lifted very high.

verse.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”

isaiah-52.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-53.summary: A group speaks and asks who has believed their message. The servant grew like a root in dry ground, with no beauty to draw them. People despised him, and the speakers did not respect him. They thought God was striking him. But he carried their sickness and was pierced for their wrongs. Like a silent lamb, he did not open his mouth. He was cut off and buried with the wicked, though he had done no violence. After his suffering he will see light, and he will make many righteous.

verse.text: Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted.

isaiah-53.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-54.summary: A woman with no children is told to sing. She will have many children, so she must make her tent bigger. She will forget the shame of her youth. Her Maker is her husband and her Redeemer. He left her for a short moment and gathers her with great mercy. As he swore about Noah’s flood, he swears not to be angry with her. He will rebuild her with jewels, and the LORD will teach her children. No weapon made against her will succeed.

verse.text: For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed, but my loving kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed,” says the LORD who has mercy on you.

isaiah-54.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-55.summary: The LORD calls everyone who is thirsty to come to the water. Those with no money may buy wine and milk without price. He asks why they spend money on what is not bread. If they listen, they will live, and he will make a lasting covenant with them. They should seek the LORD while he is near and return for pardon. His thoughts are higher than theirs, as the sky is above the earth. His word is like rain: it does what he sends it to do. They will go out with joy, and the trees will clap.

verse.text: “Hey! Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.

isaiah-55.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-56.summary: The LORD says to keep justice, because his salvation is near. The one who keeps the Sabbath and does no evil is blessed. A foreigner should not say the LORD will shut him out. A eunuch, a man who cannot father children, should not call himself a dry tree. The LORD will give faithful eunuchs a name better than sons and daughters. He will bring foreigners who hold to his covenant to his holy mountain. His house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples. But Israel’s watchmen are blind, like dogs that cannot bark.

verse.text: I will bring these to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.”

isaiah-56.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-57.summary: Good people die, and no one thinks about it. They enter peace. Then the LORD charges others with worship under trees and killing children in the valleys. They set their bed on a high mountain and sent envoys far away. Their collected idols cannot save them, and a breath will carry them off. A voice says to clear the road for God’s people. The high and holy One says he also lives with the humble. He will not be angry forever and will heal, but the wicked have no peace.

verse.text: For the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy, says: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.

isaiah-57.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-58.summary: The LORD tells the speaker to shout Israel’s sins like a trumpet. The people seek him daily and ask why he ignores their fasts. He answers that on fast days they push their workers and fight. Bowing the head like a reed is not the fast he chose. His fast is to free the oppressed and break every yoke. It is to feed the hungry, house the poor, and clothe the naked. Then their light will break out, and he will answer, “Here I am.” If they honor the Sabbath, they will delight in the LORD.

verse.text: Isn’t it to distribute your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor who are cast out to your house? When you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you not hide yourself from your own flesh?

isaiah-58.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-59.summary: The LORD’s hand is not too short to save, and his ear can hear. The people’s sins have come between them and God. Their hands shed blood, their lips lie, and no one goes to court honestly. Then the people speak: they look for light and walk in darkness. They admit that truth has fallen in the street. The LORD sees that there is no justice and no one to step in. So his own arm saves, and he puts on righteousness like armor. A Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from wrong.

verse.text: He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor. Therefore his own arm brought salvation to him; and his righteousness sustained him.

isaiah-59.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-60.summary: Zion is told to rise and shine, because her light has come. Darkness covers the earth, but the LORD’s glory rises on her. Nations and kings come to her light. Her sons and daughters come home from far away. Camels bring gold and frankincense, and ships bring her children. Foreigners rebuild her walls, and her gates stay open day and night. Peace and righteousness will rule her, and violence will end. The LORD will be her lasting light in place of sun and moon.

verse.text: Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.

isaiah-60.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-61.summary: A speaker says the Lord GOD’s Spirit is on him. The LORD has anointed him to bring good news to the humble. He is sent to heal broken hearts and announce freedom to captives. He proclaims the year of the LORD’s favor and comforts those who mourn. They get a garland in place of ashes and will rebuild old ruins. They will be called the LORD’s priests. The LORD says he loves justice and will make a lasting covenant with them. The speaker rejoices, clothed in salvation like a bride or groom.

verse.text: The Lord GOD’s Spirit is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and release to those who are bound,

isaiah-61.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-62.summary: The speaker will not keep quiet until Zion’s righteousness shines like dawn. Nations and kings will see it, and the LORD will give her a new name. She will no longer be called Forsaken, or her land Desolate. Her new names are Hephzibah and Beulah, because the LORD delights in her. God will rejoice over her as a groom over a bride. Watchmen on the walls must give the LORD no rest. He swears that enemies will no longer eat her grain. The people will be called the Holy People, the LORD’s Redeemed.

verse.text: You will not be called Forsaken any more, nor will your land be called Desolate any more; but you will be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.

isaiah-62.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-63.summary: A watcher asks who comes from Edom in red clothes. The one coming says he trod the wine press alone, in anger, with no helper. Then a speaker recalls the LORD’s loving kindness to Israel. He became their Savior and carried them in the old days. But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit, and he fought against them. The people remember Moses and the sea. They ask God to look down, calling him “our Father.” They ask why enemies have trampled his holy place.

verse.text: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and in his pity he redeemed them. He bore them, and carried them all the days of old.

isaiah-63.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-64.summary: The prayer goes on. The people ask God to tear the heavens and come down, as he once did. No eye has seen a God like him, who works for those who wait. They confess long sin and ask, “Shall we be saved?” All their right acts are like a dirty cloth, and they fade like leaves. No one calls on his name. Still they call him Father and potter, and themselves clay. Zion is a wilderness, the temple is burned, and they ask for an answer.

verse.text: But now, LORD, you are our Father. We are the clay and you our potter. We all are the work of your hand.

isaiah-64.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-65.summary: The LORD says he let himself be found by people who did not seek him. All day he held out his hands to a rebellious people. They offer sacrifices in gardens, sit among graves, and eat pig’s meat. He will repay them, yet he spares some, like a good grape cluster. His servants will eat and sing, and those who left him will go hungry. Then he says he creates new heavens and a new earth. People will build houses and live in them, and plant vineyards and eat. Wolf and lamb will feed together.

verse.text: “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be remembered, nor come into mind.

isaiah-65.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

isaiah-66.summary: The LORD says heaven is his throne and earth his footstool. He asks what house people could build for him. He looks to the one who is poor, sorry, and trembles at his word. He rejects offerings from those who choose their own ways. Zion gives birth to a nation in one day, before her pain comes. The LORD will comfort Jerusalem as a mother comforts her child. He comes with fire to judge, and gathers all nations to see his glory. All flesh will worship him, and the rebels’ bodies lie outside.

verse.text: For my hand has made all these things, and so all these things came to be,” says the LORD: “but I will look to this man, even to he who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at my word.

isaiah-66.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 758–697 BC.

jeremiah-1.summary: Jeremiah is a priest’s son from the village of Anathoth. The LORD’s word comes to him in the days of King Josiah. God says he knew Jeremiah before he was formed in the womb. He has appointed him a prophet to the nations. Jeremiah answers that he is only a youth and cannot speak. The LORD touches his mouth and puts words in it. Jeremiah sees an almond branch and a boiling pot tilted from the north. God promises to make him like a fortified city against the whole land.

verse.text: Behold, I have today set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant.”

jeremiah-2.summary: The LORD remembers Israel’s early devotion, like a bride who followed him in the desert. He asks what fault their fathers found in him. Priests, rulers, and prophets all turned away. No other nation has traded its gods, yet Israel traded its glory. The people left the spring of living water. They dug cracked tanks that hold no water. They run to Egypt and Assyria for help. They say to a tree, “You are my father.”

verse.text: “For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living waters, and cut out cisterns for themselves: broken cisterns that can’t hold water.

jeremiah-3.summary: The LORD compares Judah to an unfaithful wife who still expects to return. In Josiah’s days he points to the northern kingdom. Israel was unfaithful and was sent away. Her sister Judah saw it and was not afraid. Judah returned to God only in pretense. So God calls Israel less guilty than Judah. He invites the north to return and only admit its guilt. He promises shepherds after his own heart and healing for the faithless.

verse.text: The LORD said to me, “Backsliding Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.

jeremiah-4.summary: The LORD says Israel may return if she puts away her idols. Judah must break up its unplowed ground. A trumpet warns of disaster from the north. A lion has left its thicket to ruin the land. Jeremiah cries out in anguish at the sound of war. He sees the earth empty and the heavens without light. Mountains shake, people are gone, and the birds have fled. Yet the LORD says he will not make a full end.

verse.text: I saw the earth and, behold, it was waste and void, and the heavens, and they had no light.

jeremiah-5.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to search Jerusalem for one person who does justice. If he finds one, God will pardon the city. Jeremiah thinks the poor simply do not know God’s way. He goes to the great men, and they too have broken free. A distant nation will come and devour their harvest. The people have eyes and do not see. Rich men grow fat and do not defend the orphan. Prophets lie, priests rule by their own authority, and the people love it.

verse.text: I will go to the great men and will speak to them, for they know the way of the LORD, and the law of their God.” But these with one accord have broken the yoke, and burst the bonds.

jeremiah-6.summary: Jeremiah warns the people of Benjamin to flee Jerusalem. An army from the north prepares to attack. No one listens, for their ears are closed. Everyone is greedy, from the least to the greatest. Prophets and priests say “Peace, peace” when there is no peace. They do not know how to blush. God tells them to ask for the old paths and find rest. They answer that they will not walk in them.

verse.text: They have healed also the hurt of my people superficially, saying, ‘Peace, peace!’ when there is no peace.

jeremiah-7.summary: Jeremiah stands at the temple gate and speaks to those who enter. He tells them to change their ways. They must not trust the words “The LORD’s temple.” They must do justice and stop oppressing foreigners, orphans, and widows. They steal, murder, and worship Baal, then come and say they are safe. God asks whether his house has become a den of robbers. He tells them to remember what he did to Shiloh. They even burn their children in the valley of Hinnom.

verse.text: Don’t trust in lying words, saying, ‘The LORD’s temple, the LORD’s temple, the LORD’s temple, are these.’

jeremiah-8.summary: The bones of Judah’s kings and priests will be spread under the sky. The LORD asks why the people never turn back. Even the stork knows its seasons. The people say they are wise and have the LORD’s law. Yet the scribes’ pen has turned it into a lie. Leaders say “Peace” when there is no peace. Jeremiah’s heart is sick for his people. He asks whether there is no balm in Gilead.

verse.text: “ ‘How do you say, “We are wise, and the LORD’s law is with us”? But, behold, the false pen of the scribes has made that a lie.

jeremiah-9.summary: Jeremiah wishes his head were a spring of tears for his people. Neighbors deceive one another, and tongues are bent like bows. No one can trust a brother. The LORD will refine and test them. Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins. He calls for the mourning women, since death has climbed through the windows. The wise, the strong, and the rich must not boast. Let a person boast only in knowing the LORD.

verse.text: But let him who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I am the LORD who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness on the earth, for I delight in these things,” says the LORD.

jeremiah-10.summary: The LORD tells Israel not to learn the ways of the nations. A craftsman cuts a tree and decorates it with silver and gold. He fastens it with nails so that it will not fall. Such idols cannot speak or walk. No one is like the LORD, the living God. He made the earth by his power. Jeremiah mourns that his tent is destroyed. He admits that a person cannot direct his own steps.

verse.text: They are like a palm tree, of turned work, and don’t speak. They must be carried, because they can’t move. Don’t be afraid of them; for they can’t do evil, neither is it in them to do good.”

jeremiah-11.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to proclaim the terms of the covenant. The fathers were told to obey when they left Egypt. They did not, and their children have returned to those sins. God tells Jeremiah not to pray for them. Then the LORD shows Jeremiah a plot against his life. He had been like a gentle lamb led to slaughter. The men of Anathoth tell him to stop prophesying or die. God says he will punish them.

verse.text: “Therefore the LORD says concerning the men of Anathoth, who seek your life, saying, ‘You shall not prophesy in the LORD’s name, that you not die by our hand’—

jeremiah-13.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to buy a linen belt and wear it. Then he must hide it in a rock by the river. After many days he digs it up, and it is ruined. God says he will ruin Judah’s pride in the same way. As a belt clings to the waist, he made Israel cling to him. They would not listen. Jeremiah warns the king and the queen mother that their crowns will fall. He asks whether a leopard can change its spots.

verse.text: For as the belt clings to the waist of a man, so I have caused the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah to cling to me,’ says the LORD; ‘that they may be to me for a people, for a name, for praise, and for glory; but they would not hear.’

jeremiah-14.summary: A drought strikes Judah. Nobles send servants for water, and the cisterns are empty. The ground is cracked, and even the deer abandons her fawn. The people admit their sins and ask God to act for his name’s sake. God tells Jeremiah not to pray for them. Jeremiah says the prophets are promising peace. The LORD answers that he did not send those prophets. They and those who believe them will fall by sword and famine.

verse.text: Then I said, “Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, the prophets tell them, ‘You will not see the sword, neither will you have famine; but I will give you assured peace in this place.’ ”

jeremiah-15.summary: The LORD says he would not relent even if Moses and Samuel pleaded. The people are assigned to death, sword, famine, and exile. Jeremiah laments that his mother bore him. Everyone curses him, though he has wronged no one. He found God’s words and ate them with joy. He sat alone because God’s hand was on him. He asks why his pain never ends. God tells him to return and promises to make him a bronze wall.

verse.text: Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuses to be healed? Will you indeed be to me as a deceitful brook, like waters that fail?
