jeremiah-17.summary: Judah’s sin is engraved on its heart with an iron pen. A person who trusts in human strength is like a shrub in the desert. A person who trusts the LORD is like a tree planted by water. The heart is more deceitful than anything, and the LORD searches it. Jeremiah asks God to heal him and to shame his persecutors. The LORD sends him to the city gates. The people must carry no loads on the Sabbath. If they obey, kings will keep entering those gates.

verse.text: For he will be as a tree planted by the waters, who spreads out its roots by the river, and will not fear when heat comes, but its leaf will be green, and will not be concerned in the year of drought. It won’t cease from yielding fruit.

jeremiah-18.summary: The LORD sends Jeremiah to a potter’s house. The clay pot is spoiled on the wheel, and the potter reshapes it. God says Israel is like clay in his hand. If he warns a nation and it turns from evil, he will relent. If he promises good and a nation does evil, he will withhold it. He calls Judah to turn back. The people answer that it is hopeless and they will follow their own plans. Then they plot against Jeremiah.

verse.text: if that nation, concerning which I have spoken, turns from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do to them.

jeremiah-19.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to buy a clay jar. He must take elders and senior priests to the valley of Hinnom. There he says the people have filled the place with innocent blood. They have burned their sons as offerings to Baal. The valley will be called the Valley of Slaughter. Jeremiah breaks the jar in front of them. God will break the city like a jar that cannot be mended. Jeremiah repeats the message in the temple court.

verse.text: and shall tell them, ‘The LORD of Armies says: “Even so I will break this people and this city as one breaks a potter’s vessel, that can’t be made whole again. They will bury in Topheth until there is no place to bury.

jeremiah-20.summary: Pashhur, a chief officer of the temple, hears Jeremiah’s words. He has Jeremiah beaten and locked in the stocks. The next day Jeremiah gives him a new name: Terror on Every Side. Then Jeremiah complains to the LORD. He says God overpowered him, and he has become a joke. If he tries to keep silent, the word burns like fire in his bones. He praises the LORD as a mighty warrior. Then he curses the day he was born.

verse.text: If I say that I will not make mention of him, or speak any more in his name, then there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones. I am weary with holding it in. I can’t.

jeremiah-21.summary: King Zedekiah sends two officials to Jeremiah. Babylon’s king is attacking, and they hope the LORD will work a wonder. Jeremiah answers that God himself will fight against the city. Its people will die of sword, famine, and disease. The king will be handed to Babylon. The people may choose life by surrendering. The royal house is told to give justice every morning. It must rescue the robbed from the oppressor.

verse.text: House of David, the LORD says, ‘Execute justice in the morning, and deliver him who is robbed out of the hand of the oppressor, lest my wrath go out like fire, and burn so that no one can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.

jeremiah-22.summary: The LORD sends Jeremiah to the king’s house. The king must do justice and protect the foreigner, orphan, and widow. If not, the palace will become a ruin. One king has been carried off and will never return. Jehoiakim builds a grand house with unpaid labor. His father Josiah did justice and defended the poor. Jehoiakim will have a donkey’s burial. The young king Coniah will be thrown out like a broken pot.

verse.text: “Woe to him who builds his house by unrighteousness, and his rooms by injustice; who uses his neighbor’s service without wages, and doesn’t give him his hire;

jeremiah-23.summary: The LORD condemns the shepherds who scatter his flock. He will gather the remnant and raise a righteous Branch for David. That king will be called “The LORD our righteousness.” Jeremiah’s heart is broken because of the prophets. They commit adultery, live in lies, and encourage evildoers. They speak visions from their own minds. They tell those who despise God that all will be well. God says his word is like fire and like a hammer.

verse.text: But if they had stood in my council, then they would have caused my people to hear my words, and would have turned them from their evil way, and from the evil of their doings.

jeremiah-24.summary: Babylon has carried off King Jeconiah, the officials, and the craftsmen. The LORD shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs before the temple. One holds very good figs, and the other holds figs too bad to eat. The good figs are the exiles in Babylon. God will watch over them and bring them back. He will give them a heart to know him. The bad figs are King Zedekiah and those left in the land. They will become a horror to all kingdoms.

verse.text: For I will set my eyes on them for good, and I will bring them again to this land. I will build them, and not pull them down. I will plant them, and not pluck them up.

jeremiah-25.summary: In Jehoiakim’s fourth year Jeremiah speaks to all Judah. For twenty-three years he has warned them, and they have not listened. So the LORD will bring Nebuchadnezzar, his servant, against the land. The nations will serve Babylon’s king for seventy years. Then God will punish Babylon for its own guilt. Jeremiah takes a cup of wrath to the nations. Jerusalem drinks first, and Babylon’s king drinks last. The LORD will roar from on high against all the earth.

verse.text: “It will happen, when seventy years are accomplished, that I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation,” says the LORD, “for their iniquity. I will make the land of the Chaldeans desolate forever.

jeremiah-26.summary: Early in Jehoiakim’s reign Jeremiah speaks in the temple court. He says the house will become like Shiloh unless the people change. Priests and prophets seize him and demand his death. Officials come and hold a hearing at the gate. Jeremiah says the LORD sent him and that he is in their hands. Some elders recall the prophet Micah. King Hezekiah did not kill Micah for a similar message. Another prophet, Uriah, was killed, but an official protects Jeremiah.

verse.text: Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Didn’t he fear the LORD, and entreat the favor of the LORD, and the LORD relented of the disaster which he had pronounced against them? We would commit great evil against our own souls that way!”

jeremiah-27.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to make a yoke and wear it on his neck. He sends word to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Their envoys are visiting King Zedekiah in Jerusalem. God made the earth and gives it to whom he chooses. He has given these lands to Nebuchadnezzar for a time. Any nation that will not serve Babylon will be destroyed. Jeremiah tells Zedekiah to accept the yoke and live. He warns the priests that the temple vessels will not soon return.

verse.text: I spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying, “Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.

jeremiah-28.summary: In the same year the prophet Hananiah speaks in the temple. He says the LORD has broken Babylon’s yoke. Within two years the vessels and the exiled king will return. Jeremiah answers that he wishes it were so. Yet he says a prophet of peace is proved only when his word comes true. Hananiah takes the yoke from Jeremiah’s neck and breaks it. Jeremiah goes away. Later he tells Hananiah that he will die that year, and he does.

verse.text: As for the prophet who prophesies of peace, when the word of the prophet happens, then the prophet will be known, that the LORD has truly sent him.”

jeremiah-29.summary: Jeremiah sends a letter from Jerusalem to the exiles in Babylon. The LORD tells them to build houses and plant gardens. They should marry and have children. They should seek the peace of the city and pray for it. Prophets who promise a quick return are lying. After seventy years God will bring them back. He has plans for their peace and a future with hope. Jeremiah also answers a man who wrote from Babylon against him.

verse.text: Seek the peace of the city where I have caused you to be carried away captive, and pray to the LORD for it; for in its peace you will have peace.”

routes.title: A letter to people in exile

jeremiah-30.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to write his words in a book. Days are coming when he will restore Israel and Judah. There is a cry of terror, and it is a time of trouble for Jacob. Yet Jacob will be saved out of it. God will break the yoke from their necks. Their wound seems beyond cure, and their allies have forgotten them. God will restore their health and heal their wounds. The city will be rebuilt, and songs of thanks will rise from it.

verse.text: For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds,” says the LORD, “because they have called you an outcast, saying, ‘It is Zion, whom no man seeks after.’ ”

jeremiah-31.summary: The LORD says he has loved Israel with an everlasting love. He will rebuild her, and she will dance again. He will gather the scattered from the north, with the blind and the lame. Rachel weeps for her children, and God tells her there is hope. He will watch over his people to build and to plant. He will make a new covenant with Israel and Judah. He will write his law on their hearts. He will forgive their wrongs and remember their sin no more.

verse.text: “But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days,” says the LORD: “I will put my law in their inward parts, and I will write it in their heart. I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

jeremiah-32.summary: Jerusalem is under siege, and Jeremiah is held in the court of the guard. His cousin comes and asks him to buy a field in Anathoth. Jeremiah weighs out seventeen shekels of silver. He signs and seals the deed before witnesses. He gives the deeds to Baruch to store in a clay jar. The LORD says houses and fields will again be bought in this land. Jeremiah prays and asks why he should buy land the enemy holds. God answers that nothing is too hard for him.

verse.text: the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Take these deeds, this deed of the purchase which is sealed, and this deed which is open, and put them in an earthen vessel, that they may last many days.’

jeremiah-33.summary: The LORD speaks to Jeremiah a second time in the court of the guard. Houses have been torn down for defense and filled with the dead. God will bring health and healing to the city. He will cleanse and forgive the people. The sounds of joy will be heard again in the empty streets. Shepherds will again count their flocks. God will raise a righteous Branch for David. His covenant with David is as sure as day and night.

verse.text: the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who say, ‘Give thanks to the LORD of Armies, for the LORD is good, for his loving kindness endures forever;’ who bring thanksgiving into the LORD’s house. For I will cause the captivity of the land to be reversed as at the first,” says the LORD.

jeremiah-34.summary: Babylon’s army is attacking Jerusalem and the last towns of Judah. Jeremiah tells King Zedekiah the city will fall. Zedekiah and the people make a covenant to free their Hebrew slaves. They release them and then force them back. The LORD recalls his law that slaves go free in the seventh year. The people did right for a moment and then profaned his name. So God proclaims a “liberty” for them to sword, disease, and famine. The Babylonian army will return and burn the city.

verse.text: but you turned and profaned my name, and every man caused his servant and every man his handmaid, whom you had let go free at their pleasure, to return. You brought them into subjection, to be to you for servants and for handmaids.’ ”

jeremiah-35.summary: In Jehoiakim’s days the LORD sends Jeremiah to the Rechabite family. Jeremiah brings them into a temple room and offers them wine. They refuse, since their ancestor Jonadab forbade it. He also told them to live in tents and plant no vineyards. They have obeyed in everything. The LORD asks Judah why it will not learn from this. A family obeys a dead ancestor, and Judah ignores its God. He promises that Jonadab’s family will always have someone to serve him.

verse.text: “The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab that he commanded his sons, not to drink wine, are performed; and to this day they drink none, for they obey their father’s commandment; but I have spoken to you, rising up early and speaking, and you have not listened to me.

jeremiah-36.summary: In Jehoiakim’s fourth year the LORD tells Jeremiah to write his words on a scroll. Baruch writes as Jeremiah speaks. Baruch reads the scroll in the temple on a fast day. Officials hear it, are afraid, and tell Baruch and Jeremiah to hide. The scroll is read to the king beside a winter fire. He cuts off each part as it is read and burns it. He orders their arrest, but the LORD hides them. Jeremiah dictates the scroll again, with many words added.

verse.text: When Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was in the brazier, until all the scroll was consumed in the fire that was in the brazier.

jeremiah-37.summary: Zedekiah is king, and no one listens to Jeremiah. The king asks him to pray for the city. Egypt’s army marches out, and the Babylonians withdraw from Jerusalem. Jeremiah says they will return and burn the city. He tries to leave for his family land in Benjamin. A guard arrests him as a deserter. He is beaten and kept in a dungeon for many days. The king questions him in secret and moves him to the court of the guard.

verse.text: “The LORD says, ‘Don’t deceive yourselves, saying, “The Chaldeans will surely depart from us;” for they will not depart.

jeremiah-38.summary: Officials hear Jeremiah say that those who surrender will live. They tell the king he is weakening the soldiers. The king says he cannot stop them. They lower Jeremiah into a cistern, and he sinks in the mud. Ebedmelech, an Ethiopian servant of the palace, tells the king. With thirty men he pulls Jeremiah out with ropes padded by old rags. The king meets Jeremiah in secret and is urged to surrender. He is too afraid to do it.

verse.text: So Ebedmelech took the men with him, and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took from there rags and worn-out garments, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah.

jeremiah-39.summary: After a siege of a year and a half the wall of Jerusalem is breached. Babylon’s officers sit in the Middle Gate. Zedekiah flees at night and is caught near Jericho. His sons are killed in front of him, and he is blinded. The city is burned, and its walls are broken down. Most of the people are taken to Babylon. The poorest are left behind and given vineyards and fields. Jeremiah is released, and Ebedmelech receives a promise of life.

verse.text: But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, who had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.

routes.title: Jerusalem falls and Jeremiah is spared

jeremiah-40.summary: The captain of the guard frees Jeremiah and lets him choose where to live. Jeremiah goes to Gedaliah, the governor Babylon appointed at Mizpah. Judah’s scattered army officers come to Gedaliah. He tells them to serve Babylon and it will go well. They should gather wine, summer fruit, and oil. Jews return from Moab, Ammon, and Edom and bring in a large harvest. An officer warns Gedaliah that a man named Ishmael plans to kill him. Gedaliah does not believe it.

verse.text: As for me, behold, I will dwell at Mizpah, to stand before the Chaldeans who will come to us; but you, gather wine and summer fruits and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken.”

jeremiah-41.summary: Ishmael, a man of the royal family, comes to Mizpah with ten men. They eat with Gedaliah and then kill him and those with him. The next day Ishmael murders seventy pilgrims on their way to the temple. He throws the bodies into a cistern. He takes the people of Mizpah captive and heads for Ammon. Johanan and the other officers catch him at Gibeon. The captives are freed, and Ishmael escapes. The survivors camp near Bethlehem, ready to go to Egypt.

verse.text: because of the Chaldeans; for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon made governor over the land.

routes.title: Ishmael carries off the people of Mizpah
The rescued group camps near Bethlehem

jeremiah-42.summary: The officers and all the people come to Jeremiah. They ask him to pray that the LORD will show them the way. They promise to obey, whether the answer is pleasant or not. After ten days the word comes. If they stay in the land, God will build them up and plant them. They need not fear the king of Babylon. If they go to Egypt, the sword and famine will follow them there. Jeremiah says they deceived themselves when they asked.

verse.text: Whether it is good, or whether it is bad, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send you; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God.”

jeremiah-43.summary: The officers tell Jeremiah he is lying. They say Baruch has turned him against them. They lead all the people into Egypt, with Jeremiah and Baruch. They settle at Tahpanhes. There the LORD tells Jeremiah to bury large stones at the entrance to Pharaoh’s house. Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne over those stones. He will strike Egypt and burn the houses of its gods.

verse.text: but Baruch the son of Neriah has turned you against us, to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, that they may put us to death or carry us away captive to Babylon.”

jeremiah-44.summary: The LORD’s word comes to the Jews living across Egypt. They have seen Jerusalem ruined because of offerings to other gods. Jeremiah asks why they repeat that sin in Egypt. The men and women answer that they will not listen. They will keep burning incense to the queen of the sky. When they did so in Judah, they had food and safety. Since they stopped, they have lacked everything. Jeremiah answers that the LORD remembered those offerings, and events will show whose word stands.

verse.text: But we will certainly perform every word that has gone out of our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of the sky and to pour out drink offerings to her, as we have done, we and our fathers, our kings and our princes, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; for then we had plenty of food, and were well, and saw no evil.

jeremiah-46.summary: This is the first of Jeremiah’s messages about foreign nations. Egypt’s army is defeated at Carchemish by the king of Babylon. Its soldiers are terrified and fall back. Egypt rose like the Nile and said it would cover the earth. No medicine will heal it. A second message says Nebuchadnezzar will invade Egypt itself. Pharaoh is called a loud noise who missed his moment. Afterward Egypt will be lived in again, and Jacob need not fear.

verse.text: Egypt rises up like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge. He says, ‘I will rise up. I will cover the earth. I will destroy cities and its inhabitants.’

jeremiah-47.summary: This message concerns the Philistines. Waters rise from the north and become an overflowing flood. People cry out at the sound of horses and chariots. Fathers are too weak to turn back for their children. Tyre and Sidon lose their last helpers. Gaza and Ashkelon are silenced. A voice asks how long the LORD’s sword will keep striking. The answer is that the LORD has given it an order.

verse.text: “ ‘You sword of the LORD, how long will it be before you are quiet? Put yourself back into your scabbard; rest, and be still.’

jeremiah-48.summary: This long message concerns Moab. Its towns are named one by one as they fall. Its god Chemosh goes into exile with his priests. Moab has been at ease since its youth, like wine left undisturbed. It mocked Israel and was very proud. The speaker wails for Moab and weeps for its vineyards. Joy and gladness are gone from its fields. Yet the LORD will restore Moab’s fortunes in the last days.

verse.text: Therefore I will wail for Moab. Yes, I will cry out for all Moab. They will mourn for the men of Kir Heres.

jeremiah-49.summary: This chapter gathers messages about five peoples. Ammon trusted in its treasures and will see its capital ruined. Edom trusted in its wisdom and its high cliffs. Damascus grows weak, and its young men fall in the streets. The desert tribes of Kedar lose their tents and camels. Elam’s bow is broken, and its people are scattered. Ammon and Elam are promised restoration afterward. God says he will keep Edom’s orphans alive.

verse.text: Why do you boast in the valleys, your flowing valley, backsliding daughter? You trusted in her treasures, saying, ‘Who will come to me?’

jeremiah-50.summary: This message announces the fall of Babylon. Its gods are put to shame, and a nation from the north attacks. Israel and Judah come weeping and ask the way to Zion. They have been lost sheep, misled by their shepherds. Their enemies said harming them was no crime, since they had sinned. Assyria devoured Israel, and Babylon gnawed its bones. God will punish Babylon as he punished Assyria. The hammer of the whole earth is broken.

verse.text: All who found them have devoured them. Their adversaries said, ‘We are not guilty, because they have sinned against the LORD, the habitation of righteousness, even the LORD, the hope of their fathers.’

jeremiah-51.summary: The LORD will send a destroying wind against Babylon. Babylon was a golden cup that made the whole earth drunk. Now it falls suddenly, and its wound cannot be healed. The LORD made the earth by his power, and idols are nothing. Zion says Nebuchadnezzar swallowed her like a monster. Babylon’s thick walls will be leveled. Jeremiah writes all this in a scroll and gives it to an officer named Seraiah. Seraiah must read it in Babylon and sink it in the Euphrates.

verse.text: Then you shall say, ‘Thus will Babylon sink, and will not rise again because of the evil that I will bring on her; and they will be weary.’ ” Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.

jeremiah-52.summary: This last chapter retells the fall of Jerusalem. Zedekiah rebels, and Babylon besieges the city until the food is gone. The wall is breached, and the king is caught and blinded. The temple, the palace, and the houses are burned. The bronze pillars and vessels of the temple are carried away. The chief priests and officials are executed. The numbers of the exiles are listed. Years later the king of Babylon frees Jehoiachin and feeds him at his table.

verse.text: In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and released him from prison.

lamentations-1.summary: Jerusalem sits alone, like a widow who was once a princess. She weeps at night, and none of her friends comfort her. Judah has gone into exile, and no one comes to the feasts. Her enemies prosper, and her children are captives. The poem says she sinned and has been afflicted for it. Then the city speaks for herself. She asks those who pass by to look at her sorrow. She admits she rebelled, and she asks God to see what her enemies have done.

verse.text: “Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look, and see if there is any sorrow like my sorrow, which is brought on me, with which the LORD has afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger.

lamentations-1.dateDetail: The laments follow the capture of Jerusalem.

lamentations-2.summary: The poem says the Lord has acted like an enemy against Zion. He has thrown down her walls, her palaces, and his own sanctuary. King and priest are rejected, and the prophets receive no vision. Elders sit silent on the ground. The poet’s eyes fail with weeping, because children faint in the streets. Her prophets saw false visions and did not expose her guilt. The poet tells Zion to cry out to the Lord through the night. She asks God to look at whom he has treated this way.

verse.text: Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches! Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands toward him for the life of your young children, who faint for hunger at the head of every street.

lamentations-2.dateDetail: The laments follow the capture of Jerusalem.

lamentations-3.summary: One man speaks of the suffering he has seen under God’s anger. God has walled him in and shut out his prayer. He has become a joke, and his hope from the LORD is gone. Then he calls something to mind and has hope. The LORD’s mercies never end and are new every morning. It is good to wait quietly, for the Lord does not reject forever. He calls the people to examine their ways and return. Then he weeps again, and he asks God to judge his enemies.

verse.text: This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope.

lamentations-3.dateDetail: The laments follow the capture of Jerusalem.

lamentations-4.summary: The poet mourns that Zion’s gold has grown dim. Her precious children are treated like clay pots. Infants thirst, and no one gives them bread. Those who ate fine food now lie on trash heaps. The city’s punishment is worse than Sodom’s, which fell in a moment. This came through the sins of her prophets and priests, who shed innocent blood. The people watched in vain for a nation that could not save. Their king, the LORD’s anointed, was captured.

verse.text: It is because of the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, that have shed the blood of the just in the middle of her.

lamentations-4.dateDetail: The laments follow the capture of Jerusalem.

lamentations-5.summary: The people ask the LORD to remember what has happened to them. Strangers hold their land and houses. They are orphans, and they must buy their own water and wood. Slaves rule over them, and they risk their lives for bread. Women are abused, princes are hanged, and elders receive no respect. Music has stopped, and Mount Zion lies empty. They say the LORD reigns forever and ask why he forgets them. They ask him to bring them back, unless he has utterly rejected them.

verse.text: Turn us to yourself, LORD, and we will be turned. Renew our days as of old.

lamentations-5.dateDetail: The laments follow the capture of Jerusalem.

ezekiel-4.summary: God tells Ezekiel to draw Jerusalem on a clay brick. He must set up a model siege around it. He lies on his left side for 390 days for Israel’s guilt. Then he lies on his right side for forty days for Judah’s. He eats bread made from mixed grains, weighed out each day. He drinks a measured amount of water. He protests at cooking over human waste, and God allows cow dung. God says he will cut off Jerusalem’s supply of bread.

verse.text: Moreover he said to me, “Son of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight, and with fearfulness. They will drink water by measure, and in dismay;

ezekiel-4.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-5.summary: God tells Ezekiel to shave his head and beard with a sword. He weighs the hair into three parts. He burns one part inside the model city. He strikes one part with the sword and scatters one to the wind. He tucks a few hairs into his robe and burns some of those. God says this is Jerusalem, set among the nations. She rebelled more than the nations around her. A third die of hunger, a third by sword, and a third are scattered.

verse.text: A third part of you will die with the pestilence, and they will be consumed with famine within you. A third part will fall by the sword around you. A third part I will scatter to all the winds, and will draw out a sword after them.

ezekiel-5.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-6.summary: God tells Ezekiel to speak against the mountains of Israel. A sword is coming on the hilltop shrines. Altars will be ruined, and the dead will lie before their idols. Yet God will leave some who escape the sword. Among the nations they will remember him. They will remember how their unfaithful hearts grieved him. They will hate what they did. Then they will know that he is the LORD.

verse.text: Those of you that escape will remember me among the nations where they are carried captive, how I have been broken with their lewd heart, which has departed from me, and with their eyes, which play the prostitute after their idols. Then they will loathe themselves in their own sight for the evils which they have committed in all their abominations.

ezekiel-6.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-7.summary: God says the end has come on the four corners of the land. He will judge the people by their own ways. Violence has grown into a rod of wickedness. Buyers need not rejoice, and sellers need not mourn. The trumpet sounds, and no one goes to battle. The sword is outside, and disease and hunger are inside. People throw their silver into the streets. Prophet, priest, and king have no help to give.

verse.text: They will cast their silver in the streets, and their gold will be as an unclean thing. Their silver and their gold won’t be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD’s wrath. They won’t satisfy their souls or fill their bellies; because it has been the stumbling block of their iniquity.

ezekiel-7.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-8.summary: Ezekiel sits with Judah’s elders in his house in Babylon. A fiery figure lifts him in a vision to Jerusalem’s temple. He sees an idol at the north gate. He digs through a wall and finds seventy elders burning incense to pictures of animals. They say the LORD does not see them. He sees women weeping for the god Tammuz. He sees twenty-five men bowing to the sun with their backs to the temple. God says they have filled the land with violence.

verse.text: Then he said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in his rooms of imagery? For they say, ‘The LORD doesn’t see us. The LORD has forsaken the land.’ ”

routes.title: A vision carries Ezekiel to Jerusalem

ezekiel-8.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-9.summary: God calls six men with weapons and one man in linen with a writing kit. The glory of God moves to the temple’s threshold. The man in linen must mark those who grieve over the city’s wrongs. The others are to strike everyone without the mark. They must begin at the sanctuary. Ezekiel falls on his face and asks whether God will destroy all who remain. God answers that the land is full of blood. The man in linen reports that he has done his task.

verse.text: The LORD said to him, “Go through the middle of the city, through the middle of Jerusalem, and set a mark on the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry over all the abominations that are done within it.”

ezekiel-9.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-10.summary: Ezekiel sees the sapphire throne above the cherubim again. The man in linen takes burning coals from between the wheels. He is to scatter them over the city. The cloud fills the inner court, and the glory rises to the threshold. Ezekiel describes the wheels and the four-faced creatures once more. He knows them as the creatures he saw by the river in Babylon. The glory leaves the threshold and rests above the cherubim. They rise and stop at the east gate.

verse.text: The LORD’s glory went out from over the threshold of the house and stood over the cherubim.

ezekiel-10.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-11.summary: At the east gate Ezekiel sees twenty-five leaders who give wicked advice. They say the city is a pot and they are the meat safe inside. God says he will bring them out and judge them. One of them dies while Ezekiel speaks. The people of Jerusalem say the exiles are far from the LORD. God answers that he has been a sanctuary to the exiles. He will gather them and give them one heart and a new spirit. Then the glory leaves the city and stands on the eastern hill.

verse.text: I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them. I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them a heart of flesh,

ezekiel-11.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-12.summary: God tells Ezekiel to pack bags for exile while the people watch. In the evening he digs through the wall and carries his bag out. He covers his face so that he cannot see the land. He tells the people he is a sign for them. Their prince will leave in the dark and be taken to Babylon without seeing it. Ezekiel must eat his bread trembling. People say that visions never come true or concern the distant future. God says none of his words will be delayed any longer.

verse.text: “Say, ‘I am your sign. As I have done, so will it be done to them. They will go into exile, into captivity.

ezekiel-12.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-13.summary: God speaks against prophets who prophesy from their own minds. They are like foxes among ruins. They have not gone up to repair the gaps in the wall. They say “Peace” when there is no peace. The people build a weak wall, and these prophets cover it with whitewash. Rain, hail, and wind will bring it down. God also speaks against women who sell charms and hunt lives for bread. They discourage the righteous and encourage the wicked.

verse.text: “ ‘Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, “Peace;” and there is no peace. When one builds up a wall, behold, they plaster it with whitewash.

ezekiel-13.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-14.summary: Some of Israel’s elders come and sit before Ezekiel. God says they have set up idols in their hearts. He asks whether such men should receive an answer. He calls the people to turn from their idols. Then he describes a land that sins and is struck by famine. Even Noah, Daniel, and Job could save only themselves there. They could not save a son or a daughter. Yet some survivors will come out, and their conduct will explain the judgment.

verse.text: though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver only their own souls by their righteousness,” says the Lord GOD.

ezekiel-14.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-15.summary: God asks Ezekiel how vine wood is better than any other wood. No one makes anything from it. No one even takes a peg from it to hang a pot. It is thrown on the fire as fuel. Both ends are burned, and the middle is charred. It was useless whole, and it is more useless burned. God says the people of Jerusalem are like that vine wood. He will give them to the fire.

verse.text: Behold, it is cast into the fire for fuel; the fire has devoured both its ends, and the middle of it is burned. Is it profitable for any work?

ezekiel-15.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-16.summary: God tells Ezekiel to show Jerusalem her history. She was an unwanted baby left in a field. God said, “Live,” and later married her and dressed her as a queen. She trusted her beauty and gave herself to other gods and nations. She even sacrificed her children. Her sisters Samaria and Sodom did less wrong than she did. Sodom was proud and well fed and did not help the poor. Yet God will remember his covenant and forgive her.

verse.text: “ ‘ “Behold, this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: pride, fullness of bread, and prosperous ease was in her and in her daughters. She also didn’t strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.

ezekiel-16.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-17.summary: God gives Ezekiel a riddle about two eagles and a vine. A great eagle takes the top of a cedar and plants a seed. The seed becomes a low vine that grows toward him. Then the vine stretches its roots toward a second eagle. God explains that Babylon’s king took Judah’s king away. He made a treaty with a new king, who swore an oath. That king rebelled and sent to Egypt for horses. God will plant a tender shoot himself, and it will become a great cedar.

verse.text: But he rebelled against him in sending his ambassadors into Egypt, that they might give him horses and many people. Will he prosper? Will he who does such things escape? Will he break the covenant, and still escape?

routes.title: Envoys go to Egypt for horses

ezekiel-17.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-18.summary: The people quote a proverb: the fathers ate sour grapes, and the children’s teeth ache. God says they will not use it any more. Every life belongs to him, and the one who sins will die. A righteous man will live. His violent son will die for his own acts. That man’s son, if he does right, will live. A wicked person who turns will live, and his wrongs will not be remembered. God says he takes no pleasure in anyone’s death.

verse.text: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked?” says the Lord GOD, “and not rather that he should return from his way, and live?

ezekiel-18.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-19.summary: Ezekiel sings a funeral song for the princes of Israel. Their mother was a lioness who raised her cubs. One cub became a young lion and was caught and taken to Egypt. Another prowled among the lions and was caged and taken to Babylon. Their mother was also like a vine with strong branches. It was pulled up in anger and planted in the desert. Fire came out from its own branch. No strong branch is left to be a ruler’s scepter.

verse.text: Fire has gone out of its branches. It has devoured its fruit, so that there is in it no strong branch to be a scepter to rule.’ This is a lamentation, and shall be for a lamentation.”

routes.title: The first young lion goes to Egypt
The second young lion goes to Babylon

ezekiel-19.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-20.summary: Elders come to Ezekiel to ask something of the LORD. God refuses to be consulted by them. He tells Ezekiel to recount their fathers’ history. In Egypt, in the desert, and in the land, Israel rebelled. Each time God held back for the sake of his name. The people now think they will be like the nations and serve wood and stone. God says that will never happen. He will rule them, purge the rebels, and bring them to his holy mountain.

verse.text: “ ‘ “That which comes into your mind will not be at all, in that you say, ‘We will be as the nations, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.’

ezekiel-20.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-21.summary: God says his sword is drawn against Jerusalem, and Ezekiel must groan aloud. The sword is sharpened and polished. Ezekiel marks out two roads for the king of Babylon. One leads to the Ammonite capital and one to Jerusalem. The king stops at the fork and uses arrows, idols, and a liver to decide. The lot falls on Jerusalem. Judah’s prince must take off his crown. It will be given to the one who has the right to it.

verse.text: For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination. He shook the arrows back and forth. He consulted the teraphim. He looked in the liver.

routes.title: The sword at the fork in the road

ezekiel-21.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-22.summary: God calls Jerusalem a city of bloodshed. Its princes use their power to kill. People dishonor parents and wrong the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow. They take bribes and interest and have forgotten God. Israel has become like the waste left when metal is melted. Prophets, priests, and officials all devour the people. The common people also rob the poor and the foreigner. God looked for one person to stand in the gap and found none.

verse.text: The people of the land have used oppression and exercised robbery. Yes, they have troubled the poor and needy, and have oppressed the foreigner wrongfully.

ezekiel-22.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-23.summary: God tells a story of two sisters, Samaria and Jerusalem. Both were unfaithful from their youth in Egypt. Samaria desired the Assyrians and was handed over to them. Jerusalem saw this and did worse. She desired the Assyrians and then the Babylonians. God will bring those lovers against her as attackers. She must drink her sister’s cup of ruin. The sisters are charged with idolatry and with sacrificing their children.

verse.text: For they have committed adultery, and blood is in their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols. They have also caused their sons, whom they bore to me, to pass through the fire to them to be devoured.

ezekiel-23.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-24.summary: On the day Babylon’s siege begins, God tells Ezekiel to record the date. He gives a parable of a cooking pot that cannot be cleaned. Then God says he will take away the delight of Ezekiel’s eyes. Ezekiel must not mourn or weep. His wife dies that evening, and he does as he was told. The people ask what this means for them. God says he will take his sanctuary, the delight of their eyes. They will be too stunned to mourn, as Ezekiel was.

verse.text: ‘Speak to the house of Israel, “The Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the pride of your power, the desire of your eyes, and that which your soul pities; and your sons and your daughters whom you have left behind will fall by the sword.

ezekiel-24.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-25.summary: God speaks against four neighbors of Judah. Ammon gloated when the temple was profaned and Judah went into exile. Ammon clapped, stamped, and rejoiced with contempt. Moab said Judah was like every other nation. Edom took revenge on Judah. The Philistines acted with old hatred. God will hand Ammon and Moab to the peoples of the east. He will lay his hand on Edom and the Philistines.

verse.text: For the Lord GOD says: “Because you have clapped your hands, stamped with the feet, and rejoiced with all the contempt of your soul against the land of Israel,

ezekiel-25.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-26.summary: God speaks against the trading city of Tyre. Tyre gloated when Jerusalem fell. It expected to grow rich now that a rival gate was broken. God will bring many nations against it like waves. Nebuchadnezzar will come with horses, chariots, and siege works. Tyre’s wealth and goods will be plundered. Its stones and timber will be thrown into the sea. The rulers of the coast will tremble and sing a lament.

verse.text: They will make a plunder of your riches and make a prey of your merchandise. They will break down your walls and destroy your pleasant houses. They will lay your stones, your timber, and your dust in the middle of the waters.

ezekiel-26.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-27.summary: God tells Ezekiel to sing a lament for Tyre. The city is pictured as a beautiful ship. Its planks, mast, oars, and sail come from many lands. Men of many nations row it and guard it. A long list names its trading partners and their goods. The cargo includes metals, horses, ivory, wheat, wine, and slaves. An east wind breaks the ship in the heart of the sea. Sailors and merchants weep at its fall.

verse.text: Your riches, your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, your pilots, your repairers of ship seams, the dealers in your merchandise, and all your men of war who are in you, with all your company which is among you, will fall into the heart of the seas in the day of your ruin.

ezekiel-27.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-28.summary: God speaks to the ruler of Tyre, who says he is a god. He is a man, though he is wise and has grown rich. Foreigners will kill him, and he will not claim to be a god then. A lament follows for the king of Tyre. He was in Eden, covered with precious stones. He was blameless until wrong was found in him. Trade filled him with violence, and beauty made him proud. A short message then promises Israel a safe home.

verse.text: Your heart was lifted up because of your beauty. You have corrupted your wisdom by reason of your splendor. I have cast you to the ground. I have laid you before kings, that they may see you.

ezekiel-28.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-29.summary: God speaks against Pharaoh, the great monster lying in the Nile. Pharaoh says the river is his and he made it. God will put hooks in his jaws and leave him in the desert. Egypt was a reed staff that broke when Israel leaned on it. The land will be desolate for forty years. Then Egypt will return as a lowly kingdom. A later message says Nebuchadnezzar got no wages from Tyre. God will give him Egypt as his pay.

verse.text: The land of Egypt will be a desolation and a waste. Then they will know that I am the LORD. “ ‘ “Because he has said, ‘The river is mine, and I have made it,’

ezekiel-29.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-30.summary: God says a day of clouds is near for Egypt. The sword will come, and Egypt’s allies will fall with it. Nebuchadnezzar will destroy the land. God will end the idols of Memphis and judge Egypt’s cities by name. At Tahpanhes the day will grow dark. A second message says God has broken Pharaoh’s arm. It has not been bound up to hold a sword. God will strengthen the arms of Babylon’s king.

verse.text: At Tehaphnehes also the day will withdraw itself, when I break the yokes of Egypt there. The pride of her power will cease in her. As for her, a cloud will cover her, and her daughters will go into captivity.

ezekiel-30.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-31.summary: God asks Pharaoh whom he resembles in his greatness. Assyria was a cedar of Lebanon, taller than every tree. Deep waters fed it, and birds nested in its branches. All great nations lived in its shade. Because it grew proud of its height, God gave it to a ruthless nation. Foreigners cut it down, and its branches fell on the hills. It went down to the grave. Pharaoh and his many people will be brought down the same way.

verse.text: “Therefore thus said the Lord GOD: ‘Because he is exalted in stature, and he has set his top among the thick branches, and his heart is lifted up in his height,

ezekiel-31.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-32.summary: Ezekiel sings a lament for Pharaoh. He thought himself a lion, but he is a monster that muddies the rivers. God will catch him in a net and darken the sky over him. Then Ezekiel is told to wail for Egypt’s crowds. They go down to the pit with other fallen nations. Assyria is there, and Elam, Meshech, Tubal, Edom, and the Sidonians. Each once spread terror in the land of the living. Pharaoh will see them and be consoled over his own army.

verse.text: “Son of man, wail for the multitude of Egypt, and cast them down, even her and the daughters of the famous nations, to the lower parts of the earth, with those who go down into the pit.

ezekiel-32.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-33.summary: God again makes Ezekiel a watchman for Israel. The people say their sins weigh on them and they are wasting away. God says he takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked. A wicked person who turns and makes things right will live. A man escapes from Jerusalem and reports that the city has fallen. Those left in the ruins claim the land, and God rejects their claim. The exiles now come to hear Ezekiel. They listen as to a love song and do not act.

verse.text: They come to you as the people come, and they sit before you as my people, and they hear your words, but don’t do them; for with their mouth they show much love, but their heart goes after their gain.

routes.title: A fugitive brings news of the fall

ezekiel-33.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-35.summary: God tells Ezekiel to speak against Mount Seir, the land of Edom. Edom kept an old hatred and gave Israelites to the sword in their disaster. So bloodshed will pursue Edom. Edom said the two nations and their lands would be its own. Yet the LORD was there. God heard every insult Edom spoke against Israel’s mountains. Edom rejoiced when Israel’s land lay empty. Its own land will be made empty.

verse.text: “ ‘ “Because you have said, ‘These two nations and these two countries will be mine, and we will possess it,’ although the LORD was there,

ezekiel-35.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-47.summary: Water flows from under the temple’s threshold toward the east. The guide measures it four times, and it deepens from ankle to a river. Trees grow thick on both banks. The water runs down to the Dead Sea and makes it fresh. Fish swarm there, and fishermen spread their nets. The trees bear fruit every month, and their leaves heal. God then gives the borders of the land. Foreigners who settle there receive an inheritance with the tribes.

verse.text: You shall divide it by lot for an inheritance to you and to the aliens who live among you, who will father children among you. Then they shall be to you as the native-born among the children of Israel. They shall have inheritance with you among the tribes of Israel.

ezekiel-47.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

ezekiel-48.summary: The land is divided among the tribes in strips from north to south. Seven tribes lie north of the holy district. The district holds the sanctuary, the priests, and the Levites. The city lies beside it, and workers from every tribe farm its land. The prince’s land lies on either side. Five tribes lie to the south. The city has twelve gates, each named for a tribe. From that day the city’s name is “The LORD is there.”

verse.text: “It shall be eighteen thousand reeds in circumference; and the name of the city from that day shall be, ‘The LORD is there.’

ezekiel-48.dateDetail: The end year follows the latest date in Ezekiel 29:17.

daniel-1.summary: Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon takes Jerusalem and carries off some temple vessels. He orders young men of noble families trained for his court. Daniel and three friends are chosen and given Babylonian names. They are to eat the king’s food and drink his wine. Daniel resolves not to defile himself and asks to be excused. The official fears for his own head. Daniel proposes ten days on vegetables and water. The four look healthier, and God gives them learning and wisdom.

verse.text: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king’s delicacies, nor with the wine which he drank. Therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.

routes.title: Young nobles are taken to Babylon

daniel-1.dateDetail: Daniel 10:1 dates his last vision to the third year of Cyrus.

daniel-2.summary: The king has a troubling dream and demands that his wise men tell it. They say no one can do this except the gods. He orders all the wise men killed. Daniel asks for time and prays with his friends. God reveals the dream in the night. The king saw a statue of gold, silver, bronze, iron, and clay. A stone cut without hands struck its feet and became a great mountain. Daniel says God will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed.

verse.text: “In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which will never be destroyed, nor will its sovereignty be left to another people; but it will break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it will stand forever.

daniel-2.dateDetail: Daniel 10:1 dates his last vision to the third year of Cyrus.

daniel-3.summary: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a huge gold image on a plain. All officials must bow when the music plays, or be thrown into a furnace. Three Jewish officials refuse. The king rages and asks what god can rescue them. They answer that their God is able to save them. Even if he does not, they will not worship the image. They are thrown in, and the king sees four men walking unharmed. He calls them out and praises their God.

verse.text: But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have set up.”

daniel-3.dateDetail: Daniel 10:1 dates his last vision to the third year of Cyrus.

daniel-4.summary: King Nebuchadnezzar tells this story himself in a letter to all peoples. He dreamed of a great tree that fed and sheltered every creature. A heavenly watcher ordered it cut down, with its stump left in the ground. Daniel explains that the tree is the king. He will live like an animal until he knows that heaven rules. Daniel urges him to do right and show mercy to the poor. A year later the king boasts about Babylon and loses his mind. When he looks up to heaven, his reason returns.

verse.text: Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you, and break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor. Perhaps there may be a lengthening of your tranquility.”

daniel-4.dateDetail: Daniel 10:1 dates his last vision to the third year of Cyrus.

daniel-5.summary: King Belshazzar gives a feast for a thousand nobles. He orders the gold cups from Jerusalem’s temple brought for his guests. They drink and praise gods of gold, silver, wood, and stone. A hand appears and writes on the wall. The king turns pale, and his wise men cannot read it. Daniel is called and refuses the king’s gifts. He reads the words: numbered, weighed, divided. That night Belshazzar is killed.

verse.text: but have lifted up yourself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before you, and you and your lords, your wives, and your concubines, have drunk wine from them. You have praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which don’t see, or hear, or know; and you have not glorified the God in whose hand your breath is, and whose are all your ways.

daniel-5.dateDetail: Daniel 10:1 dates his last vision to the third year of Cyrus.

daniel-6.summary: King Darius appoints officials over the kingdom, and Daniel excels among them. His rivals can find no fault in his work. They persuade the king to ban prayer to anyone but himself for thirty days. Daniel goes home and prays three times a day, as before. The king is distressed and cannot undo his own law. Daniel is thrown to the lions, and the king spends a sleepless night. At dawn Daniel answers that God shut the lions’ mouths. The king orders respect for Daniel’s God.

verse.text: When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before.

daniel-6.dateDetail: Daniel 10:1 dates his last vision to the third year of Cyrus.

daniel-9.summary: Daniel reads in Jeremiah that Jerusalem’s ruin would last seventy years. He turns to God with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes. He confesses that all Israel has sinned and ignored the prophets. God is in the right, and shame belongs to the people. He asks God to turn his anger from Jerusalem. He asks on the ground of mercy and for God’s own name. Gabriel comes while he is still praying. He speaks of seventy weeks set for the people and the holy city.

verse.text: My God, turn your ear and hear. Open your eyes and see our desolations, and the city which is called by your name; for we do not present our petitions before you for our righteousness, but for your great mercies’ sake.

daniel-9.dateDetail: Daniel 10:1 dates his last vision to the third year of Cyrus.

hosea-2.summary: God speaks of Israel as a wife who has gone after other lovers. She thinks they gave her bread, wool, oil, and drink. She does not know that God gave her the grain and the wine. He will block her path and take back his gifts. Then he will lead her into the desert and speak kindly to her. She will call him “my husband.” He will betroth her to himself forever. He will say to “Not My People,” “You are my people.”

verse.text: I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion.

hosea-7.summary: God would heal Israel, but its guilt keeps coming to light. Thieves break in, and bands raid outside. The people do not consider that God remembers. Plotters are like an oven that smolders all night and blazes at dawn. All their kings have fallen, and none calls on God. Ephraim is like a cake baked on one side. Ephraim is like a silly dove, calling to Egypt and flying to Assyria. God will spread his net over them.

verse.text: “Ephraim is like an easily deceived dove, without understanding. They call to Egypt. They go to Assyria.

hosea-8.summary: A trumpet warns that an enemy is coming like an eagle. Israel cries that it knows God, yet it has rejected what is good. The people set up kings without asking God. They made idols of silver and gold. God rejects the calf of Samaria. A workman made it, and it is not God. They sow the wind and will reap the whirlwind. Israel has forgotten its Maker and built palaces.

verse.text: For this is even from Israel! The workman made it, and it is no God; indeed, the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.

hosea-9.summary: Hosea tells Israel not to rejoice at the harvest. The people have been unfaithful on every threshing floor. They will not stay in the LORD’s land. They will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria. They will have no offerings to bring on feast days. The days of reckoning have come. The people call the prophet a fool and the inspired man mad. Their children will be lost, and they will wander among the nations.

verse.text: The days of visitation have come. The days of reckoning have come. Israel will consider the prophet to be a fool, and the man who is inspired to be insane, because of the abundance of your sins, and because your hostility is great.

hosea-10.summary: Israel is a spreading vine that bears much fruit. The more it prospered, the more altars it built. Its heart is divided. The calf of Bethel will be carried to Assyria as a gift. Samaria’s king will vanish like a twig on water. God tells them to sow righteousness and reap kindness. They must break up their unplowed ground and seek the LORD. Instead they have plowed wickedness and trusted in their soldiers.

verse.text: Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap according to kindness. Break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, until he comes and rains righteousness on you.

hosea-11.summary: God says he loved Israel as a child and called his son out of Egypt. The more he called, the more they went away. He taught Ephraim to walk and carried them in his arms. He bent down and fed them. Now they refuse to return, and the sword will come. Then God asks how he can give them up. His heart turns over, and his compassion grows warm. He will roar like a lion, and his children will come trembling home.

verse.text: “How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I make you like Zeboiim? My heart is turned within me, my compassion is aroused.

hosea-12.summary: Ephraim chases the wind and makes treaties with Assyria and Egypt. The LORD has a charge against Judah and Jacob. In the womb Jacob grasped his brother’s heel. As a man he struggled with God, wept, and asked for favor. So the people must turn to their God. They must keep kindness and justice and wait for him. A merchant with false scales loves to cheat. Ephraim says its wealth proves it has done no wrong.

verse.text: Therefore turn to your God. Keep kindness and justice, and wait continually for your God.

hosea-13.summary: Ephraim once spoke and others trembled, but he died through Baal. Now the people make silver idols and kiss calves. They will vanish like morning mist. Yet the LORD has been their God since Egypt. He cared for them in the desert. When they were fed, they grew proud and forgot him. So he will meet them like a lion and a bear. Their kings cannot save them, and Samaria will bear its guilt.

verse.text: “Yet I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt; and you shall acknowledge no god but me, and besides me there is no savior.

joel-2.summary: A trumpet sounds in Zion, for the day of the LORD is near. An army advances like fire, and nothing escapes it. Yet even now God calls the people to return with all their heart. They should tear their hearts and not their clothes. He is gracious, merciful, and slow to anger. Everyone must gather, from elders to nursing infants. Then God will restore the years the locusts ate. Afterward he will pour out his Spirit on all people.

verse.text: Tear your heart and not your garments, and turn to the LORD, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.

joel-2.dateDetail: The Church chronology marks this date with a question mark. It has no revised year.

joel-3.summary: In those days God will gather all nations for judgment. They scattered his people and divided his land. They cast lots for his people. They traded a boy for a prostitute and sold a girl for wine. Tyre, Sidon, and Philistia sold Judah’s children far away. God will return their deeds on their own heads. Crowds gather in the valley of decision. The LORD will shelter his people, and Judah will be lived in forever.

verse.text: and have cast lots for my people, and have given a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine, that they may drink.

joel-3.dateDetail: The Church chronology marks this date with a question mark. It has no revised year.

amos-1.summary: Amos is a herdsman from Tekoa in Judah. He speaks in the days of King Jeroboam of Israel. The LORD roars from Zion, and the pastures wither. Amos announces judgment on the nations around Israel. Damascus threshed Gilead with iron sledges. Gaza and Tyre sold whole communities to Edom. Edom chased his brother with a sword and showed no pity. Ammon ripped open pregnant women to gain more land.

verse.text: The LORD says: “For three transgressions of Tyre, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment; because they delivered up the whole community to Edom, and didn’t remember the brotherly covenant;

amos-2.summary: Amos continues with Moab, which burned the bones of Edom’s king. Then he turns to Judah, which rejected the LORD’s law. Last he turns to Israel itself. The people sell the innocent for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals. They trample the heads of the poor. They lie down beside altars on clothes taken as security for debts. They told the prophets not to speak. God will press them down like a loaded cart.

verse.text: The LORD says: “For three transgressions of Israel, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment, because they have sold the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals;

amos-3.summary: God speaks to the whole family he brought up from Egypt. He chose them alone of all the families of the earth. Therefore he will punish them for their sins. Amos asks a series of questions about cause and effect. A lion does not roar without prey. When the LORD speaks, a prophet must prophesy. Foreign peoples are called to witness the oppression in Samaria. The rich houses of winter and summer will be destroyed.

verse.text: “I have chosen only you of all the families of the earth. Therefore I will punish you for all of your sins.”

amos-4.summary: Amos speaks to the wealthy women of Samaria who crush the poor. They will be led away with hooks. He tells the people, with irony, to go and sin at their shrines. They love to bring offerings and announce them. God sent hunger, drought, blight, plague, and ruin. After each one they did not return to him. So Israel must prepare to meet its God. He forms the mountains and creates the wind.

verse.text: “I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in every town; yet you haven’t returned to me,” says the LORD.

amos-5.summary: Amos sings a funeral song for Israel. God tells the people to seek him and live. They turn justice into bitterness and hate anyone who speaks truth in court. They tax the poor and take bribes. They should hate evil and set up justice at the gate. The day of the LORD will be darkness and not light. God says he hates their feasts and will not hear their songs. He wants justice to roll like a river.

verse.text: But let justice roll on like rivers, and righteousness like a mighty stream.

amos-6.summary: Amos warns those who feel safe in Zion and Samaria. They are the leading men of the first of the nations. They lie on beds of ivory and eat choice lambs. They sing to the harp and drink wine by the bowlful. They do not grieve over the ruin of their people. So they will be the first to go into exile. God hates Jacob’s pride and will give up the city. They have turned justice into poison.

verse.text: who drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the best oils, but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.

amos-8.summary: God shows Amos a basket of ripe summer fruit. The end has come for Israel. Amos speaks to those who trample the needy. They ask when the holy day will be over so they can sell grain. They shrink the measure, raise the price, and use false scales. They buy the poor for silver and sell the sweepings as wheat. God swears he will not forget. A famine is coming, a hunger to hear the LORD’s words.

verse.text: saying, ‘When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell grain? And the Sabbath, that we may market wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel large, and dealing falsely with balances of deceit;

amos-9.summary: Amos sees the Lord standing beside the altar. He orders the temple struck, and no one will escape. Israel is no different to him than distant peoples. He brought the Philistines and Syrians from other lands too. He will sift Israel like grain and not destroy it completely. Then he will raise up David’s fallen shelter. The people will rebuild their ruined cities and live in them. They will never again be uprooted from their land.

verse.text: I will bring my people Israel back from captivity, and they will rebuild the ruined cities, and inhabit them; and they will plant vineyards, and drink wine from them. They shall also make gardens, and eat their fruit.

obadiah-1.summary: Obadiah’s vision concerns Edom, the nation descended from Esau. Edom lives high in the rocks and thinks no one can bring it down. God will bring it down. Its allies will deceive it, and its wise men will perish. Edom did violence to its brother Jacob. It stood aside while strangers looted Jerusalem. It gloated, entered the gates, and seized goods. It cut down those who fled, and what it did will be done to it.

verse.text: Don’t stand in the crossroads to cut off those of his who escape. Don’t deliver up those of his who remain in the day of distress.

obadiah-1.dateDetail: The Church chronology lists Obadiah twice, both with a question mark. This uses the later entry.

jonah-1.summary: The LORD tells Jonah to go and preach against the great city of Nineveh. Jonah boards a ship going the other way. The LORD sends a violent storm. The sailors pray to their gods and throw the cargo overboard. Jonah is asleep below. The lot points to him, and he tells them to throw him in. The men row hard for land and then do as he says. The sea grows calm, and a great fish swallows Jonah.

verse.text: Nevertheless the men rowed hard to get them back to the land; but they could not, for the sea grew more and more stormy against them.

jonah-1.dateDetail: 2 Kings 14:25 places Jonah in the reign of Jeroboam II.
jonah-1.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 826–773 BC.

jonah-3.summary: The LORD’s word comes to Jonah a second time, and he goes. He walks a day into the city. He says that in forty days Nineveh will be overthrown. The people believe God and put on sackcloth. The king leaves his throne and sits in ashes. He orders everyone to fast, pray, and turn from violence. He says God may yet relent. God sees that they have turned, and he does not destroy them.

verse.text: but let them be covered with sackcloth, both man and animal, and let them cry mightily to God. Yes, let them turn everyone from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands.

jonah-3.dateDetail: 2 Kings 14:25 places Jonah in the reign of Jeroboam II.
jonah-3.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 826–773 BC.

jonah-4.summary: Jonah is very angry that Nineveh is spared. He says this is why he fled in the first place. He knew God is gracious, merciful, and slow to anger. He asks to die. He sits outside the city to see what will happen. God gives him a plant for shade and then sends a worm to kill it. Jonah is angry enough to die. God asks whether he should not care for a great city and its animals.

verse.text: Shouldn’t I be concerned for Nineveh, that great city, in which are more than one hundred twenty thousand persons who can’t discern between their right hand and their left hand, and also many animals?”

jonah-4.dateDetail: 2 Kings 14:25 places Jonah in the reign of Jeroboam II.
jonah-4.biblical: Biblical numbers in the same table: 826–773 BC.

micah-1.summary: The LORD’s word comes to Micah of Moresheth about Samaria and Jerusalem. The LORD comes down, and the mountains melt under him. Samaria will become a heap of rubble. Its idols will be smashed. Micah says he will wail and go barefoot and naked. The wound has reached the gate of Jerusalem. He names town after town in Judah’s lowlands. Each one will share in the disaster and the exile.

verse.text: For this I will lament and wail. I will go stripped and naked. I will howl like the jackals and mourn like the ostriches.

micah-1.dateDetail: Micah 1:1 names Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.

micah-3.summary: Micah addresses the rulers of Israel, who should know justice. They hate good and treat the people like meat for the pot. Prophets promise peace to those who feed them. They declare war on those who give them nothing. Micah says he is filled with the LORD’s Spirit to declare Israel’s sin. Leaders judge for bribes, priests teach for pay, and prophets speak for money. They say the LORD is among them. So Zion will be plowed like a field.

verse.text: Her leaders judge for bribes, and her priests teach for a price, and her prophets tell fortunes for money; yet they lean on the LORD, and say, “Isn’t the LORD among us? No disaster will come on us.”

micah-3.dateDetail: Micah 1:1 names Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.

micah-4.summary: In later days the mountain of the LORD’s house will be raised above the hills. Nations will come to learn his ways. He will judge between peoples and settle their disputes. They will beat swords into plows and learn war no more. Everyone will sit under his own vine and fig tree, unafraid. God will gather the lame and those who were driven away. He will rule them on Mount Zion. For now Zion must go to Babylon, and there she will be rescued.

verse.text: But every man will sit under his vine and under his fig tree. No one will make them afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of Armies has spoken.

micah-4.dateDetail: Micah 1:1 names Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.

micah-5.summary: Jerusalem is under siege, and its ruler is struck on the cheek. A new ruler will come from Bethlehem, a small town in Judah. His origins are from ancient times. He will stand and shepherd his flock in the LORD’s strength. His people will live securely. He will be their peace when Assyria invades. The remnant of Jacob will be like dew among the nations. God will remove their horses, forts, and idols.

verse.text: He shall stand, and shall shepherd in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. They will live, for then he will be great to the ends of the earth.

micah-5.dateDetail: Micah 1:1 names Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.

micah-6.summary: The LORD brings a case against his people, with the mountains as witnesses. He asks what he has done to weary them. He brought them from Egypt and sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. A worshiper asks what he should bring to the LORD. He offers calves, thousands of rams, and even his firstborn. The answer is that God has already shown what is good. Do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with God. The city, however, is full of false weights and violence.

verse.text: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does the LORD require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

micah-6.dateDetail: Micah 1:1 names Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.

micah-7.summary: Micah grieves like someone who finds no fruit after the harvest. The faithful have vanished, and officials take bribes. No one can trust a neighbor or even a family member. Yet Micah will watch and wait for the LORD. He admits his sin and expects God to plead his case. He asks God to shepherd his people. He asks who is a God like this, who pardons guilt. God will hurl all their sins into the depths of the sea.

verse.text: Who is a God like you, who pardons iniquity, and passes over the disobedience of the remnant of his heritage? He doesn’t retain his anger forever, because he delights in loving kindness.

micah-7.dateDetail: Micah 1:1 names Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.

nahum-1.summary: This book is a message about Nineveh, the capital of Assyria. The LORD is slow to anger and great in power. He will not leave the guilty unpunished. Mountains quake before him, and no one can stand against his anger. He is good and a refuge in the day of trouble. He will make a full end of those who plot against him. He tells Judah he will break Assyria’s yoke. A messenger on the mountains brings news of peace.

verse.text: Now I will break his yoke from off you, and will burst your bonds apart.”

nahum-1.dateDetail: The Church chronology marks this date with a question mark.

nahum-2.summary: An attacker advances against Nineveh. Shields are red, and chariots flash like torches in the streets. The river gates are opened, and the palace collapses. The city is stripped, and its women moan like doves. People flee, and no one turns back. Plunderers carry off endless silver and gold. Nahum asks where the lions’ den is now. The lion once filled his caves with torn prey.

verse.text: The lion tore in pieces enough for his cubs, and strangled prey for his lionesses, and filled his caves with the kill and his dens with prey.

nahum-2.dateDetail: The Church chronology marks this date with a question mark.

nahum-3.summary: Nahum cries woe to the city of blood, full of lies and plunder. Horsemen charge, and the dead lie in heaps. Nineveh sold nations by her charms and will be put to shame. No one will mourn her. She is no better than Thebes, the great city on the Nile. Thebes went into exile, and its infants were killed. Nineveh’s forts will fall like ripe figs. Her wound cannot be healed, and all who hear of it clap their hands.

verse.text: There is no healing your wound, for your injury is fatal. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you, for who hasn’t felt your endless cruelty?

nahum-3.dateDetail: The Church chronology marks this date with a question mark.

habakkuk-2.summary: Habakkuk stands at his watch post to see what God will say. The LORD tells him to write the vision plainly on tablets. It awaits its time, and he must wait for it. The proud one is not upright, and the righteous will live by faith. The conquered nations will taunt their conqueror with five woes. He piled up what was not his and built his house on plunder. Idols are teachers of lies. The LORD is in his holy temple, and all the earth must be silent.

verse.text: For the stone will cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the woodwork will answer it.

habakkuk-3.summary: Habakkuk prays and asks God to remember mercy in his anger. He recalls God coming from the south in glory. Mountains shook, and the sun and moon stood still. God went out to save his people and crush the wicked. Habakkuk’s body trembles as he waits for the day of trouble. The fig tree may not bud, and the fields may give no food. The flocks and herds may be gone. Yet he will rejoice in the LORD, who is his strength.

verse.text: yet I will rejoice in the LORD. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!

zephaniah-1.summary: The LORD’s word comes to Zephaniah in the days of King Josiah. God will sweep everything from the face of the earth. He will strike Judah and those who worship Baal and the stars. Some swear by the LORD and also by another god. The day of the LORD is near. He will search Jerusalem with lamps. He will punish those who say he does nothing, good or bad. It will be a day of wrath, and silver and gold will not save.

verse.text: It will happen at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish the men who are settled on their dregs, who say in their heart, “The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil.”

zephaniah-2.summary: Zephaniah calls the nation to gather before the day of anger comes. The humble of the land should seek the LORD. They should seek righteousness and humility. Perhaps they will be sheltered on that day. Philistia’s cities will be emptied. Moab and Ammon will become like Sodom for their pride. Ethiopia will fall by the sword. Nineveh, which said no one was like it, will become a home for wild animals.

verse.text: Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land, who have kept his ordinances. Seek righteousness. Seek humility. It may be that you will be hidden in the day of the LORD’s anger.

zephaniah-3.summary: Zephaniah cries woe to the rebellious city that listens to no one. Its officials are roaring lions, and its judges are wolves. Its prophets are reckless, and its priests profane what is holy. The LORD within it does no wrong and gives justice every morning. He will purify the speech of the nations to call on his name. He will leave a humble and lowly people in the city. Zion is told to sing, for the LORD is among them. He will save the lame and gather the outcasts.

verse.text: Behold, at that time I will deal with all those who afflict you; and I will save those who are lame and gather those who were driven away. I will give them praise and honor, whose shame has been in all the earth.
