haggai-1.summary: In the second year of Darius, Haggai speaks to the governor and the high priest. The people say it is not yet time to rebuild the LORD’s house. God asks whether they should live in paneled houses while his house lies ruined. They sow much and harvest little. Their wages go into a bag with holes. God tells them to bring wood and build. The leaders and the people obey. Within a month the work begins.

verse.text: “You looked for much, and, behold, it came to little; and when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why?” says the LORD of Armies, “Because of my house that lies waste, while each of you is busy with his own house.

haggai-2.summary: A month later Haggai speaks again. He asks who remembers the first temple in its glory. The new one looks like nothing beside it. Yet God tells the governor, the priest, and the people to be strong and work. He is with them, and his Spirit remains among them. He will shake the nations and fill this house with glory. From the day the foundation was laid, he will bless them. He tells the governor that he has chosen him.

verse.text: Yet now be strong, Zerubbabel,’ says the LORD. ‘Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land,’ says the LORD, ‘and work, for I am with you,’ says the LORD of Armies.

zechariah-1.summary: In the second year of Darius, Zechariah calls the people to return to the LORD. Their fathers ignored the prophets, and the warnings came true. Then Zechariah sees a vision at night. A man on a red horse stands among myrtle trees with other riders. They have patrolled the earth and found it quiet. The LORD’s angel asks how long Jerusalem must go without mercy. God answers with kind and comforting words. He is angry with the nations that are at ease.

verse.text: Then the LORD’s angel replied, “O LORD of Armies, how long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which you have had indignation these seventy years?”

zechariah-1.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-2.summary: Zechariah sees a man with a measuring line going to measure Jerusalem. An angel sends word to stop him. Jerusalem will be like villages without walls, since so many will live there. The LORD will be a wall of fire around it. He calls the exiles to escape from Babylon. Whoever touches them touches the apple of his eye. He is coming to live among his people. Many nations will join themselves to the LORD and be his people.

verse.text: Many nations shall join themselves to the LORD in that day, and shall be my people; and I will dwell among you, and you shall know that the LORD of Armies has sent me to you.

zechariah-2.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-3.summary: Zechariah sees the high priest Joshua standing before the LORD’s angel. The accuser stands at his right hand. The LORD rebukes the accuser and calls Joshua a stick snatched from the fire. Joshua is wearing filthy clothes. The angel orders them removed and says his guilt is taken away. He is dressed in fine robes and a clean turban. He is told to walk in God’s ways. God promises to bring his servant, the Branch.

verse.text: He answered and spoke to those who stood before him, saying, “Take the filthy garments off him.” To him he said, “Behold, I have caused your iniquity to pass from you, and I will clothe you with rich clothing.”

zechariah-3.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-6.summary: Zechariah sees four chariots come out between two bronze mountains. They go out to patrol the whole earth. Then God tells him to collect silver and gold from exiles newly come from Babylon. He must make a crown and set it on Joshua the high priest. He says a man called the Branch will build the LORD’s temple. That man will rule on his throne and be a priest there. The crown will be kept in the temple as a reminder. People from far away will come and help build.

verse.text: He will build the LORD’s temple. He will bear the glory, and will sit and rule on his throne. He will be a priest on his throne. The counsel of peace will be between them both.

zechariah-6.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-7.summary: Men come from Bethel to ask the priests a question. For years they have fasted in the fifth month. They ask whether they should continue. God asks whether their fasting was really for him. He recalls what the earlier prophets said. Judge fairly, and show kindness and mercy to one another. Do not oppress widows, orphans, foreigners, or the poor. The fathers refused to listen, and so they were scattered.

verse.text: Don’t oppress the widow, the fatherless, the foreigner, nor the poor; and let none of you devise evil against his brother in your heart.’

zechariah-7.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-8.summary: The LORD says he is returning to Zion to live in Jerusalem. Old men and women will sit in its streets with their canes. The streets will be full of boys and girls playing. God will bring his people from east and west. He tells them to be strong and finish the temple. They must speak truth and judge fairly at their gates. The fasts will become glad feasts. Ten foreigners will take hold of one Jew’s robe and ask to go with him.

verse.text: The streets of the city will be full of boys and girls playing in its streets.”

zechariah-8.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-9.summary: A message of judgment falls on Syria, Tyre, and the Philistine cities. God will guard his house against every army. Zion is told to rejoice, for her king is coming. He is righteous and humble and rides on a donkey. He will remove chariots, war horses, and bows from Israel. He will speak peace to the nations and rule from sea to sea. God will free the prisoners because of his covenant. He will save his people like a flock.

verse.text: I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem. The battle bow will be cut off; and he will speak peace to the nations. His dominion will be from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.

zechariah-9.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-10.summary: The people are told to ask the LORD for rain in the spring. Household idols speak nonsense, and fortune-tellers see lies. Their comfort is empty. So the people wander like sheep with no shepherd. God is angry with the shepherds and will care for his flock himself. He will strengthen Judah and save the house of Joseph. He will whistle for them and gather them in. He will bring them home from Egypt and Assyria.

verse.text: For the teraphim have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie; and they have told false dreams. They comfort in vain. Therefore they go their way like sheep. They are oppressed, because there is no shepherd.

zechariah-10.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-11.summary: Zechariah is told to shepherd a flock marked for slaughter. Its buyers kill the sheep and feel no guilt. Its sellers thank God that they are rich. He takes two staffs, named Favor and Union. He grows weary of the flock, and they detest him. He breaks the staff Favor and asks for his wages. They weigh out thirty pieces of silver, and he throws it to the potter. He breaks the second staff, and a worthless shepherd follows.

verse.text: Their buyers slaughter them and go unpunished. Those who sell them say, ‘Blessed be the LORD, for I am rich;’ and their own shepherds don’t pity them.

zechariah-11.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-12.summary: The LORD will make Jerusalem a cup that makes the nations stagger. All who try to lift that heavy stone will hurt themselves. The clans of Judah will be like fire among sheaves. The LORD will save the tents of Judah first. David’s house and Jerusalem will not be honored above the rest. Then God will pour out a spirit of grace and prayer. They will look on one they pierced and mourn. Every family will mourn by itself.

verse.text: The LORD also will save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of David’s house and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem not be magnified above Judah.

zechariah-12.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-13.summary: On that day a fountain will be opened to cleanse sin. God will remove the names of the idols from the land. False prophets will be ashamed and deny their trade. A sword is called against God’s shepherd. The shepherd is struck, and the sheep scatter. Two thirds of the people will perish. The last third will pass through fire and be refined like silver. They will call on God, and he will call them his people.

verse.text: I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will test them like gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will hear them. I will say, ‘It is my people;’ and they will say, ‘The LORD is my God.’ ”

zechariah-13.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

zechariah-14.summary: A day of the LORD is coming when nations will attack Jerusalem. The city will be taken, and half its people exiled. Then the LORD will fight, and his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives. Living water will flow from Jerusalem all year. The LORD will be king over all the earth. Survivors of the nations will come each year to worship him. Even the bells on the horses will be marked as holy. Every cooking pot in Jerusalem will be holy to the LORD.

verse.text: In that day there will be inscribed on the bells of the horses, “HOLY TO THE LORD”; and the pots in the LORD’s house will be like the bowls before the altar.

zechariah-14.dateDetail: Zechariah 7:1 gives his latest dated message, two years later.

malachi-1.summary: The LORD tells Israel that he has loved them, and they ask how. He points to his choice of Jacob over Esau. A son honors his father, yet the priests despise God’s name. They ask how they have done so. They offer blind, lame, and sick animals on his altar. God tells them to try giving such gifts to their governor. He would rather the temple doors were shut. His name will be great among the nations.

verse.text: When you offer the blind for sacrifice, isn’t that evil? And when you offer the lame and sick, isn’t that evil? Present it now to your governor! Will he be pleased with you? Or will he accept your person?” says the LORD of Armies.

malachi-2.summary: God warns the priests that he will curse their blessings. His covenant with Levi was one of life and peace. A priest’s lips should guard knowledge. These priests have caused many to stumble. The people are also faithless to one another. They weep at the altar because God ignores their offerings. The LORD is witness between each man and the wife of his youth. They have wearied him by asking where the God of justice is.

verse.text: Yet you say, ‘Why?’ Because the LORD has been witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have dealt treacherously, though she is your companion and the wife of your covenant.

malachi-3.summary: God says he is sending a messenger to prepare his way. The Lord they seek will come suddenly to his temple. He will be like a refiner’s fire and will purify the Levites. He will come near to judge. He will testify against those who cheat workers and oppress widows, orphans, and foreigners. He calls the people to return and stop robbing him of tithes. Some say it is useless to serve God. Those who fear the LORD are written in a book of remembrance.

verse.text: I will come near to you to judgment. I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, against the adulterers, against the perjurers, and against those who oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless, and who deprive the foreigner of justice, and don’t fear me,” says the LORD of Armies.
